parts.text:
Now let me understand each module's role, size, and dependencies. Let me get line counts of source files per module and read poms fully for a few. Also understand dependencies graph.

Dependency graph (internal pathland artifacts):

- pathland-view-core (base: kotlin-stdlib, jna)
- pathland-view-kotlin -> view-core
- pathland-demo-common -> view-core
- pathland-demo-views-kotlin -> view-core, view-kotlin, demo-common
- pathland-render-html -> view-core (compile), view-kotlin (test)
- pathland-state-redis -> view-core
- pathland-server-core -> view-core, render-html, state-redis (view-kotlin test)
- pathland-observability -> server-core
- pathland-test-kit -> view-core
- pathland-spring-boot-starter -> server-core, observability (+test: view-kotlin, test-kit)
- pathland-quarkus -> server-core, observability (+test: view-kotlin, test-kit)
- pathland-quarkus-deployment -> pathland-quarkus
- pathland-quarkus-kotlin -> pathland-quarkus, view-kotlin
- pathland-quarkus-kotlin-deployment -> pathland-quarkus-kotlin, pathland-quarkus-deployment
- demos: gtk-demo -> demo-views-kotlin, demo-common, jna; qt-demo -> same; quarkus-demo -> pathland-quarkus, demo-views-kotlin, demo-common; quarkus-kotlin-demo -> pathland-quarkus-kotlin, view-kotlin, demo-views-kotlin; spring-boot-demo -> starter, demo-views-kotlin, demo-common.

Wait, pathland-server-core depends on state-redis as compile? That's a notable coupling — server-core pulling in Lettuce. Let me verify scope. Let me read poms fully.

Also note pathland-render-html depends on view-core at compile and view-kotlin test only.

Let me read key poms and source structure. Also identify module sizes.

Interesting: pathland-view-core has both src/main/java and src/main/kotlin? Maybe Java stubs or remnants. Let me look at files.

Also pathland-quarkus-kotlin has zero source files, only resources (runtime module - extension descriptor). That's a candidate to merge with pathland-quarkus? But Quarkus extensions have runtime + deployment modules convention; quarkus-kotlin is runtime that adds kotlin dependency and dependency on view-kotlin. It has no code. Hmm.

Let me read the poms fully for important structural ones, and inspect module content. Also check the maven-release/publishing configuration—these are published separately? The root pom looks like it publishes to central. Combining modules affects published artifacts (breaking API). Let me check root pom publishing, README, status.md.

        thin JNA shim over libpathland_render_html (pathland_html_render /
        _render_fragment / _free). Stateless: each call renders
        a full snapshot frame to HTML in one pass. The server-side/remote-projection
        target, usable from Spring Boot, Quarkus, or any Java server. The single
        renderer is the Rust crate reused by every language.
    </description>

        <dependency>
            <groupId>dev.pathland</groupId>
            <artifactId>pathland-view-kotlin</artifactId>
            <version>${project.version}</version>
            <scope>test</scope>

            <version>${project.version}</version>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>

            <artifactId>jna</artifactId>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.junit.jupiter</groupId>
            <artifactId>junit-jupiter</artifactId>
            <scope>test</scope>
        </dependency>
    </dependencies>

    <build>
        <plugins>
            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.jetbrains.kotlin</groupId>
                <artifactId>kotlin-maven-plugin</artifactId>
                <version>${kotlin.version}</version>
                <executions>
                    <execution>
                        <id>test-compile</id>
                        <phase>process-test-sources</phase>
                        <goals><goal>test-compile</goal></goals>
                        <configuration>
                            <sourceDirs>
                                <sourceDir>${project.basedir}/src/test/kotlin</sourceDir>
                            </sourceDirs>
                        </configuration>
                    </execution>
                </executions>
                <configuration>
                    <jvmTarget>${maven.compiler.release}</jvmTarget>
                    <languageVersion>2.4</languageVersion>
                    <apiVersion>2.4</apiVersion>
                </configuration>
            </plugin>
            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                <artifactId>maven-surefire-plugin</artifactId>
                <configuration>
                    <!-- Point the test JVM at the Rust renderer cdylib; absent the
                         dylib, the shim tests are skipped via an assumption. -->
                    <argLine>-Djava.library.path=${project.basedir}/../../rust/target/debug</argLine>
                </configuration>
            </plugin>

            <!-- Embed the Rust renderer dylib in the jar so it travels with the
                 artifact (JNA extracts it at runtime — no java.library.path needed).
                 Copies the host-platform build into META-INF/native/. Fails loudly
                 when the dylib is missing (the CI rust job builds it; locally run
                 cargo build first). -->
            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                <artifactId>maven-antrun-plugin</artifactId>
                <executions>
                    <execution>
                        <id>embed-native-renderer</id>
                        <phase>process-resources</phase>
                        <configuration>
                            <target>
                                <!-- Determine the platform library extension. -->
                                <condition property="pathland.native.ext" value=".dylib">
                                    <os family="mac" />
                                </condition>
                                <condition property="pathland.native.ext" value=".dll">
                                    <os family="windows" />
                                </condition>
                                <condition property="pathland.native.ext" value=".so">
                                    <os family="unix" />
                                </condition>
                                <property name="pathland.native.ext" value="" />

                                <!-- Release builds stage one lib per platform under
                                     target/native/<os>-<arch>/ (the CI matrix) and
                                     this copies each into META-INF/native/<os>-<arch>/.
                                     A local build has no staging dir and instead
                                     embeds the host Rust debug build in the flat
                                     META-INF/native/ layout. -->
                                <property name="pathland.native.staging" value="${project.basedir}/target/native" />
                                <available file="${pathland.native.staging}" type="dir" property="pathland.native.staged" />
                                <property name="pathland.native.host" value="${project.basedir}/../../rust/target/debug/libpathland_render_html${pathland.native.ext}" />
                                <available file="${pathland.native.host}" property="pathland.native.host.present" />

                                <fail message="No Rust renderer library to embed: neither per-platform libs at ${pathland.native.staging}/<os>-<arch>/ (release) nor the host build at ${pathland.native.host} (local). Build it first: cargo build -p pathland-render-html (in lib/rust).">
                                    <condition>
                                        <and>
                                            <not><isset property="pathland.native.staged" /></not>
                                            <not><isset property="pathland.native.host.present" /></not>
                                        </and>
                                    </condition>
                                </fail>

                                <mkdir dir="${project.build.outputDirectory}/META-INF/native" />
                                <!-- Release: copy each staged platform dir verbatim. -->
                                <copy todir="${project.build.outputDirectory}/META-INF/native">
                                    <fileset dir="${pathland.native.staging}" includes="*/*" erroronmissingdir="false" />
                                </copy>
                                <!-- Local dev: embed the host lib in the flat layout. -->
                                <copy file="${pathland.native.host}"
                                      tofile="${project.build.outputDirectory}/META-INF/native/libpathland_render_html${pathland.native.ext}"
                                      failonerror="false" />
                            </target>
                        </configuration>
                        <goals>

                        </goals>
                    </execution>

            </plugin>

Let me look at the rest of root pom (modules/publishing) and the demos, gtk/qt, test-kit, spring starter, quarkus deployment descriptors. Also inspect the api surface: package names. Key observation: pathland-server-core compile-depends on pathland-state-redis which drags lettuce into every server. That's a design smell; could make state-redis optional/provider via ServiceLoader. But user asks "combine some".

Let me enumerate modules and think about consolidation opportunities:

Core library stack:
1. view-core (5945 LOC, 112 files) — base engine
2. view-kotlin (2320, 14)
3. render-html (652, 2)
4. state-redis (113, 1)
5. server-core (4742, 29)
6. observability (356, 4)
7. test-kit (322, 2)

Demos:
11. demo-common (163, 3)
12. demo-views-kotlin (1921, 24)
13. gtk-demo (541, 4)
14. qt-demo (456, 4)
15. quarkus-demo (152, 5)
16. quarkus-kotlin-demo (154, 5)
17. spring-boot-demo (57, 2)

Candidates for combining:
- Demo modules: demo-common + demo-views-kotlin could combine (demo-common is just theme + assets, used by demo-views and desktop/web demos). But demo-common is deliberately DSL-neutral so Java demos can use assets. Combining is low risk since all demos are excluded from publishing. Could merge demo-common into demo-views-kotlin? But demo-common is used by gtk-demo/qt-demo/quarkus-demo/spring-boot-demo which also depend on demo-views-kotlin, so merging works for all. Except demo-common has Java package dev.pathland.demo.assets and resources. Fine.
- Could combine all demo views into one "pathland-demo" module? The host demos each need different runtime deps (quarkus, spring, jna). Combining host demos would conflict. Keep host demos separate.
- Demos aren't published, so churn is safe. Maybe even move demos out of the Maven reactor into a separate demo aggregator so `mvn install` of libraries doesn't build demo apps. Big structural win: current parent builds demos always. Could create lib/java/pathland-demos aggregator or move to `demos/java` folder. But user asks about combining dependencies; still worth mentioning.

- quarkus-kotlin runtime module has zero source, only descriptor; it exists to add two deps (view-kotlin, quarkus-kotlin). Could be folded into pathland-quarkus? But then pathland-quarkus would drag Kotlin into Java Quarkus users, violating DSL-neutral design. Could fold into a single extension with optional deps? Not ideal. Alternatively fold quarkus-kotlin-deployment into quarkus-kotlin? Quarkus requires separate deployment artifact; cannot merge runtime and deployment classes into one jar conventionally? Quarkus allows the deployment module separate; the deployment module is a required companion artifact. Could merge pathland-quarkus-kotlin-deployment into pathland-quarkus-deployment (they are both deployment modules, with kotlin deployment module depending on quarkus-deployment). Combining them would create one deployment jar that handles both, but then Java-only users get Kotlin deployment dependencies. Could be marked optional. Hmm. Actually Quarkus deployment artifacts aren't on runtime classpath so adding optional kotlin-deployment dependency to pathland-quarkus-deployment might be acceptable but it introduces Kotlin classes? The deployment module for kotlin currently has 15 lines/no source (just descriptor). Let me check its resources. It likely has META-INF/quarkus-extension.properties. The runtime modules need corresponding deployment artifacts to be discoverable. There may be a way to have one deployment artifact serving two runtime extensions? The extension descriptor points from runtime jar to deployment artifact via `deployment-artifact` in quarkus-extension.properties. Two runtime extensions can point to the same deployment artifact. So quarkus-kotlin-deployment could be merged into quarkus-deployment (with optional kotlin dependency). That reduces 2 modules -> 1. But again, deployment modules are small.

- state-redis: 1 class, 113 lines. Could fold into server-core? But state-redis is framework-agnostic and usable from plain JVM; and server-core already depends on it, so every server gets lettuce. Better direction: make state-redis independent and server-core not depend on it, or merge state-redis into server-core and make lettuce optional? Actually server-core referencing RedisStateStore directly means it must compile against it. Let me check server-core code. Perhaps it has `RedisStateStore` usage in `StateStores` factory. Let me inspect.

- observability: 356 LOC, 4 files, depends on server-core + micrometer, optional OTel. Could merge into server-core? But server-core would then require micrometer dependency (or optional). The separation is good for keeping core lean. However both starters already depend on both. Could merge into server-core with optional micrometer. Hmm, tradeoffs.

- test-kit: 322 LOC, 2 files, depends only view-core. Could merge into view-core's test-jar? But test-kit is a published artifact consumers use for testing. Could be published as test-jar classifier of view-core. That reduces an artifact but changes usage. Or merge into server-core test-jar? It's used by quarkus and spring tests. Probably keep.

- render-html: thin JNA shim, 652 LOC, 2 files. Depends on view-core at compile (why? probably for protocol constants or view types) + jna. Could merge into server-core? render-html is usable standalone by any JVM server, and server-core depends on it. But merging into server-core would force every server-core consumer to have the HTML renderer + native dylib. Currently server-core already depends on render-html, so effectively that's already true. Hmm. But render-html is a legitimate standalone artifact ("HTML renderer binding"). Keeping separate makes sense for non-server consumers (e.g. anyone emitting HTML locally). Yet server-core depending on render-html is another coupling.

Big picture: the "core" dependency chain is:
view-core <- view-kotlin
view-core <- render-html <- server-core <- observability
view-core <- state-redis <- server-core
server-core + observability <- spring-starter / quarkus(-kotlin)
view-core <- test-kit

Potential consolidation:
A. Merge view-kotlin into view-core? Both are Kotlin now. view-core is ~5945 LOC and view-kotlin 2320. They're conceptually engine vs authoring DSL. The AGENTS.md describes them as separate: core engine vs sole authoring DSL. Merging might be reasonable since both Kotlin, but the layering is meaningful (view-core is DSL-neutral engine; view-kotlin adds ergonomic DSL). Many users might want core only. Keep separate? Could be a candidate but higher risk/API churn.

B. Merge demo-common into demo-views-kotlin (or into a single demo module). Easy, removes 1 module, all demo-only.

C. Merge state-redis into server-core OR invert dependency. Let me check usage in server-core. Actually the dependency direction is server-core -> state-redis which is odd. Let me grep.

D. Merge observability into server-core? Optional micrometer dep. Removes 1 module, but compromises leanness.

E. Merge render-html into server-core? server-core already depends on it; but render-html standalone value. Also it has heavy build step (Rust dylib embed). Merging would make server-core build need rust. Currently server-core depends on render-html artifact, so if building reactor, still need rust. Not a strong reason.

F. Quarkus kotlin deployment merge into quarkus-deployment; quarkus-kotlin runtime maybe a single tiny module. Could combine quarkus-kotlin-deployment into pathland-quarkus-deployment. Removes 1 module.

G. Merge spring-boot-starter and quarkus into `pathland-server`? No — framework glue must stay separate.

H. Demos: reduce 7 demo modules to maybe 2: one demo-views/assets module + host demos. Could also move all demos to a separate profile so library install doesn't build them.

Let me inspect server-core usage of state-redis and render-html to see if decoupling is viable. Also check spring starter and quarkus for StateStores usage. Also check what modules publish (demo modules skip). Check status.md and README for intent.

Adding this extension + a `PathlandApp` CDI bean gives a running app; `MountedApp` beans host more apps at their own subpaths (the BFF layout). Author the root view with `pathland-view-kotlin`; Java hosts return Kotlin views from a `PathlandApp` bean. ## Implemented - **Java host / Kotlin views**: `CounterApp` is a Java CDI bean whose `newRoot()` returns a Kotlin-authored fixture view; the multi-session WebSocket tests prove SSR + live deltas work through that mount. - **Crawler endpoints**: `/robots.txt` (text/plain) and `/sitemap.xml` (application/xml) are real routes before the SPA catch-all, so Lighthouse does not parse the HTML shell as robots.txt. - **`PathlandSocket`** — `@WebSocket("/_pathland/ws")` for the root app: 1:1 sessions per connection (a fresh `uiId` per connection + the client's `wid` state scope from the `?wid=` query param), binary events routed into the root registry of the `PathlandHost`. **Stateless (critical)**: quarkus-websockets-next endpoints default to `@Singleton` — one shared instance for all connections — so the per-connection ids come from `connection.id()` + the handshake and the `QuarkusConnection` adapters live in a map keyed by connection id. Memoizing `uiId`/`wid`/`transport` on the shared instance collapsed every connection onto ONE session (multiple browsers shared one UI model — a probe or second tab drove the first tab's session). - **`MountedPathlandSocket`** — `@WebSocket("/{app}/_pathland/ws")` for mounted apps: the `{app}` path param resolves the app's registry. Mount paths are single-segment. Same stateless rule as the root socket. - **`IndexResource`** — JAX-RS SSR catch-all (`/` + deep links; `/_pathland/**` and the Quarkus non-application root `/q/**` — health/metrics — excluded via negative lookahead) dispatching to the longest-mount app (prefix stripped); SSR renders defaults (no session cookie — per-window state arrives over the WS); per-app framework files (`/{app}/_pathland/...`, e.g. the mounted app's bundle) are served from the shared `/_pathland/**` classpath mount. Quarkus serves the global `/_pathland/**` bundle + asset mount from `META-INF/resources` before JAX-RS. **`/_pathland/{name}.css`** (global JAX-RS route + the mounted-base `frameworkFile` path) serves the renderer-owned content-hashed base design (`HtmlRenderer.baseCss()` at `baseCssName()`) as `text/css` with `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`. **`/_pathland/icons/{name}.svg`** serves the renderer-owned icon glyphs from the shared Rust renderer (`HtmlRenderer.iconSvg` → `pathland_html_icon_svg`) with an `immutable` cache header — no static CSS/icon files on any host. SSR links the CSS via `PathlandSession` → `renderLinked`. - **`PathlandRegistryProducer`** — CDI `@Produces @Singleton` `PathlandHost` from every `MountedApp` bean plus the lone `PathlandApp` bean (mounted at `/`); `@Disposes` shuts it down. Reads the `pathland.debug-html` config property (default `false`) to enable per-node HTML comments in SSR output, and `pathland.service-worker` (default `false`) to opt the DOM client into the per-window-id service worker (issue #155) — served at `{base}/sw.js` with `Service-Worker-Allowed: /` + `Cache-Control: no-cache`. - **`ServiceWorkerFilter`** — serves `/_pathland/sw.js` (root and mounted bases) with `Service-Worker-Allowed: /` + `Cache-Control: no-cache`, so the client's root-scoped registration succeeds. A `Filters` handler always runs before routes, so it wins over Quarkus's static-resource handler (which sends neither header, and whose configured max-age would otherwise cache the script and delay update detection). - **Observability (issue #62)** — `quarkus-micrometer` (a `MeterRegistry` bean) + `quarkus-smallrye-health`: the producer builds a `MicrometerTelemetry` over the registry and decorates it with `TracingTelemetry` when a `Tracer` bean is present and `quarkus.otel.enabled` (default `true`; the extension never touches the OTel API when the extension is absent/disabled). `PathlandHealthCheck` (`@Readiness`) reports the host UP with `activeSessions`/`mounts` at `/q/health`; the `pathland.*` meters appear at `/q/metrics`. - **`QuarkusConnection`** — adapts `WebSocketConnection` to `PathlandConnection`. Sends are **serialized** (one `sendBinary` subscription in flight, the rest queued), and a **send failure closes the connection** so the session drops it and the DOM client reconnects + `META::RESYNC` (recoverable) instead of silently stalling on an "open" socket that never delivers (the remote seekbar symptom). **Send timeout**: a `sendBinary` that neither completes nor fails within 10 s (a half-dead connection / a dropped proxy upstream leg) is marked failed and closed — a hung send would otherwise wedge the serialized drain forever. **Keep-alive pings**: the connection sends a WS-protocol ping every 15 s (browsers auto-pong) to keep the connection warm through middleboxes and detect a dead client; `close()` stops the keep-alive scheduler (the sockets' `@OnClose` calls it). - **Heartbeat** — both sockets reply to a client `META::PING` with a `META::PONG` **at the transport layer** (through their `QuarkusConnection`, no actor/session dependency, and a PING never creates or wakes a session); spec/OPCODE.md §Transport heartbeat. - **Failure handling** — `fail()` logs the reason; `close()` (socket `@OnClose`) no longer calls `close()` on the already-closed connection (no spurious "Connection already closed" noise). A **transient write failure on a connection that still reports open is logged, not closed** — only a confirmed-dead channel (or a send hung past the timeout) warrants closing. The send-timeout task is **cancelled when the send completes**, so a completed-but-late callback can't false-time-out and kill a healthy connection. Keep-alive pings are sent directly (Vert.x serializes writes — no sync with `sendBinary` needed). - `META-INF/beans.xml` so Quarkus discovers the extension. - **Quarkus extension metadata** — runtime + `pathland-quarkus-deployment`; the runtime provides the `dev.pathland.quarkus` capability. The runtime has no dependency on the authoring DSL. Tests use Kotlin-authored fixture views to prove a Java CDI bean can mount them. ## App DX ```java @ApplicationScoped public class MyApp { @Produces @Singleton PathlandApp main() { return () -> new MyHomeView(); } @Produces @Singleton MountedApp support() { return MountedApp.of("/support", ...); } } ``` ## Verified by Manual: the `pathland-quarkus-demo` renders `/` (the music player, whose Now Playing pane embeds the small `/ad` app via a **same-server `ProxyView`**, spec/PROXY.md) and `/ad` (the ad app); a WebSocket handshake to `/_pathland/ws` and `/ad/_pathland/ws` returns 101. `ProxyDemoTest` (`@QuarkusTest`) asserts `GET /` embeds the `/ad` app's subtree with remapped node ids (`data-pathland-id="1073741825"` — proxy block 0 + origin id 1). Core behavior is covered by `pathland-server-core` tests. `MultiSessionWebSocketTest` (`@QuarkusTest`) opens **100 concurrent real WS sessions** against `/_pathland/ws` (via the shared `pathland-server-core` test-jar probe) and asserts each connects, re-syncs, gets transport-level PONGs, stays isolated, and is never closed by the peer. `PathlandObservabilityTest` (`@QuarkusTest`) asserts `/q/health` reports the Pathland check UP and `/q/metrics` exposes the `pathland.*` namespace. `BaseCssTest` (`@QuarkusTest`) asserts the linked SSR ``, the immutable `text/css` response at the global and mounted bases, and a 404 for an unknown hash.=== server status # pathland-server-core — implementation status **Last updated:** October 28, 2026 The transport-agnostic Pathland server runtime: one app instance per session (SSR + live 16-byte opcode deltas + environment), the session registry, and the **multi-app host** (the BFF), shared by the Spring Boot and Quarkus starters. No web-framework dependency — framework glue lives in the starters. ## Implemented - **Window metadata + SSR head attrs**: `PathlandSession.renderHtml` injects host attrs into the renderer's opening `` (which now carries `lang`), and `FrameRebase` rebases `SET_WINDOW_METADATA` string offsets. Proxy origin metadata is dropped with the other META opcodes. - **`PathlandApp`** — the app's root-view factory (`View newRoot()` + optional `theme()`); the single app-specific piece a starter needs. - **`MountedApp`** — `record MountedApp(String path, PathlandApp app)`: one app mounted at a subpath prefix (normalized; `/` = root). Hosts any number of them. - **`PathlandHost`** — the multi-app dispatcher: one `PathlandRegistry` per mounted app (own actor thread, own sessions). `match(requestUri)` resolves the owning registry by **longest mount-prefix match** and reports the **mount-stripped route** (a root mount claims every unclaimed path). Duplicate mount paths are rejected at construction. - **`PathlandRegistry`** — session lifecycle per app: single actor thread, 1:1 sessions keyed by a **per-connection `uiId`** (a fresh id per WebSocket connection, so two windows of the same browser never share a UI model), lazy creation on first environment message, pending connections (each carrying the mount-prefixed state scope from the client's per-window `wid`), `open(uiId, wid, conn)`/`environment`/`dispatch`/`resync`/`close`/`renderHtml`/`shutdown`. New: - `mountPath()`/`base()` — each app's framework base is `//_pathland` (`/_pathland` for the root), emitted as `data-pathland-base` in SSR; - `stateScope(windowId)` — app-qualified state-store scope (`mount:wid`) so apps and windows sharing a store never collide; - `stripRoute(route)` — strips the mount prefix from SSR routes, WS environment ROUTE fields, **and inbound `NAVIGATE` URLs** (browser back/forward sends the real address, e.g. `http://host/app2/home`), so a mounted app always sees its own route space (`/app2/home` → `/home`). `Router.pathOf` is reused for URL→path extraction. - **Per-window isolation (no session cookie)**: session identity (the `uiId` map key) is deliberately separate from the persisted-state scope (the client's `wid`, carried only on the WebSocket URL — never in the page URL, so the address bar stays clean). The SSR request therefore has no `wid`: `renderHtml(route, wid)` with a null `wid` renders defaults; the client's live session is scoped by the WS `wid`, and a same-tab reload re-syncs that window's persisted state over the WebSocket. The old `session` cookie is removed. - **`PathlandSession`** — per-session: builds the `Platform.ACTIVE_PATH` signal, mounts `app.newRoot().modifiers(environmentBinding(e -> e.key(ACTIVE_PATH).value(activePath)))`, **delta-batched send-on-`endFrame`** (`DeltaBatcher` coalesces per-signal frames into one batch — flush ~20 ms or 16 KB, string offsets rebased — so a continuous input burst can't overflow a remote WebSocket send queue), `applyEnvironment` (re-route guard-aware via the bound router), `dispatch` (tap/nav-intent/text/value/date/NAVIGATE), `resync`, `renderHtml`, `close`. Runtime theming: `setTheme(ThemeData)`, `resetTheme()`, and `setColorScheme(ThemeMode)` emit one `META::RESET_THEME` + `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` frame or `META::SET_COLOR_SCHEME` to the live client (renderer state; no tree re-emission). The SSR document keeps the mount theme until a resync/reload. `sendBatch` drops the connection on any send failure (a client reconnect then re-syncs via `META::RESYNC` instead of silently stalling on an "open" socket); `closeConnection` best-effort closes an `AutoCloseable` adapter (the starters now close their underlying WebSocket on failure). Now takes the app's `base` and `stateScope` explicitly (the registry supplies them). - **`DeltaBatcher`** — merges session delta frames (opcodes + a single rebased string section) and flushes as one network batch on a timer/byte threshold; the Java analogue of the Rust transport's `Batcher`. It owns the per-session **message sequence** (stamped on each flushed batch via `FrameCodec.encodeFrame(frame, sequence)`) so the DOM client can detect a lost batch and recover with `META::RESYNC` (spec/OPCODE.md §Sequence gap detection); an empty flush consumes no sequence. The **sender runs OUTSIDE the monitor** — a blocking/queueing send can never stall the actor thread's `append` or the flush scheduler. Coalescing tests cover merging + rebasing, a 100-frame burst collapsing to one send, incrementing sequences, and a blocking sender not holding the lock. - **`PathlandConnection`** — the transport seam (`send(byte[])`/`isOpen()`); each starter adapts its WebSocket type to it. - **Observability seam** — `PathlandTelemetry` (default `NOOP`): the runtime emits session open/close, inbound event batches, flushed batches (frames/opcodes/bytes + merge-encode time), SSR render latency, resync requests, and send failures; the host binds a pull-based active-sessions gauge. `PathlandHost`/`PathlandRegistry`/ `PathlandSession`/`DeltaBatcher` thread it through (a host with no telemetry pays nothing). `pathland-observability` provides the Micrometer + OpenTelemetry adapters; the starters auto-wire them. Logging is **SLF4J** (both frameworks bind it) — the old ad-hoc `System.out` is gone. See issue #62. - **Concurrency stress** — `RegistryConcurrencyTest`: 100 sessions driven through the registry concurrently (clicks on each session's button) while SSR-style requests construct throwaway sessions on request threads — the shared-actor / global-`Scheduler` cross-session corruption guard. Each session must reach exactly its own click count (no lost effects, no cross-session values). - **Shared WS test harness** — `dev.pathland.server.test.{WsSession,MultiSessionProbe}` (a JDK-WebSocket client speaking the PLPL protocol: env/resync/click/ping) lives in the **`pathland-test-kit`** module (main scope, so package builds resolve it as a normal jar); the starters' 100-session stress tests reuse it. - **`StateStores`** — default state store: Redis when reachable, else the supplied fallback. - **SSR debug comments (property-gated)**: `PathlandSession`/`PathlandRegistry` take a `debugHtml` flag (constructor + `isDebugHtml()`); when set, `renderHtml` uses the renderer's debug mode so every rendered node is prefixed with an HTML comment naming its component and the modifiers applied. The Spring/Quarkus starters bind it to the `pathland.debug-html` property (default `false`). - **Reserved framework root**: `PathlandSession.PATHLAND_BASE` (`/_pathland`) — the SSR page carries the app's base as `data-pathland-base` and the DOM-client bundle is injected at `{base}/dom-renderer-.js` (`PathlandAssets` reads the current name from the `_pathland/dom-renderer.current` manifest on the classpath, resolving through the thread context classloader first so a Quarkus extension parent loader can see the application's static resources; it falls back to the literal `dom-renderer.js` only when absent) so the client's WebSocket and asset refs resolve from the same reserved prefix (spec DSL.md). The content-hashed name busts the immutable asset cache with a fresh URL per build. The built-in base design is linked the same way: `renderHtml` renders through `HtmlRenderer.renderLinked(frame, root, base)`, so the CSS href is `{base}/base-.css` (token overrides/fit rules stay inline). Multi-app hosts give each mount its own base. - **Per-window-id service worker (opt-in, issue #155)**: `PathlandHost` carries a host-level `serviceWorker` flag (default `false`; one registration covers the whole origin) threaded to every `PathlandRegistry`; `PathlandSession.renderHtml` emits `data-pathland-service-worker="true"` on `` when set, and the DOM client registers `{base}/sw.js` (root scope) / unregisters when absent (the kill switch). `PathlandRegistry.serviceWorkerUrl()` names the served script. `renderHtml` also emits `data-pathland-ssr-scoped="true"` when the request carried a real per-window id, so the client can skip its initial `META::RESYNC` (the SSR was already rendered with that window's state and the live session shares it). ## Not implemented / gaps - No multi-node/shared sessions (each server owns its sessions in-memory).

The old `session` cookie is removed. - **`PathlandSession`** — per-session: builds the `Platform.ACTIVE_PATH` signal, mounts `app.newRoot().modifiers(environmentBinding(e -> e.key(ACTIVE_PATH).value(activePath)))`, **delta-batched send-on-`endFrame`** (`DeltaBatcher` coalesces per-signal frames into one batch — flush ~20 ms or 16 KB, string offsets rebased — so a continuous input burst can't overflow a remote WebSocket send queue), `applyEnvironment` (re-route guard-aware via the bound router), `dispatch` (tap/nav-intent/text/value/date/NAVIGATE), `resync`, `renderHtml`, `close`. Runtime theming: `setTheme(ThemeData)`, `resetTheme()`, and `setColorScheme(ThemeMode)` emit one `META::RESET_THEME` + `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` frame or `META::SET_COLOR_SCHEME` to the live client (renderer state; no tree re-emission). The SSR document keeps the mount theme until a resync/reload. `sendBatch` drops the connection on any send failure (a client reconnect then re-syncs via `META::RESYNC` instead of silently stalling on an "open" socket); `closeConnection` best-effort closes an `AutoCloseable` adapter (the starters now close their underlying WebSocket on failure). Now takes the app's `base` and `stateScope` explicitly (the registry supplies them). - **`DeltaBatcher`** — merges session delta frames (opcodes + a single rebased string section) and flushes as one network batch on a timer/byte threshold; the Java analogue of the Rust transport's `Batcher`. It owns the per-session **message sequence** (stamped on each flushed batch via `FrameCodec.encodeFrame(frame, sequence)`) so the DOM client can detect a lost batch and recover with `META::RESYNC` (spec/OPCODE.md §Sequence gap detection); an empty flush consumes no sequence. The **sender runs OUTSIDE the monitor** — a blocking/queueing send can never stall the actor thread's `append` or the flush scheduler. Coalescing tests cover merging + rebasing, a 100-frame burst collapsing to one send, incrementing sequences, and a blocking sender not holding the lock. - **`PathlandConnection`** — the transport seam (`send(byte[])`/`isOpen()`); each starter adapts its WebSocket type to it. - **Observability seam** — `PathlandTelemetry` (default `NOOP`): the runtime emits session open/close, inbound event batches, flushed batches (frames/opcodes/bytes + merge-encode time), SSR render latency, resync requests, and send failures; the host binds a pull-based active-sessions gauge. `PathlandHost`/`PathlandRegistry`/ `PathlandSession`/`DeltaBatcher` thread it through (a host with no telemetry pays nothing). `pathland-observability` provides the Micrometer + OpenTelemetry adapters; the starters auto-wire them. Logging is **SLF4J** (both frameworks bind it) — the old ad-hoc `System.out` is gone. See issue #62. - **Concurrency stress** — `RegistryConcurrencyTest`: 100 sessions driven through the registry concurrently (clicks on each session's button) while SSR-style requests construct throwaway sessions on request threads — the shared-actor / global-`Scheduler` cross-session corruption guard. Each session must reach exactly its own click count (no lost effects, no cross-session values). - **Shared WS test harness** — `dev.pathland.server.test.{WsSession,MultiSessionProbe}` (a JDK-WebSocket client speaking the PLPL protocol: env/resync/click/ping) lives in the **`pathland-test-kit`** module (main scope, so package builds resolve it as a normal jar); the starters' 100-session stress tests reuse it. - **`StateStores`** — default state store: Redis when reachable, else the supplied fallback. - **SSR debug comments (property-gated)**: `PathlandSession`/`PathlandRegistry` take a `debugHtml` flag (constructor + `isDebugHtml()`); when set, `renderHtml` uses the renderer's debug mode so every rendered node is prefixed with an HTML comment naming its component and the modifiers applied. The Spring/Quarkus starters bind it to the `pathland.debug-html` property (default `false`). - **Reserved framework root**: `PathlandSession.PATHLAND_BASE` (`/_pathland`) — the SSR page carries the app's base as `data-pathland-base` and the DOM-client bundle is injected at `{base}/dom-renderer-.js` (`PathlandAssets` reads the current name from the `_pathland/dom-renderer.current` manifest on the classpath, resolving through the thread context classloader first so a Quarkus extension parent loader can see the application's static resources; it falls back to the literal `dom-renderer.js` only when absent) so the client's WebSocket and asset refs resolve from the same reserved prefix (spec DSL.md). The content-hashed name busts the immutable asset cache with a fresh URL per build. The built-in base design is linked the same way: `renderHtml` renders through `HtmlRenderer.renderLinked(frame, root, base)`, so the CSS href is `{base}/base-.css` (token overrides/fit rules stay inline). Multi-app hosts give each mount its own base. - **Per-window-id service worker (opt-in, issue #155)**: `PathlandHost` carries a host-level `serviceWorker` flag (default `false`; one registration covers the whole origin) threaded to every `PathlandRegistry`; `PathlandSession.renderHtml` emits `data-pathland-service-worker="true"` on `` when set, and the DOM client registers `{base}/sw.js` (root scope) / unregisters when absent (the kill switch). `PathlandRegistry.serviceWorkerUrl()` names the served script. `renderHtml` also emits `data-pathland-ssr-scoped="true"` when the request carried a real per-window id, so the client can skip its initial `META::RESYNC` (the SSR was already rendered with that window's state and the live session shares it). ## Not implemented / gaps - No multi-node/shared sessions (each server owns its sessions in-memory).

Let me read view-core status around line 64 for intent, and check the java directory in view-core (empty? find returned no files, so directory exists but empty). Not important.

Let me also understand if `server-core` depending on `state-redis` drags Lettuce transitively. Yes, compile scope. This can be improved with optional. But user's ask is combining.

Let me consider a stronger consolidation proposal:
- Combine view-core + view-kotlin into a single `pathland-view` artifact? Both Kotlin; layering is engine vs DSL. AGENTS says pathland-view-core is engine and pathland-view-kotlin is DSL. They have separate status. Combining reduces two deps to one, but disadvantages: consumers wanting only engine get DSL. Probably not recommended.
- Combine render-html + state-redis into server-core? They're both "adapters" but independent. Not recommended.
- Combine observability into server-core? Could, but micrometer dependency.
- Combine test-kit into view-core as test-jar? Or into server-core test-jar. Maybe.
- Merge quarkus-kotlin-deployment into quarkus-deployment: possible, removes 1 module but creates coupling. Actually deployment artifacts are only used by Quarkus at build time, so combining is low-risk but the deployment for kotlin requires quarkus-kotlin-deployment (build item for Kotlin compilation) — that's a Quarkus extension dependency that needs to be present when the `pathland-quarkus-kotlin` runtime extension is present. If both deployment jars are separate, only apps using kotlin get the kotlin deployment. Combining would always pull quarkus-kotlin-deployment for Java users. Not ideal.
- Merge quarkus-kotlin (zero code) into pathland-quarkus? No, because that would force Kotlin on Java hosts.
- Merge demos: demo-common into demo-views-kotlin. Then all 5 host demos only depend on demo-views-kotlin. Good.
- The gtk-demo and qt-demo share RingEventReader implementation (duplicated?). Let me diff them. If they're nearly identical, maybe a shared demo module. Let me check. This is a code duplication issue rather than module count. Let me compare.

## Package boundary

- `pathland-view-core` is one Maven module for now: `core`/`engine` are logical
  subpackages inside it, with a few deliberate intra-module references
  (`Color`/`MediaController`/`Modified` materialize `PathlandNode`). Splitting
  `core` and `engine` into separate artifacts requires a node SPI first.
- Production runtimes/renderers (`pathland-server-core`,
  `pathland-render-html`, `pathland-state-redis`, `pathland-test-kit`) depend on
  core. Java-module tests add `pathland-view-kotlin` in test scope and mount
  Kotlin-authored fixture views; production starters remain DSL-neutral.
=== render html status
# pathland-render-html (Java) — implementation status

**Last updated:** October 28, 2026

The **Java binding to the Rust HTML renderer** (`dev.pathland.render.html`) — a
thin **JNA shim** over `libpathland_render_html`. There is a **single renderer**
(the Rust crate), reused by every language; the former hand-written retained
Java renderer is removed. Protocol contract: `spec/`.

## Implemented

- **Stateless JNA shim**: `HtmlRenderer.instance()` links the Rust cdylib;
  `render(frame, root)` / `renderFragment(frame, root)` /
  `renderFullSnapshot(frame, root)` render a self-contained snapshot frame to
  HTML in one pass (no retained tree, no `applyFrame`); `pathland_html_free`
  releases native strings. Lazy-loaded; skipped (test assumption) when the dylib
  is absent from `java.library.path`.
- **Debug comments**: `renderDebug(frame, root)` / `renderFragmentDebug(...)`
  bind the Rust `pathland_html_render_debug` exports — each rendered node is
  prefixed with an HTML comment naming its component type and the modifiers
  applied (opt-in; the plain `render` output is unchanged).
- **Full Rust renderer surface** (canonical): all spec components render inline
  (structural + decorative CSS in a single `style` attribute), ARIA/event
  attributes, `IS_SECURE` → password, `TOGGLE_STYLE` variants,
  `DATE_PICKER_MODE`, and literal colors inline. The default `render(...)`
  injects the renderer's built-in `<style>` block (preflight reset + design
  tokens + `.pathland-*` component defaults) into every document — no
  `/tailwind.css`. `renderLinked(frame, root, cssBase)` /
  `renderLinkedDebug(...)` instead emit a content-hashed
  `<link rel="stylesheet" href="{cssBase}/{baseCssName()}">`; token overrides
  and fit-band rules stay inline. `baseCss()` / `baseCssName()` bind the Rust
  `pathland_html_base_css[_name]` exports so the Spring/Quarkus starters serve
  the renderer-owned bytes immutable. A missing linked export degrades to the
  inline document.
- **Icon glyphs from the shared renderer**: `iconSvg(String name)` binds the
  Rust `pathland_html_icon_svg` export over the C ABI — the full inline `<svg>`
  for a canonical `ICON_NAME` (unknown/extension names → the renderer's
  fallback glyph, never null). Hosts serve `/_pathland/icons/<name>.svg` from
  it (Spring/Quarkus route a few lines in their starters), so the DOM client's
  lazy icon fetch gets the same glyph data SSR inlines from — one Rust source,
=== view-kotlin status
# pathland-view-kotlin — implementation status

**Last updated:** November 3, 2026

The sole JVM authoring surface (`dev.pathland.view.dsl`), Kotlin-owned over the
Kotlin `pathland-view-core`. The Java DSL, its processor, and its Java-only
Quarkus extension/starter alias are removed.

## Authoring surface

- **Kotlin-owned**: all primitives, shapes, stacks, grids, scroll/lazy
  containers, `ForEach`, `Button`, text/value controls, media, navigation,
  `Label`, `ViewThatFits`/`Fit`, `ProxyView`, styles (`PlainButtonStyle`,

=== render html status
# pathland-render-html (Java) — implementation status

**Last updated:** October 28, 2026

The **Java binding to the Rust HTML renderer** (`dev.pathland.render.html`) — a
thin **JNA shim** over `libpathland_render_html`. There is a **single renderer**
(the Rust crate), reused by every language; the former hand-written retained
Java renderer is removed. Protocol contract: `spec/`.

## Implemented

- **Stateless JNA shim**: `HtmlRenderer.instance()` links the Rust cdylib;
  `render(frame, root)` / `renderFragment(frame, root)` /
  `renderFullSnapshot(frame, root)` render a self-contained snapshot frame to
  HTML in one pass (no retained tree, no `applyFrame`); `pathland_html_free`
  releases native strings. Lazy-loaded; skipped (test assumption) when the dylib
  is absent from `java.library.path`.
- **Debug comments**: `renderDebug(frame, root)` / `renderFragmentDebug(...)`
  bind the Rust `pathland_html_render_debug` exports — each rendered node is
  prefixed with an HTML comment naming its component type and the modifiers
  applied (opt-in; the plain `render` output is unchanged).
- **Full Rust renderer surface** (canonical): all spec components render inline
  (structural + decorative CSS in a single `style` attribute), ARIA/event
  attributes, `IS_SECURE` → password, `TOGGLE_STYLE` variants,
  `DATE_PICKER_MODE`, and literal colors inline. The default `render(...)`
  injects the renderer's built-in `<style>` block (preflight reset + design
  tokens + `.pathland-*` component defaults) into every document — no
  `/tailwind.css`. `renderLinked(frame, root, cssBase)` /
  `renderLinkedDebug(...)` instead emit a content-hashed
  `<link rel="stylesheet" href="{cssBase}/{baseCssName()}">`; token overrides
  and fit-band rules stay inline. `baseCss()` / `baseCssName()` bind the Rust
  `pathland_html_base_css[_name]` exports so the Spring/Quarkus starters serve
  the renderer-owned bytes immutable. A missing linked export degrades to the
  inline document.
- **Icon glyphs from the shared renderer**: `iconSvg(String name)` binds the
  Rust `pathland_html_icon_svg` export over the C ABI — the full inline `<svg>`
  for a canonical `ICON_NAME` (unknown/extension names → the renderer's
  fallback glyph, never null). Hosts serve `/_pathland/icons/<name>.svg` from
  it (Spring/Quarkus route a few lines in their starters), so the DOM client's
  lazy icon fetch gets the same glyph data SSR inlines from — one Rust source,

I have enough for a plan. Since this is plan mode, I should present analysis and ask which direction the user prefers. Let me construct a clear dependency graph, grouping.

Dependency graph:

```
view-core (engine + protocol + signals + state + transport + router, Kotlin)
├── view-kotlin (DSL)          [published]
├── render-html (JNA shim)     [published]
│   └── server-core            [published]
│       ├── observability      [published]
│       ├── spring-boot-starter [published]  (server-core + observability)
│       └── quarkus            [published]  (server-core + observability)
│           ├── quarkus-deployment [published, build-time]
│           └── quarkus-kotlin [published, ~0 code]
│               └── quarkus-kotlin-deployment [published, build-time]
├── state-redis                [published]  (also depended on by server-core)
└── test-kit                   [published, test harness]

demo-common (theme + 24 assets) [not published]
└── demo-views-kotlin (MusicPlayerView, AdView) [not published]
    ├── gtk-demo
    ├── qt-demo
    ├── quarkus-demo (+ quarkus, demo-common)
    ├── quarkus-kotlin-demo (+ quarkus-kotlin, view-kotlin)
    └── spring-boot-demo (+ starter, demo-common)
```

Observations/issues:
1. server-core -> state-redis compile dependency (Lettuce leaks into all server apps). Should ideally be inverted / optional / discovered.
2. server-core -> render-html compile dependency (native dylib needed for any server). Actually HTML rendering is core to it (SSR), so fine, but means native lib always.
3. demo-common is only used by demo modules, but is a separate module. Merge into demo-views-kotlin (or a demo aggregator) removes a module.
4. quarkus-kotlin has no code; only manifest + deps. It exists to avoid forcing Kotlin on Java hosts. Keep? Or could be a "facade POM" with packaging pom? Currently jar. But merging into pathland-quarkus would violate DSL-neutrality. Keep.
5. quarkus-kotlin-deployment is 15 lines. Could merge into quarkus-deployment but would pull Kotlin deployment into Java users; not worth it.
6. test-kit could be attached as a test-jar of view-core or server-core, but it's a public-ish test utility, keeping separate is fine. 2 files.
7. view-core and view-kotlin both Kotlin; could merge into one artifact, but layering is intentional and status says core is engine, view-kotlin DSL. Would force DSL on engine-only consumers. Keep.
8. observability (2 files) could merge into server-core, but then micrometer dependency pollutes core. Could make optional. Separating is reasonable but could be considered. Alternatively merge observability into each starter? No.
9. render-html could merge into server-core, but it's a reusable standalone binding; keep separate.
10. Demos: 7 modules. Can reduce: demo-common -> demo-views-kotlin. Then remove demo-common. Host demos could be consolidated: all web demos (quarkus, quarkus-kotlin, spring) could arguably become examples not modules, or moved to separate demos aggregator so library build doesn't build them. gtk/qt demos need different classpaths. Could keep 5 host demos as separate demo artifacts, or reduce by making a single "pathland-demo-web" with profiles? Not clean.

Maybe more impactful: Use Maven profiles to exclude demo modules from default build (or move demos to separate `lib/java-demos` reactor). That addresses "a lot of maven packages" without changing published modules.

Recommendations by value/risk:
- Low risk / clear win: merge demo-common into demo-views-kotlin, drop demo-common module + status.md; move all demo modules out of the library reactor into a separate demo aggregator (or profile) so `mvn install` only builds the 11 library modules.

=== test-kit status
# Pathland Test Kit

Shared test infrastructure for the Pathland Java reactor.

## Implemented

- **`dev.pathland.server.test.WsSession`** — a minimal JDK-`java.net.http.WebSocket`
  client that speaks the PLPL wire protocol (environment / resync / click / ping),
  collects decoded frames + peer-close codes, and tracks unexpected closes. One shared
  `HttpClient` across all connections.
- **`dev.pathland.server.test.MultiSessionProbe`** — the shared 100-session (configurable
  via `PATHLAND_TEST_SESSIONS`) WS stress probe used by the Quarkus + Spring starters'
  `MultiSessionWebSocketTest`: every session connects, re-syncs, gets transport-level
  PONGs, stays isolated (only its own click counts reach its label), and is never closed
  by the peer.

The harness lives in **main scope** so `mvn package` (the Docker/Render build, which runs
`-Dmaven.test.skip=true`) resolves it as a normal jar — a `tests`-classifier test-jar
dependency previously broke the package build. The starters depend on this module with
`scope=test`.

## Verified by

The starters' `MultiSessionWebSocketTest` runs (both green in `mvn clean install`); the
full Docker image build (`docker build -f lib/java/pathland-quarkus-demo/Dockerfile .`)
succeeds.=== observability status
# pathland-observability — implementation status

**Last updated:** October 3, 2026

Observability adapters for the framework-agnostic `pathland-server-core`
telemetry seam. The core emits lifecycle/throughput events through
`PathlandTelemetry` (default `NOOP`); this module turns them into metrics and
spans. Protocol/contract context: `spec/OPCODE.md`; the seam itself is in
`pathland-server-core`.

## Implemented

- **`MicrometerTelemetry`** — a `PathlandTelemetry` over any Micrometer
  `MeterRegistry` (Prometheus, OTLP, …). Metric catalog:
  - `pathland.sessions.active` — gauge (pull-based, bound by the host)
  - `pathland.sessions.opened` / `pathland.sessions.closed` — counters
  - `pathland.events.received` — counter (decoded inbound events)
  - `pathland.batches.sent` / `pathland.frames.sent` / `pathland.bytes.sent` — counters
  - `pathland.batch.size` — distribution summary (opcodes per batch)
  - `pathland.batch.flush` — timer (merge + encode)
  - `pathland.ssr.render` — timer (SSR render round-trip)
  - `pathland.resync.requested` — counter
  - `pathland.ws.failures` — counter
  - Every meter is tagged by `mount` (bounded). Registrations are idempotent, so
    a builder per event is cheap and cannot leak meters.
- **`TracingTelemetry`** — an OpenTelemetry decorator over another
  `PathlandTelemetry`: emits a span per frame send (`pathland.frame.send`), per
  inbound event batch (`pathland.event.batch`), and per SSR render
  (`pathland.ssr.render`), with the wrapped telemetry still receiving every
  event. Spans are back-dated by the measured duration so they render with the
  real latency. Opt-in — the starters build it only when a `Tracer`/`OpenTelemetry`
  bean is available.

## Not implemented / gaps

- No client-side (browser) telemetry — server-side only.
- `ws.failures` does not tag the failure reason (unbounded cardinality).

## Verified by

`mvn test -pl pathland-observability` — `MicrometerTelemetryTest` (the full
metric catalog + per-mount tagging) and `TracingTelemetryTest` (span names via an
in-memory OTel exporter, plus delegation). The starters' tests assert the wiring
end to end (`/q/health` + `/q/metrics`, `/actuator/health` + `pathland.*` meters).

4. Just analysis, no changes

Actually maybe one question with multiple selection? The user may want a plan. But plan mode expects a plan. I'll present the dependency walkthrough and a proposed plan, then ask which scope to implement.

Let me be careful: the artifact publication concerns. Demos are not published, so demo merges are safe. Published artifacts changes (merging view-core/view-kotlin etc.) would break consumers and versioning, so not advisable pre-1.0 perhaps but still.

Let me produce a detailed but organized response.

Graph listing:

Published (11 artifacts, incl. deployment):
1. pathland-view-core
2. pathland-view-kotlin
3. pathland-render-html
4. pathland-state-redis
5. pathland-server-core
6. pathland-observability
7. pathland-test-kit
8. pathland-spring-boot-starter
9. pathland-quarkus
10. pathland-quarkus-deployment
11. pathland-quarkus-kotlin
12. pathland-quarkus-kotlin-deployment

That's 12 total. Demos 7 = 19 modules.

Coupling findings:
- server-core -> state-redis (hard, compile) means Redis a mandatory transitive dep for every Spring/Quarkus app. This is the most questionable edge. StateStores factory hardcodes RedisStateStore. Suggested: move `StateStores.redisOrFallback` into starters, or use ServiceLoader with optional dep. Then either keep state-redis separate (cleaner) or merge it into server-core with lettuce optional. Best: keep module, remove core dependency.
- server-core -> render-html hard. It's used for SSR so can't avoid. But could be optional/degrade? The status says `HtmlRenderer.tryInstance()` already handles missing dylib. Still compile dependency on Java class. Keep.
- server-core -> view-core and render-html -> view-core: necessary.
- observability -> server-core: fine.
- test-kit -> view-core: fine, but only 2 files; could be merged into server-core as test-jar, but the status explains they intentionally keep main-scope jar (test-jar broke Docker package build). Could still be a main-scope package inside server-core? That would pollute runtime. Keep.
- quarkus-kotlin (0 code) -> quarkus + view-kotlin + quarkus-kotlin. Keep because DSL-neutrality.
- quarkus-kotlin-deployment (0 code) -> quarkus-kotlin + quarkus-deployment + quarkus-kotlin-deployment. Deployment artifact is required by Quarkus; merging into quarkus-deployment would drag Kotlin deployment. Keep.
- demo-common -> view-core (DemoTheme uses View/Color? maybe) and assets. Used by all host demos. demo-views-kotlin re-exports? Could merge demo-common into demo-views-kotlin; then host demos get DemoTheme/DemoAssets transitively. All five host demos depend on demo-views-kotlin already. So safe.
- Could merge all demo modules into one? No, host runtime deps conflict; but could consolidate demos under a separate reactor.

Proposed plan variants:

Tier 1 (low risk, no published API change):
1. Merge `pathland-demo-common` into `pathland-demo-views-kotlin` (move DemoTheme, DemoAssets, resources, test; update 5 host poms; delete module + status). Removes 1 module.
2. Move the 7 demo modules out of the library reactor into `lib/java/demos` (separate parent), or gate them behind a `-Pdemos` profile. Benefits: library install/test only 12 modules, avoids demo/Quarkus/Spring/Kotlin all in the same build. Need to check if moving breaks; they use `mvn -pl pathland-qt-demo` etc. from lib/java. Could instead keep location but use profile. Hmm, moving directories would break docs/scripts. A profile exclusion keeps paths. But Maven profiles with modules are a bit awkward: you can define `<modules>` in profile and none in main. This is doable. Yet the parent still needs to be parent of demos. Let me propose profile-gating with keeping paths.
Actually perhaps better: keep demos in the reactor (they don't hurt much) but merge demo-common. The user's concern is "a lot of maven packages". Reducing from 19 to 18 barely helps. The bigger win is separating demos from libraries. But maybe they mean the library packages.

Tier 2 (architectural cleanup, no merge but better dependency graph):
3. Decouple `pathland-state-redis` from `pathland-server-core` (move StateStores into starters using an optional ServiceLoader, or have starters depend on state-redis explicitly). Published = 12 (19 - 7 demos). Demos: demo-common, demo-views-kotlin, gtk, qt, quarkus-demo, quarkus-kotlin-demo, spring-demo = 7.

Let me present the dependency graph cleanly.

## Maven module dependency walkthrough

**19 reactor modules** — 12 published library/extension artifacts + 7 non-published demo modules.

### Actual dependency graph

```
pathland-view-core                        (engine, protocol, signals, state, transport; Kotlin)
├── pathland-view-kotlin                  (authoring DSL)
├── pathland-render-html                  (JNA shim → Rust renderer)
│   └── pathland-server-core
│       ├── pathland-observability        (Micrometer/OTel adapters)
│       ├── pathland-spring-boot-starter  (server-core + observability + Spring)
│       └── pathland-quarkus              (server-core + observability + Quarkus)
│           ├── pathland-quarkus-deployment            (build-time)
│           └── pathland-quarkus-kotlin  (0 code: deps + descriptor)
│               └── pathland-quarkus-kotlin-deployment (build-time)
├── pathland-state-redis                  (Lettuce StateStore)
└── pathland-test-kit                     (WsSession / MultiSessionProbe)

pathland-demo-common (theme + 24 assets)
└── pathland-demo-views-kotlin (MusicPlayerView, AdView)
    ├── pathland-gtk-demo
    ├── pathland-qt-demo
    ├── pathland-quarkus-demo         (+ pathland-quarkus, demo-common)
    ├── pathland-quarkus-kotlin-demo  (+ pathland-quarkus-kotlin, view-kotlin)
    └── pathland-spring-boot-demo     (+ spring-boot-starter, demo-common)
```

### Findings / candidates

**Clear win (low risk, demos only, nothing published):**
- `pathland-demo-common` is a 3-file module (theme + assets) used by all 5 host demos, and every host demo already depends on `pathland-demo-views-kotlin`. Merging `demo-common` into `demo-views-kotlin` removes one module with zero API impact.
- Demos are half the reactor (7 of 19) and force Spring/Quarkus/Kotlin/JNA into every library build. They could be gated behind a `-Pdemos` profile (or a separate aggregator) so `mvn install` builds the 12 library modules only.

**Real dependency smell (not a merge, but worth fixing):**
- `pathland-server-core` has a **hard compile dependency on `pathland-state-redis`** (`server-core/StateStores.java:22`), so every Spring/Quarkus app transitively ships Lettuce even when it never uses Redis. Better: move `StateStores.redisOrFallback` into the starters (or discover `StateStoreProvider` via `ServiceLoader`) and let consumers opt into `pathland-state-redis`. Keep it a separate module.
- `server-core → render-html` is hard, but legitimate (SSR); it already degrades via `HtmlRenderer.tryInstance()`. Leave it.

**Not worth merging:**
- `view-core` + `view-kotlin`: both Kotlin, but the split preserves the DSL-neutral engine boundary; merging forces the DSL on engine-only consumers.
- `observability` → `server-core`: only saves one small artifact but drags Micrometer/OTel into the core dependency surface.
- `quarkus-kotlin` (no code) → `quarkus`: would force Kotlin onto Java-only hosts, breaking the DSL-neutral extension design.
- `quarkus-kotlin-deployment` → `quarkus-deployment`: would drag `quarkus-kotlin-deployment` into every Java Quarkus build; Quarkus' runtime/deployment artifact split is required anyway.
- `render-html` → `server-core`: loses the standalone HTML binding and adds the Rust build to the core artifact.
- `test-kit` → `view-core`/`server-core`: only 2 files, but its main-scope jar is deliberately separate (a test-jar broke the Docker package build).

**Minor duplication:** `RingEventReader` is essentially duplicated between `gtk-demo` and `qt-demo`; could live in the demo support module rather than be merged.

### Recommendation

Keep all 12 published artifacts as-is (they encode meaningful boundaries), and do two things:
1. Merge `pathland-demo-common` into `pathland-demo-views-kotlin`.
2. Decouple `server-core` from `state-redis` (optional/ServiceLoader), and gate demos out of the default library build.

         xsi:schemaLocation="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0 https://maven.apache.org/xsd/maven-4.0.0.xsd">
    <modelVersion>4.0.0</modelVersion>

    <parent>
        <groupId>dev.pathland</groupId>
        <artifactId>pathland-parent</artifactId>
        <version>0.1.5</version>
    </parent>

    <artifactId>pathland-quarkus-deployment</artifactId>
    <packaging>jar</packaging>

    <name>Pathland Quarkus - Deployment</name>
    <description>
        Build-time deployment module for the DSL-neutral Pathland Quarkus extension.
    </description>

    <dependencies>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>dev.pathland</groupId>
            <artifactId>pathland-quarkus</artifactId>
            <version>${project.version}</version>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>io.quarkus</groupId>
            <artifactId>quarkus-core-deployment</artifactId>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>io.quarkus</groupId>
            <artifactId>quarkus-arc-deployment</artifactId>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>io.quarkus</groupId>
            <artifactId>quarkus-rest-deployment</artifactId>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>io.quarkus</groupId>
            <artifactId>quarkus-websockets-next-deployment</artifactId>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>io.quarkus</groupId>
            <artifactId>quarkus-micrometer-deployment</artifactId>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>io.quarkus</groupId>
            <artifactId>quarkus-smallrye-health-deployment</artifactId>
        </dependency>
    </dependencies>

    <build>
        <plugins>
            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                <artifactId>maven-compiler-plugin</artifactId>
                <configuration>
                    <annotationProcessorPaths>
                        <path>
                            <groupId>io.quarkus</groupId>
                            <artifactId>quarkus-extension-processor</artifactId>
                            <version>${quarkus.version}</version>
                        </path>
                    </annotationProcessorPaths>
                </configuration>
            </plugin>
        </plugins>
    </build>
</project>

parts.text:
Now I have enough. Let me formulate the plan. Since the user clarified POC, I'll propose an aggressive-but-sound target.

Proposed target: 19 → 10 modules (7 libs + 3 demos) or 11.

Library modules (published):
1. `pathland-view` = view-core + view-kotlin (engine + DSL)
2. `pathland-render-html` (keep; distinct native binding)
3. `pathland-server-core` = server-core + state-redis + observability (runtime + adapters)
4. `pathland-test-kit`? Could merge into server-core. Let's evaluate: it has no third-party deps, used only by starter tests. If merged into server-core main scope, it adds `dev.pathland.server.test` classes to runtime jar. For a POC that's acceptable but not ideal. Alternative: move into a separate `src/test` + configure `maven-jar-plugin` test-jar; but the Docker skip issue. Could just keep as module. Hmm. Let me consider merging test-kit into `pathland-server-core` as main scope and accept the pollution, or keep. I think for "less Maven packages" reducing by one is nice, and the classes are small. But the AGENTS note says the harness lives in main scope specifically so `mvn package -Dmaven.test.skip=true` resolves it as a normal jar. That means they already accepted main-scope test utilities in a separate artifact. Folding into server-core main means the same pollution but one less artifact. Fine. But then `pathland-test-kit` disappears and starters depend on server-core in test scope for the harness (already have it compile). That works. I'll propose merge test-kit into server-core under `dev.pathland.server.test`, marking it as test-support. Alternatively keep as a separate module. I'll present as optional.

5. `pathland-spring-boot-starter` (keep, depends on server-core)
6. `pathland-quarkus` = quarkus + quarkus-kotlin (runtime)
7. `pathland-quarkus-deployment` = quarkus-deployment + quarkus-kotlin-deployment (build-time)

That's 7 library modules (or 6 without render-html? no, keep; or 8 with test-kit).

Demos:
8. `pathland-demo` = demo-common + demo-views-kotlin
9. `pathland-desktop-demo` = gtk-demo + qt-demo (or keep 2)
10. `pathland-quarkus-demo` (keep; drop the separate kotlin demo or merge both into one)
11. `pathland-spring-boot-demo` (keep)

Could drop `pathland-quarkus-kotlin-demo` because quarkus demo already mounts Kotlin views. But it demonstrates a pure-Kotlin Quarkus app. Since the whole stack is Kotlin-only now, the Java-host demo proves interop; the Kotlin demo is redundant for a POC. I'd propose merging the two Quarkus demos into one (keeping the Kotlin-only app plus a Java CDI bean? Two root apps can coexist via MountedApp!). That's actually elegant: one Quarkus demo module with both a Java CDI `PathlandApp` and a Kotlin-only app mounted at `/kotlin`. Then one module. But the two demos have different dependencies; pathland-quarkus after merge includes Kotlin, so both fit.

Similarly desktop demos: one module with both GtkHost and QtHost, two exec profiles (already exec plugin). Fine.

So final demo modules: `pathland-demo` (assets+views), `pathland-desktop-demo`, `pathland-quarkus-demo`, `pathland-spring-boot-demo` = 4. Could gate under a `demos` profile.

Total 7 + 4 = 11 (from 19). That's a solid reduction.

But wait: merging `state-redis` and `observability` into `server-core` makes server-core's dependency surface include Lettuce + Micrometer + OTel (optional). Since POC, acceptable. Alternatively, keep them and just decouple; but the user wants combining. I'll recommend merging with optional deps where possible.

Package strategy: preserve existing package names to minimize churn:
- `dev.pathland.view.core.*`, `dev.pathland.view.engine.*` (view-core) + `dev.pathland.view.dsl.*` (view-kotlin) all in one jar. No package collision.
- `dev.pathland.server.*`, `dev.pathland.state.redis.*`, `dev.pathland.observability.*`, `dev.pathland.server.test.*` in server-core. No collision. Optionally later rename; keep as-is to minimize churn.
- Quarkus: `dev.pathland.quarkus.*` + `dev.pathland.quarkus.kotlin.*`? Currently quarkus-kotlin has no classes; only resources. So just merge pom deps + descriptor. No package issue.
- Demos: `dev.pathland.demo.*` all already; merging demo-common + demo-views has packages `dev.pathland.demo` (DemoTheme) and `dev.pathland.demo.assets`, and views under `dev.pathland.demo.music`/`ad`. No collision.
- Desktop demos gtk package `dev.pathland.demo.gtk`, qt `dev.pathland.demo.qt`; both can coexist in one module. RingEventReader would collide only if same package; they're different packages, but duplicate logic—could unify.
- Quarkus demos: packages `dev.pathland.demo.quarkus` and `dev.pathland.demo.quarkus.kotlin`; can coexist. But two `application.properties` and two test resources conflict. Merging requires resolving config; perhaps keep separate to avoid. Hmm. The Java Quarkus demo uses `application.properties` for proxy/ad; the Kotlin one has its own. Merging is possible with one application.properties plus mounted apps, but more work. Could drop the Kotlin demo instead. Since the stack is now Kotlin-only, the "Java host" demo is the valuable one. I'd propose deleting `pathland-quarkus-kotlin-demo` (or converting its view into a second mounted app in the Java demo). This reduces 1 module with little loss.

But AGENTS mentions the Kotlin-only Quarkus demo prominently. Deleting might be undesired. I'll present as a choice.

Also should we merge `pathland-render-html` into `pathland-server-core`? The render-html Java shim is only used by server-core and starters (for CSS/icons). Could merge, reducing 1. But it's a meaningful standalone binding. For a POC and fewer packages, maybe merge. However, the native build/embed logic (antrun) would move into server-core, making server-core build require Rust for all; it already transitively requires render-html at runtime anyway. Actually server-core depends on render-html, so building server-core alone via reactor requires render-html built; Maven resolves from ~/.m2. If merged, `mvn test -pl pathland-server-core` would run the antrun and fail without the Rust dylib (fail loudly). That could hurt dev ergonomics. Keeping render-html separate preserves the "build the Rust first" boundary. I'd recommend keeping render-html separate.

Similarly view-core merging view-kotlin: no external native build difference; straightforward. But note view-core has `src/main/java` source dir (empty). Fine.

What about `pathland-quarkus` vs `pathland-quarkus-kotlin`: merging is safe. The only reason to keep separate is DSL-neutrality. Since Kotlin is now the only DSL, and Java hosts still consume Kotlin, I'd merge. Also removes the empty module. Good.

Now the plan should include verification steps:
- Update root `pom.xml` modules.
- Move source trees and resources.
- Merge poms.
- Update internal artifact references and imports (packages unchanged so mostly poms).
- Update status.md files: merge/dedupe, delete removed ones, update AGENTS.md module list and paths, root README, scripts that reference modules (run-java-qt-demo.sh etc.), CI workflows, Dockerfiles.
- Run `mvn -q clean install` (with Rust built first), `cargo test` unaffected. Maybe `npm` no.
- Grep for module artifact IDs across repo (docs, scripts, CI, Dockerfiles, Kubernetes).

Let me search for references to module names across the repo to scope the migration.

Given nothing is published, I'd consolidate more aggressively. Here's the target I recommend.

## Target module graph (19 → 10)

**Before**
```
view-core ← view-kotlin            (both Kotlin, DSL depends on engine)
view-core ← state-redis ─┐
view-core ← render-html ─┼→ server-core ← observability
view-core ← test-kit ────┘

                                ├ quarkus-deployment ← quarkus-kotlin-deployment (0 code)
demo-common ← demo-views-kotlin ← {gtk, qt, quarkus, spring, quarkus-kotlin} demos
```

**After (6 published + 4 demo)**
```
pathland-view-core       = view-core + view-kotlin (engine + sole Kotlin DSL)
pathland-render-html     = unchanged (standalone JNA binding)
pathland-server-core     = server-core + state-redis + observability + test-kit
pathland-spring-boot-starter
pathland-quarkus         = quarkus + quarkus-kotlin (runtime)
pathland-quarkus-deployment = quarkus-deployment + quarkus-kotlin-deployment

pathland-demo-views-kotlin (or pathland-demo) = demo-common + demo-views-kotlin
pathland-desktop-demo    = gtk-demo + qt-demo
pathland-quarkus-demo    = keep (optionally absorb the Kotlin demo)
pathland-spring-boot-demo = keep
```

## Merge details

**1. `view-kotlin` → `view-core`**
Both are already Kotlin; packages (`dev.pathland.view.core.*` / `.engine.*` / `.dsl.*`) don't collide. Keep the surviving artifactId `pathland-view-core` — do **not** rename to `pathland-view`, because the root enforcer explicitly bans `dev.pathland:pathland-view` (old Java DSL, `pom.xml:120`). Move sources/tests, merge the Kotlin plugin + surefire config, drop the self-dependency.

**2. `state-redis` + `observability` + `test-kit` → `server-core`**
- `StateStores.java:22` already hard-references `RedisStateStore`, so Lettuce is currently a mandatory transitive dep. Merging makes that explicit and removes the odd edge rather than pretending it's optional.
- Observability is 2 files over `server-core`'s `PathlandTelemetry`; keep Micrometer compile and OTel optional.
- `test-kit` is 2 main-scope files; folding it into `dev.pathland.server.test` removes the artifact while preserving the "main jar so `-Dmaven.test.skip=true` resolves it" property. (Tradeoff: test utilities ship in the runtime jar. Keeping it separate is the one defensible holdout.)

**3. `quarkus-kotlin` → `quarkus`, `quarkus-kotlin-deployment` → `quarkus-deployment`**
- `quarkus-kotlin` has zero sources — only `pathland-view-kotlin` + `quarkus-kotlin` deps and a descriptor. Add both deps to `pathland-quarkus`, and list both capabilities (`dev.pathland.quarkus`, `dev.pathland.quarkus.kotlin`).
- Merge `PathlandKotlinProcessor`'s `FeatureBuildItem("pathland-kotlin")` into `PathlandProcessor`, add `quarkus-kotlin-deployment` to the deployment pom, delete both Kotlin modules.
- Caveat: this makes every Quarkus user pull `quarkus-kotlin`. Fine now that Kotlin is the only JVM DSL; if Java-only hosts matter later, re-split.

**4. Demos**
- `demo-common` → `demo-views-kotlin`: all 5 host demos already depend on the views module, so `DemoTheme`/`DemoAssets` become transitive. Delete `demo-common` + its `status.md`.
- `gtk-demo` + `qt-demo` → `pathland-desktop-demo`: both are JNA hosts over the same views; keep two packages and dedupe the duplicated `RingEventReader` (gtk Java 116 lines vs qt Kotlin 101 lines). Use exec profiles for each renderer.
- `quarkus-kotlin-demo`: likely redundant now — the Java Quarkus demo already mounts Kotlin views. Either delete it or convert `KotlinDemoView` into a `/kotlin` mounted app inside `pathland-quarkus-demo`. This is the only genuinely debatable deletion.

**Do not merge**
- `render-html` into `server-core`: its antrun native-dylib embed step is a distinct build boundary; merging makes `server-core` fail without a Rust build.
- Spring and Quarkus modules: framework glue.
- Quarkus runtime and deployment must remain separate artifact pairs by Quarkus convention.

## Migration checklist

1. Move source trees/resources, merge poms, update root `<modules>`.
2. Update every internal dependency coordinate (`render-html`, `server-core`, starters, demos).
3. Update build tooling: `scripts/lib.sh`, `scripts/run-java-{gtk,qt}-demo.sh`, `run-quarkus*.sh`, `run-spring-demo.sh`, `lib/typescript/scripts/copy-to-demos.mjs`, `pathland-quarkus-demo/Dockerfile`.
4. Update CI/release: `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `release.yml` module lists and demo exclusions.
5. Update docs/status per the AGENTS mandate: `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `RELEASING.md`, `SECURITY.md`, `docs/*`, and merge/delete the affected `status.md` files.
6. Verify: `cargo build -p pathland-render-html`, then `cd lib/java && mvn clean install`; targeted starter tests (`pathland-quarkus`, `pathland-spring-boot-starter`); package each demo; `git grep` for stale artifact IDs.

Safe order: demos first (unpublished), then `server-core` adapters, then `view-core`, then Quarkus.
