@@ -0,0 +1,85 @@
+package dev.pathland.demo.qt
+
+import com.sun.jna.Callback
+import com.sun.jna.Library
+import com.sun.jna.Native
+import com.sun.jna.Pointer
+import java.io.File
+import java.util.Locale
+
+/**
+ * JNA binding to the Rust Qt renderer cdylib (`libpathland_qt`).
+ *
+ * The Kotlin DSL emits opcodes into a `libpathland_core` ring
+ * ([dev.pathland.view.core.ffm.RingOpcodeSink]); [runRing] hands that borrowed
+ * ring to the in-process Qt Quick renderer (`pathland_qt_run_ring`), which pumps
+ * it in place. Native inputs are reported back through a no-payload callback;
+ * the host drains them from the ring itself.
+ */
+class QtRendererNative private constructor() {
+
+    /** Invoked (with no payload) on the Qt main thread after a raw input was written. */
+    fun interface EventCallback : Callback {
+        fun invoke()
+    }
+
+    /** The C ABI surface, mapped by JNA onto the Rust cdylib. */
+    interface NativeQtRenderer : Library {
+        fun pathland_qt_set_asset_root(dir: String)
+        fun pathland_qt_run_ring(ring: Pointer, onEvent: EventCallback?, width: Int, height: Int)
+    }
+
+    private val nativeQt: NativeQtRenderer
+
+    init {
+        val libraryPath = resolveLibraryPath()
+            ?: throw IllegalStateException(
+                "libpathland_qt not found; set -Dpathland.qt.lib to its full path " +
+                    "(cargo build -p pathland-render-qt)",
+            )
+        nativeQt = Native.load(libraryPath, NativeQtRenderer::class.java)
+    }
+
+    /**
+     * Set the directory that web-style `/_pathland/...` media/image source paths
+     * resolve against. Call before [runRing]; an empty value clears it.
+     */
+    fun setAssetRoot(dir: String) {
+        nativeQt.pathland_qt_set_asset_root(dir)
+    }
+
+    /**
+     * Run the Qt renderer over the borrowed ring. Blocks until the Qt event loop
+     * exits. On macOS the JVM must run with `-XstartOnFirstThread`.
+     */
+    fun runRing(ring: Pointer, onEvent: EventCallback?, width: Int, height: Int) {
+        nativeQt.pathland_qt_run_ring(ring, onEvent, width, height)
+    }
+
+    companion object {
+        private val INSTANCE: QtRendererNative by lazy { QtRendererNative() }
+
+        /** The process-wide binding; lazily links `libpathland_qt` on first call. */
+        fun instance(): QtRendererNative = INSTANCE
+
+        /** Resolve the native library's full path (system property, then `java.library.path`). */
+        internal fun resolveLibraryPath(): String? {
+            val override = System.getProperty("pathland.qt.lib")
+            if (override != null) return override
+            val fileName = "libpathland_qt" + platformLibraryExtension()
+            val libraryPath = System.getProperty("java.library.path") ?: return null
+            for (dir in libraryPath.split(File.pathSeparator)) {
+                val candidate = File(dir, fileName)
+                if (candidate.isFile) return candidate.absolutePath
+            }
+            return null
+        }
+
+        private fun platformLibraryExtension(): String {
+            val os = System.getProperty("os.name", "").lowercase(Locale.ROOT)
+            if (os.contains("mac")) return ".dylib"
+            if (os.contains("win")) return ".dll"
+            return ".so"
+        }
+    }
+}

+# pathland-desktop-demo — implementation status
+
+**Last updated:** November 5, 2026
+
+Runs the shared Kotlin `MusicPlayerView` (`dev.pathland.demo.music` from
+`pathland-demo-views-kotlin`) under the **native GTK4 renderer**
+(`libpathland_gtk`, `dev.pathland.demo.gtk.GtkHost`) or the **Qt Quick renderer**
+(`libpathland_qt`, `dev.pathland.demo.qt.QtHost`) — the cross-language,
+shared-renderer story. Protocol contract: `spec/`.
+
+## How it works
+
+- The Kotlin DSL mounts the view through its fine-grained `Emitter` into a
+  `libpathland_core` shared ring (`RingOpcodeSink`, **zero-copy**).
+- The in-process renderer pumps the same ring in place
+  (`pathland_gtk_run_ring` / `pathland_qt_run_ring`); no
+  `pathland-view-native` host is involved.
+- Native inputs round-trip as `EVENT` opcodes that the host drains
+  (`pathland_core_drain_events`) and dispatches into the app's bindings via the
+  shared `InputDispatcher` (taps, text/value/date inputs, **media events**,
+  router back).
+- State/theme/platform seeding mirrors the server session: `PersistentState`
+  over an `InMemoryStateStore`, `DemoTheme.adaptive()` as the emitter theme.
+- **App-driven media**: the renderer plays the demo's tracks and reports
+  `MEDIA_*` events back through the ring. The app's web-style
+  `/_pathland/assets/...` paths resolve against a local asset root: the demo
+  extracts its audio + covers from the shared `pathland-demo-views-kotlin` jar
+  at startup (`DemoAssets.extractToTemp`) and calls the renderer's
+  `set_asset_root`.
+
+## Implemented
+
+- **`GtkRendererNative`** — JNA binding to `libpathland_gtk`
+  (`pathland_gtk_run_ring` + `pathland_gtk_set_asset_root`); library resolved
+  from `pathland.gtk.lib` or `java.library.path`.
+- **`QtRendererNative`** — JNA binding to `libpathland_qt`
+  (`pathland_qt_run_ring` + `pathland_qt_set_asset_root`); library resolved
+  from `pathland.qt.lib` or `java.library.path`.
+- **`RingEventReader`** (shared, `dev.pathland.demo.desktop`) — decodes raw ring
+  `EVENT` opcodes into `dev.pathland.view.core.transport.Event`, resolving
+  `TEXT_CHANGED`/`NAVIGATE` strings from the shared host → guest event arena
+  (header `0x40`), plus `MEDIA_*` and `FIT_CHANGED` (routed to the emitter's fit
+  sink, so the `SizeThatFits` slot swaps to its wide candidate).
+- **`GtkHost`** (`main`) — Java host; mounts the Apple Music-style player,
+  extracts the demo assets, runs GTK (1180×800), drains and dispatches events.
+- **`QtHost`** (`main`) — Kotlin host; mounts the player, extracts the demo
+  assets, runs Qt Quick, drains and dispatches events.
+- The `Emitter` sets `BINDING_ID` on bound controls for `RingOpcodeSink`s (the
+  GTK renderer gates `TEXT_CHANGED`/`VALUE_CHANGED` on it).
+
+## Not implemented / gaps
+
+- **GTK playback requires GStreamer** with the mp3 decoding plugins installed;
+  without it the app runs but the pipeline errors on play.
+- The GTK renderer's `attach_control_events` covers `TOGGLE`/`SLIDER`/
+  `TEXT_FIELD`/`PICKER` only: `DATE_PICKER`, `STEPPER`, `COLOR_PICKER`, and
+  `TEXT_EDITOR` render but do not (yet) emit events under GTK.
+- Qt6 dev libraries are required to build/run the Qt renderer.
+- macOS requires `-XstartOnFirstThread` for both hosts.
+- No automated GUI test (headless renderer tests live in the Rust crates).
+
+## Verified by
+
+`mvn test -pl pathland-desktop-demo` — `RingEventReaderTest` (headless, no GTK/Qt;
+pointer/value/date/text/navigate/media/fit decoding and bounds behaviour).
+Manual: `scripts/run-java-gtk-demo.sh` and `scripts/run-java-qt-demo.sh`.

@@ -1,44 +0,0 @@
-# pathland-observability — implementation status
-
-**Last updated:** October 3, 2026
-
-Observability adapters for the framework-agnostic `pathland-server-core`
-telemetry seam. The core emits lifecycle/throughput events through
-`PathlandTelemetry` (default `NOOP`); this module turns them into metrics and
-spans. Protocol/contract context: `spec/OPCODE.md`; the seam itself is in
-`pathland-server-core`.
-
-## Implemented
-
-- **`MicrometerTelemetry`** — a `PathlandTelemetry` over any Micrometer
-  `MeterRegistry` (Prometheus, OTLP, …). Metric catalog:
-  - `pathland.sessions.active` — gauge (pull-based, bound by the host)
-  - `pathland.sessions.opened` / `pathland.sessions.closed` — counters
-  - `pathland.events.received` — counter (decoded inbound events)
-  - `pathland.batches.sent` / `pathland.frames.sent` / `pathland.bytes.sent` — counters
-  - `pathland.batch.size` — distribution summary (opcodes per batch)
-  - `pathland.batch.flush` — timer (merge + encode)
-  - `pathland.ssr.render` — timer (SSR render round-trip)
-  - `pathland.resync.requested` — counter
-  - `pathland.ws.failures` — counter
-  - Every meter is tagged by `mount` (bounded). Registrations are idempotent, so
-    a builder per event is cheap and cannot leak meters.
-- **`TracingTelemetry`** — an OpenTelemetry decorator over another
-  `PathlandTelemetry`: emits a span per frame send (`pathland.frame.send`), per
-  inbound event batch (`pathland.event.batch`), and per SSR render
-  (`pathland.ssr.render`), with the wrapped telemetry still receiving every
-  event. Spans are back-dated by the measured duration so they render with the
-  real latency. Opt-in — the starters build it only when a `Tracer`/`OpenTelemetry`
-  bean is available.
-
-## Not implemented / gaps
-
-- No client-side (browser) telemetry — server-side only.
-- `ws.failures` does not tag the failure reason (unbounded cardinality).
-
-## Verified by
-
-`mvn test -pl pathland-observability` — `MicrometerTelemetryTest` (the full
-metric catalog + per-mount tagging) and `TracingTelemetryTest` (span names via an
-in-memory OTel exporter, plus delegation). The starters' tests assert the wiring
-end to end (`/q/health` + `/q/metrics`, `/actuator/health` + `pathland.*` meters).

-/**
- * Runs the shared Kotlin [MusicPlayerView] under the native Qt Quick renderer.
- *
- * The Kotlin DSL mounts the view through the fine-grained [Emitter] into a
- * `libpathland_core` shared ring ([RingOpcodeSink], zero-copy). The in-process
- * Qt renderer pumps the same ring in place (`pathland_qt_run_ring`); native
- * inputs round-trip as `EVENT` opcodes that this host drains and dispatches
- * through [InputDispatcher] into the app's bindings.
- *
- * No Swing, no Qt API — only Pathland authoring.
- */
-object QtHost {
-
-    /** Max events drained per wake (× 16 bytes each). */
-    private const val MAX_EVENTS = 64
-    private const val WINDOW_WIDTH = 1180
-    private const val WINDOW_HEIGHT = 800
-
-    @JvmStatic
-    fun main(args: Array<String>) {
-        val core = PathlandCore.instance()
-        RingOpcodeSink(core).use { sink ->
-            val handle = sink.handle()
-
-            // The session's state + theme, exactly as the server session seeds them.
-            val state = PersistentState(InMemoryStateStore(), "desktop")
-            // A placeholder host path signal: MusicPlayerView has no router.
-            val activePath = Signals.signal("/")
-
-            val emitter = Emitter(sink, DemoTheme.adaptive())
-            val result = emitter.mount(MusicPlayerView.make(), Environment(state))
-            val dispatcher = InputDispatcher(result, activePath)
-            val reader = RingEventReader(core.ringPtr(handle), core.ringLen(handle))
-
-            // Wake callback: drain raw EVENT opcodes and route them into the app's
-            // bindings. Re-emission happens on the Qt main thread, the only writer.
-            val onEvent = QtRendererNative.EventCallback {
-                val buf = Memory(MAX_EVENTS.toLong() * 16)
-                val n = core.drainEvents(handle, buf, MAX_EVENTS)
-                if (n > 0) {
-                    dispatcher.dispatch(reader.decode(buf.getByteArray(0, n * 16)))
-                }
-            }
-
-            val renderer = QtRendererNative.instance()
-            renderer.setAssetRoot(DemoAssets.extractToTemp().toString())
-
-            // Blocks until the window closes; the ring (handle) must outlive it.
-            renderer.runRing(core.ringMut(handle), onEvent, WINDOW_WIDTH, WINDOW_HEIGHT)
-        }
-    }
-}

-/**
- * JNA binding to the Rust Qt renderer cdylib (`libpathland_qt`).
- *
- * The Kotlin DSL emits opcodes into a `libpathland_core` ring
- * ([dev.pathland.view.core.ffm.RingOpcodeSink]); [runRing] hands that borrowed
- * ring to the in-process Qt Quick renderer (`pathland_qt_run_ring`), which pumps
- * it in place. Native inputs are reported back through a no-payload callback;
- * the host drains them from the ring itself.
- */
-class QtRendererNative private constructor() {
-
-    /** Invoked (with no payload) on the Qt main thread after a raw input was written. */
-    fun interface EventCallback : Callback {
-        fun invoke()
-    }
-
-    /** The C ABI surface, mapped by JNA onto the Rust cdylib. */
-    interface NativeQtRenderer : Library {
-        fun pathland_qt_set_asset_root(dir: String)
-        fun pathland_qt_run_ring(ring: Pointer, onEvent: EventCallback?, width: Int, height: Int)
-    }
-
-    private val nativeQt: NativeQtRenderer
-
-    init {
-        val libraryPath = resolveLibraryPath()
-            ?: throw IllegalStateException(
-                "libpathland_qt not found; set -Dpathland.qt.lib to its full path " +
-                    "(cargo build -p pathland-render-qt)",
-            )
-        nativeQt = Native.load(libraryPath, NativeQtRenderer::class.java)
-    }
-
-    /**
-     * Set the directory that web-style `/_pathland/...` media/image source paths
-     * resolve against. Call before [runRing]; an empty value clears it.
-     */
-    fun setAssetRoot(dir: String) {
-        nativeQt.pathland_qt_set_asset_root(dir)
-    }
-
-    /**
-     * Run the Qt renderer over the borrowed ring. Blocks until the Qt event loop
-     * exits. On macOS the JVM must run with `-XstartOnFirstThread`.
-     */
-    fun runRing(ring: Pointer, onEvent: EventCallback?, width: Int, height: Int) {
-        nativeQt.pathland_qt_run_ring(ring, onEvent, width, height)
-    }
-
-    companion object {
-        private val INSTANCE: QtRendererNative by lazy { QtRendererNative() }
-
-        /** The process-wide binding; lazily links `libpathland_qt` on first call. */
-        fun instance(): QtRendererNative = INSTANCE
-
-        /** Resolve the native library's full path (system property, then `java.library.path`). */
-        internal fun resolveLibraryPath(): String? {
-            val override = System.getProperty("pathland.qt.lib")
-            if (override != null) return override
-            val fileName = "libpathland_qt" + platformLibraryExtension()
-            val libraryPath = System.getProperty("java.library.path") ?: return null
-            for (dir in libraryPath.split(File.pathSeparator)) {
-                val candidate = File(dir, fileName)
-                if (candidate.isFile) return candidate.absolutePath
-            }
-            return null
-        }

-            val os = System.getProperty("os.name", "").lowercase(Locale.ROOT)
-            if (os.contains("mac")) return ".dylib"
-            if (os.contains("win")) return ".dll"
-            return ".so"
-        }
-    }
-}

-/**
- * Decodes raw `EVENT`-category opcodes drained from the shared ring into
- * [Event] objects, resolving strings from the shared host → guest event arena.
- */
-class RingEventReader(
-    private val ringPtr: Pointer?,
-    private val ringLen: Long,
-) {
-
-    private val eventArenaOffset: Int =
-        if (ringPtr != null && ringLen >= OFF_EVENT_ARENA_OFFSET + 4L) {
-            ringPtr.getInt(OFF_EVENT_ARENA_OFFSET.toLong())
-        } else {
-            0
-        }
-
-    /** Decode consecutive 16-byte opcodes from [raw] (a drain buffer). */
-    fun decode(raw: ByteArray): List<Event> {
-        val events = ArrayList<Event>()
-        var off = 0
-        while (off + OPCODE_SIZE <= raw.size) {
-            if ((raw[off].toInt() and 0xFF) != CATEGORY_EVENT) {
-                off += OPCODE_SIZE
-                continue
-            }
-            val command = raw[off + 1].toInt() and 0xFF
-            val flags = u16(raw, off + 2)
-            val a = i32(raw, off + 4)
-            val b = i32(raw, off + 8)
-            val c = i32(raw, off + 12)
-            decodeOne(command, flags, a, b, c)?.let(events::add)
-            off += OPCODE_SIZE
-        }
-        return events
-    }
-
-    private fun decodeOne(command: Int, flags: Int, a: Int, b: Int, c: Int): Event? =
-        when (command) {
-            Commands.Event.POINTER_DOWN -> Event.pointerDown(a, f32(b), f32(c))
-            Commands.Event.POINTER_UP -> Event.pointerUp(a, f32(b), f32(c))
-            Commands.Event.POINTER_MOVE -> Event.pointerMove(a, f32(b), f32(c), flags)
-            Commands.Event.KEY_DOWN -> Event.keyDown(a, b, c, flags)
-            Commands.Event.KEY_UP -> Event.keyUp(a, b, c)
-            Commands.Event.VALUE_CHANGED -> Event.valueChanged(a, f32(b))
-            Commands.Event.TEXT_CHANGED -> Event.textChanged(a, arenaString(b))
-            Commands.Event.FOCUS_CHANGED -> Event.focusChanged(a, b != 0)
-            Commands.Event.EDITING_CHANGED -> Event.editingChanged(a, b != 0)
-            Commands.Event.SUBMIT -> Event.submit(a)
-            Commands.Event.SCROLL -> Event.scroll(a, f32(b), f32(c))
-            Commands.Event.WHEEL -> Event.wheel(a, f32(b), f32(c))
-            Commands.Event.DATE_CHANGED -> Event.dateChanged(a, b, c)
-            Commands.Event.MEDIA_PLAY_STATE_CHANGED -> Event.mediaPlayStateChanged(a, b != 0)
-            Commands.Event.MEDIA_TIME_UPDATED -> Event.mediaTimeUpdated(a, f32(b))
-            Commands.Event.MEDIA_ENDED -> Event.mediaEnded(a)
-            Commands.Event.MEDIA_VOLUME_CHANGED -> Event.mediaVolumeChanged(a, f32(b))
-            Commands.Event.MEDIA_DURATION_CHANGED -> Event.mediaDurationChanged(a, f32(b))
-            Commands.Event.FIT_CHANGED -> Event.fitChanged(a, f32(b))
-            Commands.Event.NAVIGATE ->
-                if ((flags and Commands.Flags.NAVIGATE_URL) != 0) {
-                    Event.navigate(arenaString(b))
-                } else {
-                    Event.navigateBack()
-                }
-            else -> null
-        }
-
-    /** Resolve a string from the shared event arena at [ref] (`[u32 len][bytes]`). */
-    private fun arenaString(ref: Int): String? {
-        if (ref < 0 || ringPtr == null || eventArenaOffset <= 0) return null
-        val base = eventArenaOffset.toLong() + ref
-        if (base + 4 > ringLen) return null
-        val len = ringPtr.getInt(base)
-        if (len < 0 || base + 4 + len > ringLen) return null
-        val bytes = ringPtr.getByteArray(base + 4, len)
-        return String(bytes, StandardCharsets.UTF_8)
-    }
-
-    private companion object {
-        const val OPCODE_SIZE = 16
-        const val CATEGORY_EVENT = 0x03
-        const val OFF_EVENT_ARENA_OFFSET = 0x40
-
-        fun u16(raw: ByteArray, off: Int): Int =
-            (raw[off].toInt() and 0xFF) or ((raw[off + 1].toInt() and 0xFF) shl 8)
-
-        fun i32(raw: ByteArray, off: Int): Int =
-            (raw[off].toInt() and 0xFF) or
-                ((raw[off + 1].toInt() and 0xFF) shl 8) or
-                ((raw[off + 2].toInt() and 0xFF) shl 16) or
-                ((raw[off + 3].toInt() and 0xFF) shl 24)
-
-        fun f32(bits: Int): Float = java.lang.Float.intBitsToFloat(bits)
-    }
-}

-# pathland-qt-demo — implementation status
-
-**Last updated:** November 3, 2026
-
-Fully Kotlin JNA desktop demo: the shared Kotlin `MusicPlayerView` under the native
-Qt Quick renderer (`libpathland_qt`), over the `libpathland_core` shared ring.
-
-## Implemented
-
-- **`QtHost`** — mounts the Kotlin music player through the emitter into the shared
-  ring, seeds per-session state/theme, extracts the shared demo assets, and runs
-  `pathland_qt_run_ring`; blocks until the window closes.
-- **`QtRendererNative`** — JNA binding for `pathland_qt_run_ring` +
-  `pathland_qt_set_asset_root`; resolves `pathland.qt.lib` or `java.library.path`.
-- **`RingEventReader`** — decodes raw ring `EVENT` opcodes, event-arena strings,
-  media events, and `FIT_CHANGED`.
-- **Fully Kotlin host** — no Java DSL, no Swing/Qt API in app code.
-
-## Not implemented / gaps
-
-- Qt6 dev libraries are required to build/run the renderer.
-- macOS needs `-XstartOnFirstThread`.
-- No automated GUI test; the headless `RingEventReaderTest` covers decoding.
-
-## Verified by
-
-`mvn test -pl pathland-qt-demo` — `RingEventReaderTest` (5 tests). Manual:
-`scripts/run-java-qt-demo.sh`.

+package dev.pathland.demo.quarkus.kotlin
+
+import dev.pathland.view.core.FontWeight
+import dev.pathland.view.core.View
+import dev.pathland.view.dsl.Button
+import dev.pathland.view.dsl.ForEach
+import dev.pathland.view.dsl.HStack
+import dev.pathland.view.dsl.Component
+import dev.pathland.view.dsl.Text
+import dev.pathland.view.dsl.TextField
+import dev.pathland.view.dsl.VStack
+import dev.pathland.view.dsl.computed
+import dev.pathland.view.dsl.fontSize
+import dev.pathland.view.dsl.fontWeight
+import dev.pathland.view.dsl.frame
+import dev.pathland.view.dsl.padding
+
+/**
+ * A small Kotlin-owned view that exercises persisted state, two-way text input,
+ * reactive plain-Kotlin control flow, `ForEach`, and the Kotlin modifier sugar.
+ */
+class KotlinDemoView : Component() {
+
+    private var count by state(0)
+    private val name = mutableState("", "demo.name")
+    private var items by state(listOf("First item", "Second item"))
+
+    override fun body(): View = VStack(spacing = 16f) {
+        Text("Pathland Kotlin Demo")
+            .fontSize(28f)
+            .fontWeight(FontWeight.BOLD)
+        Text("SSR plus live 16-byte opcode deltas, authored in Kotlin.")
+
+        HStack(spacing = 12f) {
+            Text("Count: $count")
+            Button("Increment") { count += 1 }
+            Button("Reset") { count = 0 }
+        }
+
+        TextField("Your name", name)
+        Text(computed { "Hello, ${name.value.ifBlank { "world" }}" })
+
+        HStack(spacing = 12f) {
+            Button("Add item") { items = items + "Item ${items.size + 1}" }
+            Button("Clear items") { items = emptyList() }
+        }
+
+        ForEach(items) { item, _ -> Text("• $item") }
+    }.padding(24).frame { maxWidth(720f) }
+}

-/**

- * WebSocket endpoint, sessions and state; this bean supplies a fresh Kotlin root.
- *

- * The player's Now Playing pane embeds the ad app via a `ProxyView`
- * (spec/PROXY.md) — a same-server proxy on a loopback WebSocket.

-@ApplicationScoped
-class KotlinDemoApplication : PathlandApp {
-

-    @field:ConfigProperty(name = "pathland.demo.ad-url", defaultValue = "http://localhost:8080/ad")
-    lateinit var adUrl: String
-
-    override fun newRoot(): View = MusicPlayerView.make(adUrl)
-
-    /** The origin app mounted at `/ad`: the small sponsored-proxy ad app. */
-    @Produces
-    @Singleton
-    fun adApp(): MountedApp = MountedApp.of("/ad", PathlandApp { AdView() })
-}

-# pathland-quarkus-kotlin — implementation status
-
-**Last updated:** November 1, 2026
-
-Quarkus extension for the Kotlin authoring DSL. It depends on the DSL-neutral
-`pathland-quarkus` extension, `pathland-view-kotlin`, and `quarkus-kotlin`.
-
-## Implemented
-
-- Runtime module `pathland-quarkus-kotlin` + deployment module
-  `pathland-quarkus-kotlin-deployment`.
-- Provides the `dev.pathland.quarkus.kotlin` capability.
-- No server/runtime logic of its own; SSR, WebSocket, sessions, state and assets
-  stay in `pathland-quarkus`.
-- **No Java DSL dependency**: the removed Java DSL/processor are not in the
-  dependency tree; Kotlin is the only authoring surface.
-
-## Build contract
-
-The extension can enable Quarkus Kotlin support, but it cannot add a Kotlin
-compiler plugin to an application. Kotlin apps must configure
-`kotlin-maven-plugin` (or the Gradle Kotlin plugin), including `all-open` for
-CDI/JAX-RS annotations. The Kotlin demo and (later) the codestart carry that
-configuration.
-
-## Not implemented / gaps
-
-- No Quarkus codestart yet.
-- Native image is not supported; the Rust HTML renderer is loaded through JNA.

+package dev.pathland.view.dsl
+
+import dev.pathland.view.core.ButtonStyle
+import dev.pathland.view.core.EmptyContent
+import dev.pathland.view.core.Environment
+import dev.pathland.view.core.View
+import dev.pathland.view.core.protocol.Commands

+import dev.pathland.view.core.signal.Signal
+import dev.pathland.view.engine.PathlandNode
+
+internal fun buttonView(
+    title: Signal<String>?,
+    action: (() -> Unit)?,
+    children: List<View>,
+): View = coreView(Components.BUTTON) { node, env ->
+    val label = children.firstOrNull() ?: title?.let { textView(it) }
+    val style = Environment.value(Environment.BUTTON_STYLE).get() ?: PlainButtonStyle
+    val content = style.makeBody(ButtonStyle.Configuration(label))
+    if (content != null && content !== EmptyContent.INSTANCE) {
+        node.children.add(content.render(env))
+    }
+    val mask = (node.properties[Properties.EVENT_LISTENERS] as? Int ?: 0) or
+        Commands.Listeners.POINTER_DOWN or Commands.Listeners.POINTER_UP
+    node.properties[Properties.EVENT_LISTENERS] = mask
+    if (action != null) node.tapActions.add(Runnable(action))
+}
+
+/** A button with a plain-text title. */
+fun Button(title: String, action: () -> Unit): View =
+    buttonView(dev.pathland.view.core.signal.Signals.constant(title), action, emptyList()).registerChild()
+
+/** A button whose title is bound to a signal. */
+fun Button(title: Signal<String>, action: () -> Unit): View =
+    buttonView(title, action, emptyList()).registerChild()
+
+/**
+ * A button with a custom label: `Button(action = { save() }) { Text("Save") }`.
+ * The action is a named argument because the trailing lambda is the label.
+ */
+fun Button(action: () -> Unit, content: () -> Unit): View {
+    val children = collectChildren(content)
+    return buttonView(null, action, children).registerChild()
+}
+
+/** A button with both a title and an explicit label subtree (the subtree wins). */
+fun Button(title: String, action: () -> Unit, content: () -> Unit): View {
+    val children = collectChildren(content)
+    return buttonView(dev.pathland.view.core.signal.Signals.constant(title), action, children).registerChild()
+}

+package dev.pathland.view.dsl
+
+import dev.pathland.view.core.Environment
+import dev.pathland.view.core.View
+import dev.pathland.view.engine.PathlandNode
+import dev.pathland.view.core.signal.Signal
+import dev.pathland.view.core.signal.Signals
+import dev.pathland.view.core.signal.WritableSignal
+import dev.pathland.view.core.state.PersistentState
+import java.util.function.UnaryOperator
+import kotlin.properties.ReadWriteProperty
+import kotlin.reflect.KProperty
+
+/**
+ * Base class for application-authored Kotlin views.
+ *
+ * A subclass declares its subtree in [body]; a signal read there re-renders only this
+ * component (the emitter tracks the slot). Persisted state is declared with
+ * [state] / [mutableState] and is bound to the session's [PersistentState] before the
+ * first body render — no annotation processor or kapt.
+ *
+ * Constructing a [Component] inside a builder block auto-registers it, so
+ * `VStack { CounterView() }` needs no `.children(...)`.
+ */
+abstract class Component : View {
+
+    private val stateSignals = mutableListOf<StateSignal<*>>()
+
+    init {
+        // Inline construction (`VStack { CounterView() }`) auto-registers. A view
+        // constructed as a field of another view must not leak into the enclosing
+        // builder scope; it is added explicitly with `+field` inside body().
+        if (!insideAnotherViewConstructor()) {
+            registerChild()
+        }
+    }
+
+    /**
+     * A persisted, two-way state signal keyed by the property name:
+     * `private var count by state(0)` or with an explicit store key
+     * `private var count by state(0, "counter")`.
+     */
+    protected fun <T : Any> state(initial: T, key: String? = null): StateDelegate<T> =
+        StateDelegate(mutableState(initial, key))
+
+    /**
+     * A persisted state signal for code that wants the signal directly:
+     * `val name = mutableState("")` can be passed to `TextField(text = name)`.
+     */
+    protected fun <T : Any> mutableState(initial: T, key: String? = null): StateSignal<T> {
+        val state = StateSignal(initial, key)
+        stateSignals.add(state)
+        return state
+    }
+
+    final override fun renderNode(env: Environment): PathlandNode {
+        val persistent = env.state()
+        return PersistentState.withCurrent(persistent) {
+            persistent?.let { state ->
+                stateSignals.forEach { it.bind(state) }
+            }
+            val resolved = body()
+            check(resolved !== this) {
+                "${javaClass.name} must return its subtree from body()"
+            }
+            resolved.renderNode(env)
+        }
+    }
+
+    abstract override fun body(): View
+
+    private fun insideAnotherViewConstructor(): Boolean {
+        val self = javaClass
+        return java.lang.StackWalker
+            .getInstance(java.lang.StackWalker.Option.RETAIN_CLASS_REFERENCE)
+            .walk { frames ->
+                frames.anyMatch { frame ->
+                    frame.methodName == "<init>" &&
+                        frame.declaringClass != self &&
+                        frame.declaringClass != Component::class.java &&
+                        Component::class.java.isAssignableFrom(frame.declaringClass)
+                }
+            }
+    }
+}
+
+/**
+ * A persisted state value. It behaves as a [WritableSignal] so it can be passed
+ * straight to two-way controls; binding to the session store happens before the
+ * owning view's [Component.body] runs.
+ */
+class StateSignal<T : Any> internal constructor(
+    initial: T,
+    var key: String? = null,
+) : WritableSignal<T> {
+
+    private var current: WritableSignal<T> = Signals.signal(initial)
+    private var bound = false
+
+    internal fun bind(persistent: PersistentState) {
+        if (bound) return
+        val storeKey = checkNotNull(key) { "State has no key (declare it with `by state(...)`) " }
+        current = persistent.signal(storeKey, current.get())
+        bound = true
+    }
+
+    override fun get(): T = current.get()
+
+    override fun set(value: T) = current.set(value)
+
+    override fun update(fn: UnaryOperator<T>) = current.update(fn)
+
+    override fun asReadonly(): Signal<T> = current.asReadonly()
+
+    /** The auto-saved persisted value (the signal itself is a [WritableSignal]). */
+    var value: T
+        get() = get()
+        set(value) = set(value)
+}
+
+/** Property-delegate form of [StateSignal]. */
+class StateDelegate<T : Any> internal constructor(
+    val signal: StateSignal<T>,
+) : ReadWriteProperty<Any?, T> {
+
+    operator fun provideDelegate(thisRef: Any?, property: KProperty<*>): StateDelegate<T> {
+        if (signal.key == null) {
+            signal.key = property.name
+        }
+        return this
+    }
+
+    override fun getValue(thisRef: Any?, property: KProperty<*>): T = signal.get()
+
+    override fun setValue(thisRef: Any?, property: KProperty<*>, value: T) = signal.set(value)
+}

+private class FitSlot(private val fits: List<FitCandidate>) : View {
+    private val fitIndex = Signals.signal(0)
+    private val fitReported = Signals.signal(false)
+
+    override fun renderNode(env: Environment): PathlandNode {
+        val node = PathlandNode(Components.SIZE_THAT_FITS)
+        node.properties[Properties.FIT_QUERY] = FloatArray(fits.size) { fits[it].minWidth }
+        val hint = Emitter.current()?.currentSlotOldFitSelection()
+        if (hint != null && hint != fitIndex.get()) {
+            Signals.untracked { fitIndex.set(hint); null }
+        }
+        val index = fitIndex.get().coerceIn(0, (fits.size - 1).coerceAtLeast(0))
+        node.fitSelection = index
+        node.fitReported = fitReported.get()
+        node.fitInput = Consumer { incoming ->
+            if (incoming != null && incoming in fits.indices) {
+                node.fitReported = true
+                node.fitSelection = incoming
+                fitIndex.set(incoming)
+                fitReported.set(true)
+            }
+        }
+        if (PathlandNode.SNAPSHOT_EMISSION.get() && !fitReported.get()) {
+            fits.forEach { node.children.add(it.view.render(env)) }
+        } else {

+/**
+ * A Kotlin-owned view over the shared engine's [PathlandNode]. This is the base
+ * for the Kotlin DSL's primitives and containers; it is independent of any
+ * authoring DSL.
+ */
+internal class CoreView(
+    private val component: Int,
+    private val children: List<View> = emptyList(),
+    private val configure: (PathlandNode, Environment) -> Unit = { _, _ -> },
+) : View {
+
+    override fun renderNode(env: Environment): PathlandNode {
+        val node = PathlandNode(component)
+        configure(node, env)
+        for (child in children) {
+            node.children.add(child.render(env))
+        }
+        return node
+    }
+}

+    component: Int,
+    children: List<View> = emptyList(),
+    configure: (PathlandNode, Environment) -> Unit = { _, _ -> },
+): View = CoreView(component, children, configure)
+
+/** A Group is a bare VStack container with no spacing/alignment. */
+internal fun groupView(children: List<View>): View =
+    coreView(dev.pathland.view.core.protocol.Components.VSTACK, children)

+    private val icon: Signal<String>?,
+    private val iconView: View?,
+) : View {
+
+    override fun renderNode(env: Environment): dev.pathland.view.engine.PathlandNode {
+        val style = Environment.value(Environment.LABEL_STYLE).get() ?: FallbackLabelStyle
+        val titleValue = title?.get()
+        val iconValue = icon?.get()
+        val titlePart = if (nonBlank(titleValue)) title?.let { textView(it).lineLimit(1) } else null
+        val iconPart = iconView ?: if (nonBlank(iconValue)) icon?.let { imageView(it) } else null

+        if (nonBlank(titleValue) && title != null) {

+        }
+        return content.renderNode(env)
+    }

+    LabelView(title, icon?.let { Signals.constant(it) }, null).registerChild()

+package dev.pathland.view.dsl

+
+/**
+ * Build a seeded router:
+ *
+ * ```
+ * val router = navigator("/") {
+ *     route("/", HomeView())
+ *     route("/users/:id") { params -> UserView(params.intValue("id")) }
+ *     fallback(NotFoundView())
+ * }
+ * ```
+ */
+fun navigator(initialPath: String = "/", routes: Navigation.Builder.() -> Unit): Router =
+    Navigation.navigator(initialPath).apply(routes).build()
+
+/** Build a router bound to the host-provided active-path signal (deep links/popstate). */
+fun navigator(activePath: Signal<String>, routes: Navigation.Builder.() -> Unit): Router =
+    Navigation.navigator().apply(routes).build(activePath)
+
+/** The navigation slot (SwiftUI `NavigationStack` shape). */
+fun NavigationStack(
+    router: Router,
+    chrome: Chrome = Chrome.PLATFORM_DEFAULT,
+): View = Navigation.container(router, chrome).registerChild()
+
+/** Alias of [NavigationStack] using the protocol's component name. */
+fun NavigationContainer(
+    router: Router,
+    chrome: Chrome = Chrome.PLATFORM_DEFAULT,
+): View = NavigationStack(router, chrome)
+
+/** A text-labelled navigation link. */
+fun NavigationLink(
+    label: String,
+    to: String,
+    router: Router? = null,
+): View = navigationLinkView(textView(label), to, router)
+
+private fun navigationLinkView(label: View, to: String, router: Router?): View {
+    val action = if (router == null) ({}) else ({ router.push(to) })
+    val button = buttonView(null, action, listOf(label))
+    return if (router == null) button.modifiers(NavigationIntent.push(to)).registerChild()
+    else button.registerChild()
+}
+
+/** A navigation link with a custom label subtree. */
+fun NavigationLink(
+    to: String,
+    router: Router? = null,
+    content: () -> Unit,
+): View {
+    val children = collectChildren(content)
+    val label = when (children.size) {
+        0 -> textView("")
+        1 -> children[0]
+        else -> groupView(children)
+    }
+    return navigationLinkView(label, to, router)
+}
+
+/** A reactive "is this the active route" signal. */
+fun isActive(router: Router, path: String): Signal<Boolean> = Navigation.isActive(router, path)
+
+/** Declare a route-change intent on any view; the emitter resolves the nearest router. */
+fun View.navigate(to: String): View = modifiers(NavigationIntent.navigate(to))
+
+/** Push onto the nearest router's back-stack. */
+fun View.push(to: String): View = modifiers(NavigationIntent.push(to))
+
+/** Replace the current route without touching the back-stack. */
+fun View.replace(to: String): View = modifiers(NavigationIntent.replace(to))

+/** A writable signal (Angular-style). */
+fun <T> signal(initial: T): WritableSignal<T> = Signals.signal(initial)
+
+/** A named writable signal (names surface in dependency errors). */
+fun <T> signal(name: String, initial: T): WritableSignal<T> = Signals.signal(name, initial)
+
+/** A writable signal with a custom equality comparator. */
+fun <T> signal(initial: T, equal: (T, T) -> Boolean): WritableSignal<T> =
+    Signals.signal(initial) { a, b -> equal(a, b) }
+
+/** A lazy, memoized derived signal. */
+fun <T> computed(block: () -> T): Signal<T> = Signals.computed { block() }
+
+/** An immutable signal carrying a static value. */
+fun <T> constant(value: T): Signal<T> = Signals.constant(value)
+
+/** Register an effect; runs immediately, then on tracked dependency changes. */
+fun effect(block: () -> Unit): EffectRef = Signals.effect { block() }
+
+/** Read signals without recording dependencies on the enclosing context. */
+fun <T> untracked(block: () -> T): T = Signals.untracked { block() }
+
+/** The current value (SwiftUI-shaped signal read). */
+val <T> Signal<T>.value: T
+    get() = get()
+
+/** A two-way signal value: `count.value = 1`, `count.value += 1`. */
+var <T> WritableSignal<T>.value: T
+    get() = get()
+    set(value) = set(value)
+
+/** Derive a read-only signal from this one. */
+fun <T, R> Signal<T>.map(transform: (T) -> R): Signal<R> =
+    Signals.computed { transform(get()) }
+
+/** A read-only view of a writable signal. */
+fun <T> WritableSignal<T>.readonly(): Signal<T> = asReadonly()

+package dev.pathland.view.dsl
+
+import dev.pathland.view.core.Environment
+import dev.pathland.view.core.signal.Signal

+import org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertArrayEquals
+import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test
+import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets
+import java.nio.file.Files
+import java.nio.file.Path
+
+/**
+ * Cross-language engine traces: the same scenarios are run through the Kotlin
+ * JVM emitter and compared byte-for-byte with the self-contained PLPL frames
+ * emitted by the canonical Rust engine.
+ */
+class EngineTraceTest {
+
+    @Test
+    fun mountTextStackMatchesTheRustEngine() {
+        val sink = FrameOpcodeSink()
+        Emitter(sink).mount(VStack(spacing = 8f) { Text("Hello") }, Environment.DEFAULT)
+        assertFrame("mount_text_stack", "000-mount", sink.frame())
+    }
+
+    @Test
+    fun signalTextDeltaMatchesTheRustEngine() {
+        val sink = FrameOpcodeSink()
+        val emitter = Emitter(sink)
+        val text = signal("Hello")
+        emitter.mount(VStack { Text(text) }, Environment.DEFAULT)
+        assertFrame("signal_text_delta", "000-mount", sink.frame())
+
+        text.set("World")
+        assertFrame("signal_text_delta", "001-set-text", sink.frame())
+    }
+
+    @Test
+    fun structuralAddRemoveMatchesTheRustEngine() {
+        val sink = FrameOpcodeSink()
+        val emitter = Emitter(sink)
+        val items = signal(listOf("a"))
+        emitter.mount(ForEach(items) { item, _ -> Text(item) }, Environment.DEFAULT)
+        assertFrame("structural_add_remove", "000-mount", sink.frame())
+
+        items.set(listOf("a", "b"))
+        assertFrame("structural_add_remove", "001-add-child", sink.frame())
+
+        items.set(listOf("a"))
+        assertFrame("structural_add_remove", "002-remove-child", sink.frame())
+    }
+
+    @Test
+    fun styledTextMountMatchesTheRustEngine() {
+        val sink = FrameOpcodeSink()
+        Emitter(sink).mount(Text("Hello").fontSize(17f), Environment.DEFAULT)
+        assertFrame("styled_text_mount", "000-mount", sink.frame())
+    }
+
+    @Test
+    fun propertySignalDeltaMatchesTheRustEngine() {
+        val sink = FrameOpcodeSink()
+        val emitter = Emitter(sink)
+        val spacing: WritableSignal<Float> = signal(8f)
+        emitter.mount(VStack(spacing = spacing) { Text("Hello") }, Environment.DEFAULT)
+        assertFrame("property_signal_delta", "000-mount", sink.frame())
+
+        spacing.set(12f)
+        assertFrame("property_signal_delta", "001-set-spacing", sink.frame())
+    }
+
+    private fun assertFrame(scenario: String, step: String, frame: ProtocolFrame) {
+        val file = traceRoot().resolve(scenario).resolve("$step.plpl.hex")
+        assertArrayEquals(readHex(file), FrameCodec.encodeFrame(frame), "$scenario/$step")
+    }
+
+    private fun readHex(file: Path): ByteArray {
+        val hex = StringBuilder()
+        for (line in Files.readAllLines(file, StandardCharsets.UTF_8)) {
+            if (line.isNotBlank() && !line.startsWith("#")) hex.append(line.trim())
+        }
+        return hex.toString().chunked(2).map { it.toInt(16).toByte() }.toByteArray()
+    }
+
+    private fun traceRoot(): Path {
+        var dir: Path? = Path.of(System.getProperty("user.dir")).toAbsolutePath()
+        while (dir != null) {
+            val candidate = dir.resolve("spec/engine-traces")
+            if (Files.isDirectory(candidate)) return candidate
+            dir = dir.parent
+        }
+        error("could not locate spec/engine-traces from ${System.getProperty("user.dir")}")
+    }
+}

+            .map { it.b() }
+
+    private fun nodeId(frame: ProtocolFrame, component: Int): Int =
+        frame.opcodes().first {
+            it.category() == Categories.TREE &&
+                it.command() == Commands.Tree.CREATE_NODE &&
+                it.b() == component
+        }.a()
+
+    private fun hasProperty(frame: ProtocolFrame, node: Int, property: Int, value: Int): Boolean =
+        frame.opcodes().any {
+            it.category() == Categories.PARAMETER &&
+                it.command() == Commands.Parameter.SET_PROPERTY &&
+                it.a() == node &&
+                (it.b() and 0xFFFF) == property &&
+                it.c() == value
+        }
+
+    @Test
+    fun registeredAudioControllerGetsAPinnedRootNode() {
+        val controller = MediaController("/track.mp3")
+        val sink = FrameOpcodeSink()
+        Emitter(sink).mount(AudioRoot(controller), Environment.DEFAULT)
+
+        val frame = sink.frame()
+        assertEquals(1, createdComponents(frame).count { it == Components.MEDIA_CONTROLLER })
+        val controllerId = nodeId(frame, Components.MEDIA_CONTROLLER)
+        val rootId = nodeId(frame, Components.VSTACK)
+        assertTrue(
+            frame.opcodes().any {
+                it.category() == Categories.TREE &&
+                    it.command() == Commands.Tree.INSERT_CHILD &&
+                    it.a() == rootId && it.b() == controllerId
+            },
+            "the controller is a root child",
+        )
+        assertTrue(
+            frame.opcodes().any {
+                it.category() == Categories.PARAMETER &&
+                    it.command() == Commands.Parameter.SET_PROPERTY &&
+                    it.a() == controllerId &&
+                    (it.b() and 0xFFFF) == Properties.MEDIA_SOURCE &&
+                    frame.stringAt(it.c()) == "/track.mp3"
+            },
+            "the controller carries its resource",
+        )
+    }
+
+    @Test
+    fun videoStaysInPlaceAndBindsTheRootController() {
+        val controller = MediaController("https://example.com/clip.mp4")
+        val sink = FrameOpcodeSink()
+        Emitter(sink).mount(
+            VStack {
+                Text("before")
+                Video(controller)
+                Text("after")
+            },
+            Environment.DEFAULT,
+        )
+
+        val frame = sink.frame()
+        val created = createdComponents(frame)
+        val videoIndex = created.indexOf(Components.VIDEO)
+        val controllerIndex = created.indexOf(Components.MEDIA_CONTROLLER)
+        assertTrue(videoIndex in 0 until controllerIndex, "video keeps its authored position")
+        val videoId = nodeId(frame, Components.VIDEO)
+        val controllerId = nodeId(frame, Components.MEDIA_CONTROLLER)
+        assertTrue(
+            hasProperty(frame, videoId, Properties.MEDIA_CONTROLLER_ID, controllerId),
+            "video references the root controller",
+        )
+    }
+
+    @Test
+    fun controllerIdSurvivesRootReRendersAndPropertyDeltasTargetIt() {
+        val controller = MediaController("/track.mp3")
+        val tick = Signals.signal(0)
+        val sink = FrameOpcodeSink()
+        val emitter = Emitter(sink)
+        emitter.mount(AudioRoot(controller, tick), Environment.DEFAULT)
+
+        val controllerId = nodeId(sink.frame(), Components.MEDIA_CONTROLLER)
+        tick.set(1)
+        val delta = sink.frame()
+        assertFalse(
+            delta.opcodes().any {
+                it.category() == Categories.TREE &&
+                    (it.command() == Commands.Tree.CREATE_NODE ||
+                        it.command() == Commands.Tree.DELETE_NODE) &&
+                    (it.a() == controllerId || it.b() == Components.MEDIA_CONTROLLER)
+            },
+            "a root re-render must not recreate the controller",
+        )
+        assertTrue(delta.opcodes().any {
+            it.category() == Categories.PARAMETER &&
+                it.command() == Commands.Parameter.SET_TEXT &&
+                delta.stringAt(it.b()) == "t1"
+        })
+
+        controller.play()
+        val propertyDelta = sink.frame()
+        assertTrue(
+            hasProperty(propertyDelta, controllerId, Properties.PLAYBACK_STATE, 1),
+            "transport changes target the pinned controller node",
+        )
+    }
+
+    @Test
+    fun videoAddedInANestedBranchProjectsItsControllerAfterMount() {
+        val controller = MediaController("https://example.com/late.mp4")
+        val sink = RecordingSink()
+
+        class Branch(private val controller: MediaController) : Component() {
+            val show = Signals.signal(false)
+            override fun body(): View = VStack {
+                if (show.get()) Video(controller) else Text("none")
+            }
+        }
+
+        val branch = Branch(controller)
+        Emitter(sink).mount(VStack { Text("root"); +branch }, Environment.DEFAULT)
+        assertTrue(sink.frames.none { Components.MEDIA_CONTROLLER in createdComponents(it) })
+
+        branch.show.set(true)
+        val frames = sink.frames.toList()
+        val controllerFrame = frames.first { Components.MEDIA_CONTROLLER in createdComponents(it) }
+        val videoFrame = frames.last { Components.VIDEO in createdComponents(it) }
+        val controllerId = nodeId(controllerFrame, Components.MEDIA_CONTROLLER)
+        val videoId = nodeId(videoFrame, Components.VIDEO)
+        assertTrue(
+            hasProperty(videoFrame, videoId, Properties.MEDIA_CONTROLLER_ID, controllerId),
+            "a late video binds the projected controller",
+        )
+    }
+
+    @Test
+    fun unregisteringRemovesTheRootController() {
+        val controller = MediaController("/track.mp3")
+        val sink = FrameOpcodeSink()
+        val emitter = Emitter(sink)
+        emitter.registerMediaController(controller)
+        emitter.mount(VStack { Text("audio") }, Environment.DEFAULT)
+        val controllerId = nodeId(sink.frame(), Components.MEDIA_CONTROLLER)
+
+        emitter.unregisterMediaController(controller)
+        val delta = sink.frame()
+        assertTrue(
+            delta.opcodes().any {
+                it.category() == Categories.TREE &&
+                    it.command() == Commands.Tree.DELETE_NODE &&
+                    it.a() == controllerId
+            },
+            "unregister removes the controller node",
+        )
+    }
+
+}

+The shared, framework-agnostic JVM engine, runtime and authoring DSL for the
+Pathland protocol, written entirely in Kotlin. It owns the `View` SPI and shared
+authoring vocabulary, the retained-tree diff emitter,
+signals/computed/effects, the wire codec, router, cross-platform state, JNA ring
+interop, and the `dev.pathland.view.dsl` SwiftUI-shaped builders/modifiers.
+Server and renderer modules depend on this one module; Java hosts consume the
+Kotlin-authored views through JVM interop.
 
 ## Implemented
 
 - **Protocol** (`dev.pathland.view.core.protocol`): `Components`, `Properties`,
   `Commands`, `Categories`, `ValueTypes`, `Opcode`, `ValueEncoder`, `WireValue`,
   `TokenPath`.
 - **Signals** (`dev.pathland.view.core.signal`): `signal`/`state`/`computed`/
   `effect`/`untracked`, synchronous glitch-free flush, equality suppression, error
   caching/retry, circular-dependency detection, and a thread-safe global
   `Scheduler`. `Signals.state` binds to the ambient session `PersistentState`
   during a component render.
 - **State** (`dev.pathland.view.core.state`): `PersistentState`, untyped
   `StateStore`, in-memory store and provider. Kotlin `Component` state delegates
   bind directly before `body()`; the Java `State` field/binder machinery and
   annotation processor are removed.
 - **Transport** (`dev.pathland.view.core.transport`): `ProtocolFrame`,
   `FrameCodec`, `Event`, `EnvironmentData`, `OpcodeSink`, `FrameOpcodeSink`.
 - **Router** (`dev.pathland.view.core.router`): `Route`, `RouteTable`, `Router`,
   `Navigation`, `NavigationContainer`, `NavigationIntent`, `Params`, `Chrome`,
   `NavOp`. `NavigationLink` and the navigation helpers live in the Kotlin DSL.
 - **JNA interop** (`dev.pathland.view.core.ffm`): lazy `PathlandCore` binding and
   `RingOpcodeSink` over `libpathland_core`.
 - **Emitter** (`dev.pathland.view.engine`): `Emitter`, `PathlandNode`, `ViewSlot`,
   `RenderResult`, `InputDispatcher`, `ReactiveValues`, `DateInput`, `MediaInput`.
   Implements mount/id assignment, diff-based reactive emission, node-level binding
   effects, structural reconciliation, fit/media/navigation routing, and the
   zero-opcode unchanged recompute contract. Registered `MediaController`s are
   projected as pinned, non-visual root children; `unregisterMediaController`
   removes them without touching the app tree.
 - **Shared SPI/values** (`dev.pathland.view.core`): `View`, `ViewModifier`,
   `Configurable`, `ChildrenView`, `Modified`, `ViewBuilder`,
   `Environment*`, `Platform`, `Theme*`, `MediaController`, `WindowMetadata`,
   `ProxyConfig`, `Color`, `Length`, shared enums, style protocols, and modifier
   wrappers.
 - **Protocol manifest validation** (`ProtocolManifestTest`): the hand-written
   protocol constants (`Components`, `Properties`, `Commands`, `Categories`,
   `ValueTypes`) are checked against `spec/protocol.tsv` — including no extra
   public numeric constants and the full `ValueTypes.forProperty` mapping. No
   Java source is generated.
 - **Shared engine traces**: the Kotlin DSL tests run the mount/text/property
   scenarios against the Rust-emitted PLPL fixtures under `spec/engine-traces/`,
   byte-for-byte. The canonical order lives in `spec/ENGINE.md`.
 - **Tests**: `pathland-view-core` owns the signal, state, frame-codec, and
   protocol-manifest tests; Kotlin DSL tests exercise the emitter end-to-end, and
   the server/HTML/desktop consumers cover their integration paths.
 
+## Authoring DSL (`dev.pathland.view.dsl`)
+
+- **SwiftUI-shaped builders**: `Text`, `Image`, `Icon`, `Color`, `Rectangle`,
+  `Circle`, `Ellipse`, `Capsule`, `RoundedRectangle`, `Shape`, `Divider`, `Spacer`,
+  `ProgressView`, `Gauge`, `Label`, `Group`.
+- **Containers**: `VStack`, `HStack`, `ZStack`, `Grid`, `GridRow`, `ScrollView`,
+  `LazyVStack`, `LazyHStack`, `LazyVGrid`, `LazyHGrid`, `ViewThatFits`/`Fit`,
+  `ProxyView`, `ForEach`.
+- **Controls**: `Button` (title or label subtree), `TextField`, `SecureField`,
+  `TextEditor`, `Toggle`, `Slider`, `Stepper`, `DatePicker`, `Picker`, `Menu`,
+  `ColorPicker`.
+- **Automatic child collection**: `VStack { Text("a"); Text("b") }` needs no
+  `.children(...)`. A custom `Component` constructed inline in a block
+  auto-registers; a view stored as a field is added explicitly with `+field`.
+- **Signals**: `signal`, `computed`, `constant`, `effect`, `untracked`,
+  `Signal<T>.value`, `WritableSignal<T>.value`, `Signal<T>.map`, `readonly`.
+- **Modifier sugar**: `.padding`, `.frame`, `.offset`, `.position`, `.fixedSize`,
+  layout priority/z-index/aspect ratio, the full text-formatting surface,
+  foreground/background/border/corner radius/shadow, visual effects, transforms,
+  visibility/disabled/hit-testing, accessibility, tap/pointer events,
+  environment binding, styles, window metadata, and navigation intents.
+- **Persisted state**: `Component` base class + `val count by state(0)`
+  (auto-keyed by property name) or `state(0, "key")`; a `mutableState(0)` signal
+  form for two-way controls.
+- **Reactive bodies**: plain `if`/`when`/`for` in `body()`; `ForEach` over a static
+  list or `Signal<List<T>>` with row-scoped child collection.
+- **Navigation**: `navigator { route(...) }`, `NavigationStack`, `NavigationLink`,
+  `isActive`, and `.navigate`/`.push`/`.replace` intents.
+- **Media**: `Video(controller)` stays where the app places it; audio remains
+  view-less. `controller.register()` projects a controller at the root.
+- **Naming**: the composite base is `Component` (renamed from `KotlinView` now
+  that the Java DSL is gone); see #174.
+- **Java hosting**: a Java Spring Boot / Quarkus app mounts a Kotlin view through
+  the Java-friendly `PathlandApp` functional interface
+  (`return () -> MusicPlayerView.make();`). Kotlin roots expose public
+  constructors and/or `@JvmStatic make(...)` factories.
+

-  `core` and `engine` into separate artifacts requires a node SPI first.

-/**
- * Base class for application-authored Kotlin views.
- *
- * A subclass declares its subtree in [body]; a signal read there re-renders only this
- * component (the emitter tracks the slot). Persisted state is declared with
- * [state] / [mutableState] and is bound to the session's [PersistentState] before the
- * first body render — no annotation processor or kapt.
- *
- * Constructing a [Component] inside a builder block auto-registers it, so
- * `VStack { CounterView() }` needs no `.children(...)`.
- */
-abstract class Component : View {
-
-    private val stateSignals = mutableListOf<StateSignal<*>>()
-
-    init {
-        // Inline construction (`VStack { CounterView() }`) auto-registers. A view
-        // constructed as a field of another view must not leak into the enclosing
-        // builder scope; it is added explicitly with `+field` inside body().
-        if (!insideAnotherViewConstructor()) {
-            registerChild()
-        }
-    }
-
-    /**
-     * A persisted, two-way state signal keyed by the property name:
-     * `private var count by state(0)` or with an explicit store key
-     * `private var count by state(0, "counter")`.
-     */
-    protected fun <T : Any> state(initial: T, key: String? = null): StateDelegate<T> =
-        StateDelegate(mutableState(initial, key))
-
-    /**
-     * A persisted state signal for code that wants the signal directly:
-     * `val name = mutableState("")` can be passed to `TextField(text = name)`.
-     */
-    protected fun <T : Any> mutableState(initial: T, key: String? = null): StateSignal<T> {
-        val state = StateSignal(initial, key)
-        stateSignals.add(state)
-        return state
-    }
-
-    final override fun renderNode(env: Environment): PathlandNode {
-        val persistent = env.state()
-        return PersistentState.withCurrent(persistent) {
-            persistent?.let { state ->
-                stateSignals.forEach { it.bind(state) }
-            }
-            val resolved = body()
-            check(resolved !== this) {
-                "${javaClass.name} must return its subtree from body()"
-            }
-            resolved.renderNode(env)
-        }
-    }
-
-    abstract override fun body(): View
-
-    private fun insideAnotherViewConstructor(): Boolean {
-        val self = javaClass
-        return java.lang.StackWalker
-            .getInstance(java.lang.StackWalker.Option.RETAIN_CLASS_REFERENCE)
-            .walk { frames ->
-                frames.anyMatch { frame ->
-                    frame.methodName == "<init>" &&
-                        frame.declaringClass != self &&
-                        frame.declaringClass != Component::class.java &&
-                        Component::class.java.isAssignableFrom(frame.declaringClass)
-                }
-            }
-    }
-}
-
-/**
- * A persisted state value. It behaves as a [WritableSignal] so it can be passed
- * straight to two-way controls; binding to the session store happens before the
- * owning view's [Component.body] runs.
- */
-class StateSignal<T : Any> internal constructor(
-    initial: T,
-    var key: String? = null,
-) : WritableSignal<T> {
-
-    private var current: WritableSignal<T> = Signals.signal(initial)
-    private var bound = false
-
-    internal fun bind(persistent: PersistentState) {
-        if (bound) return
-        val storeKey = checkNotNull(key) { "State has no key (declare it with `by state(...)`) " }
-        current = persistent.signal(storeKey, current.get())
-        bound = true
-    }
-
-    override fun get(): T = current.get()
-
-    override fun set(value: T) = current.set(value)
-
-    override fun update(fn: UnaryOperator<T>) = current.update(fn)
-
-    override fun asReadonly(): Signal<T> = current.asReadonly()
-
-    /** The auto-saved persisted value (the signal itself is a [WritableSignal]). */
-    var value: T
-        get() = get()
-        set(value) = set(value)
-}
-
-/** Property-delegate form of [StateSignal]. */
-class StateDelegate<T : Any> internal constructor(
-    val signal: StateSignal<T>,
-) : ReadWriteProperty<Any?, T> {
-
-    operator fun provideDelegate(thisRef: Any?, property: KProperty<*>): StateDelegate<T> {
-        if (signal.key == null) {
-            signal.key = property.name
-        }
-        return this
-    }
-
-    override fun getValue(thisRef: Any?, property: KProperty<*>): T = signal.get()
-
-    override fun setValue(thisRef: Any?, property: KProperty<*>, value: T) = signal.set(value)
-}

@@ -1,87 +0,0 @@
-# pathland-view-kotlin — implementation status
-
-**Last updated:** November 3, 2026
-
-The sole JVM authoring surface (`dev.pathland.view.dsl`), Kotlin-owned over the
-Kotlin `pathland-view-core`. The Java DSL, its processor, and its Java-only
-Quarkus extension/starter alias are removed.
-
-## Authoring surface
-
-- **Kotlin-owned**: all primitives, shapes, stacks, grids, scroll/lazy
-  containers, `ForEach`, `Button`, text/value controls, media, navigation,
-  `Label`, `ViewThatFits`/`Fit`, `ProxyView`, styles (`PlainButtonStyle`,
-  `BorderedButtonStyle`, label styles, `NativeVideoStyle`), and the complete
-  modifier vocabulary (padding/frame/fonts/colors/borders/shadows/effects/
-  transforms/interaction/accessibility/environment/styles/window metadata).
-- **Dependency boundary**: main depends on `pathland-view-core` only.
-- Tests are Kotlin-only; golden engine traces and opcode/property assertions
-  replace the former Java-vs-Kotlin parity oracle.
-
-## Implemented
-
-- **SwiftUI-shaped builders**: `Text`, `Image`, `Icon`, `Color`, `Rectangle`,
-  `Circle`, `Ellipse`, `Capsule`, `RoundedRectangle`, `Shape`, `Divider`, `Spacer`,
-  `ProgressView`, `Gauge`, `Label`, `Group`.
-- **Containers**: `VStack`, `HStack`, `ZStack`, `Grid`, `GridRow`, `ScrollView`,
-  `LazyVStack`, `LazyHStack`, `LazyVGrid`, `LazyHGrid`, `ViewThatFits`/`Fit`,
-  `ProxyView`.
-- **Controls**: `Button` (title or label subtree), `TextField`, `SecureField`,
-  `TextEditor`, `Toggle`, `Slider`, `Stepper`, `DatePicker`, `Picker`, `Menu`,
-  `ColorPicker`.
-- **Automatic child collection**: `VStack { Text("a"); Text("b") }` needs no
-  `.children(...)`. A custom `Component` constructed inline in a block
-  auto-registers; a view stored as a field is added explicitly with `+field`
-  inside `body()` (it does not leak into the enclosing scope). An explicit
-  `view.add()` / `+view` is available for Java-constructed or prebuilt views.
-- **Signals**: `signal`, `computed`, `constant`, `effect`, `untracked`,
-  `Signal<T>.value`, `WritableSignal<T>.value`, `Signal<T>.map`, `readonly`.
-- **Modifier sugar**: `.padding`, `.frame`, `.offset`, `.position`, `.fixedSize`,
-  layout priority/z-index/aspect ratio, the full text-formatting surface,
-  foreground/background/border/corner radius/shadow, visual effects, transforms,
-  visibility/disabled/hit-testing, accessibility, tap/pointer events,
-  environment binding, styles, window metadata, and navigation intents. A child
-  modifier replaces its auto-registered leaf in the enclosing builder, so
-  `VStack { Text("x").fontSize(20f) }` keeps the modifier. The core
-  `View.modifiers(...)` operation remains available as an escape hatch.
-- **Persisted state**: `Component` base class + `val count by state(0)`
-  (auto-keyed by property name) or `state(0, "key")`; a `mutableState(0)` signal
-  form for two-way controls. Bound to the session's `PersistentState` before the
-  first `body()` render — no kapt and no annotation processor.
-- **`Signals.state`**: Components and services can create persisted signals with
-  `Signals.state("key", initial)` while the framework's session state is active
-  during render. Outside a state context it falls back to an in-memory signal.
-- **Reactive bodies**: plain `if`/`when`/`for` in `body()`; `ForEach` over a static
-  list or `Signal<List<T>>` with row-scoped child collection.
-- **Navigation**: `navigator { route(...) }`, `NavigationStack`, `NavigationLink`,
-  `isActive`, and `.navigate`/`.push`/`.replace` intents.
-- **Media**: `Video(controller)` stays where the app places it; audio remains
-  view-less. `controller.register()` projects a controller at the root (ordinary
-  audio services call it while rendering).
-- **Tests**: structure/opcode/property assertions, auto-collection,
-  child-modifier application, modifier property parity, fine-grained signal
-  deltas, persisted/stateful bodies, reactive `ForEach`, two-way
-  `TextField`/`Slider`/`Stepper`, navigation swaps and link intents, and media
-  projection (audio root nodes,
-  authored `VIDEO` placement, stable controller ids, and late nested videos).
-
-## Naming
-
-- The composite base is `Component` (renamed from `KotlinView` now that the Java
-  DSL is gone). Whether to align the authoring type with SwiftUI's single `View`
-  protocol is tracked by #174.
-
-## Java hosting
-
-- A Java Spring Boot / Quarkus app mounts a Kotlin view through the Java-friendly
-  `PathlandApp` functional interface (`return () -> MusicPlayerView.make();`).
-- Kotlin root views expose public constructors and/or `@JvmStatic make(...)`
-  factories with Java-friendly parameter types.
-- Tests in `pathland-spring-boot-starter` and `pathland-quarkus` prove a Java
-  host renders a Kotlin fixture and receives live signal deltas.
-
-## Not implemented / gaps
-
-- No Kotlin Multiplatform target yet — the module is JVM-only over
-  `pathland-view-core`.
-- `SecureField` is Kotlin-owned (`TEXT_FIELD` + `IS_SECURE`).

 # Pathland Rust Workspace
 
 The Rust core of Pathland: the **opcode engine** that emits the declarative
 view structure as a fixed 16-byte opcode ring buffer into shared linear memory,
 consumed by host renderers. Runs natively on desktop (C ABI + GTK renderer).
 
 ```
 crates/
 │  # ── The three elements ────────────────────────────────────────────────
 ├── pathland-view/          # RETAINED UI — SwiftUI-style view DSL: VStack/HStack/Text/
 │                           #   Button + chainable modifiers (spacing/padding/fontSize/
 │                           #   color/background) building a retained tree (no_std)
 ├── pathland-core/          # OPCODE ENGINE — retained tree types (Node/Component) + the
 │                           #   diff-based reactive emitter + 16-byte opcode, ring buffer,
 │                           #   bump arena, constants, events (no_std, zero-alloc steady state)
 ├── pathland-core-transport/# OPCODE ENGINE — transport: shared-memory ring owner + network
 │                           #   batch encode/decode + batching policy (std)
 ├── pathland-render-gtk/    # RENDERER — opcode frames -> native GTK4 widgets (incremental);
 │                           #   the only crate that touches GTK/glib/pango
 │  # ── Retained-UI projection (host/driver surface for other languages) ──
 ├── pathland-view-native/   # native C-ABI shim + NativeHost over a zero-copy shared ring
 │                           #   (Swift/Java; cdylib name stays "pathland_native")
 ├── pathland-core-capi/     # minimal shared-memory ring C ABI for foreign hosts
 │                           #   (libpathland_core): create/destroy, ring push, frame
 │                           #   boundaries, zero-copy read, event drain/send
 └── pathland-render-gtk-demo/ # GTK4 desktop demo: authors the DSL, renders through
                               #   pathland-render-gtk (uses NO GTK APIs directly)
 ```
 
 ## Java libraries (framework-agnostic)
 
 The reusable Java libraries live in `../java/` (Maven reactor, `dev.pathland`):
 
-- `pathland-view` — SwiftUI-like view DSL + Angular-style signals/computed/effects,
-  fine-grained opcode emitter, wire codec, JNA ring interop (`dev.pathland.view`)
+- `pathland-view-core` — Kotlin engine, signals, wire codec, router, state, JNA
+  ring interop, and the SwiftUI-like `dev.pathland.view.dsl` authoring DSL
 - `pathland-render-html` — pure-function HTML renderer (SSR) over the opcode stream
-- `pathland-state-redis` — Redis-backed `StateStore` (Lettuce)
+- `pathland-server-core` — server runtime, telemetry adapters, Redis `StateStore`
 - `pathland-quarkus-demo` — Quarkus SSR + WebSocket demo consuming the libraries
 
 ## Specification
 
 - [`spec/OPCODE.md`](../../spec/OPCODE.md) — the 16-byte opcode protocol
 - [`spec/CONFORMANCE.md`](../../spec/CONFORMANCE.md) — golden byte vectors
 
 ## Protocol manifest
 
 `pathland-protocol-manifest` emits `spec/protocol.tsv`, the target-neutral
 machine-readable ID manifest consumed by non-Rust bindings. It emits data only;
 each language owns its own representation. Regenerate after changing
 `pathland-core` constants:
 
 ```bash
 cargo run -p pathland-protocol-manifest
 ```
 
 ## Engine trace fixtures
 
 `pathland-engine-golden` emits shared self-contained PLPL frames under
 `spec/engine-traces/`; the JVM `EngineTraceTest` compares against them
 byte-for-byte. Regenerate after an emission change:
 
 ```bash
 cargo run -p pathland-engine-golden -- --emit
 ```
 
 ## Run tests
 
 ```bash
 PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH" cargo test
 ```
 
 ## Verify the no_std / wasm32 direction guard
 
 `pathland-core` and `pathland-view` must stay `no_std` + `alloc` and compile for
 `wasm32-unknown-unknown`, so the core can still target a browser/embedded/remote
 projection later. Verify with:
 
 ```bash
 ./check-wasm.sh
 ```
 
 ## Run the GTK desktop demo (native, zero-copy shared ring)
 
 ```bash
 PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH" cargo run -p pathland-render-gtk-demo
 ```
 
 Requires GTK4 (`brew install gtk4` on macOS).
 
 ## Run the Java libraries (build + test)
 
 The Java libraries build against `libpathland_core` when the native ring path is
 used (desktop/JNA). Build and test the whole reactor:
 
 ```bash
 PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH" cargo build -p pathland-core-capi
 cd ../java && mvn -q install
 ```
 
 The `pathland-view` core (views, signals, emitter, codec, HTML renderer) needs no
 native library and runs on the JVM alone; only the JNA ring sink loads
 `libpathland_core`.
 
 
 ## Engine example
 
 The engine emits declarative structure (no rects). A signal changes a property;
 the next `emit` writes only the delta opcodes.
 
 ```rust
 use pathland_core::{init_memory, Guest, MemoryLayout};
 use pathland_view::{assign_ids, text, vstack, View, ViewExt};
 
 let layout = MemoryLayout::default();
 let mut mem = vec![0u8; layout.total_bytes()];
 init_memory(&mut mem, &layout);
 
 let mut guest = Guest::new(&mut mem, &layout);
 let mut engine = pathland_core::Engine::new();
 
 let mut root = vstack![text("Hello")]
     .spacing(4.0)
     .padding(8.0)
     .build();
 assign_ids(&mut root, &mut 1);
 
 guest.begin_frame();
 engine.emit(&root, &mut guest).unwrap(); // full structure
 guest.end_frame();
 
 root.properties.insert(pathland_core::property_id::SPACING, 12.0f32.to_bits());
 
 guest.begin_frame();
 engine.emit(&root, &mut guest).unwrap(); // exactly one SET_PROPERTY
 guest.end_frame();
 ```
 
 Emission in the steady state allocates nothing; only changed nodes produce
 opcodes, so an unchanged tree emits zero opcodes. Native renderers map the
 structure onto their native elements (GTK4 widgets, DOM elements).
 
 ## Network transport example
 
 Frames emitted into the ring can be serialized into network batches and flushed
 on a time/size policy (`BatchEncoder` / `Batcher`); a `BatchDecoder` rebuilds a
 `Frame`-compatible view so the same `RenderTree::apply_frame` consumes batches
 and shared-memory frames identically. See `spec/OPCODE.md#transport`.
