 ### 5.6 Custom modifiers (developer-authored)
 
 In SwiftUI any developer can define a modifier that applies to **any** existing
 view — and Pathland is the same. This is a **first-class, MUST** property of
 every conformant DSL: modifiers are never hard-bound to a view type.
 
 - **Applicable to any view.** A modifier works on a library primitive
   (`Text`), a container (`VStack`), a control (`Button`), a custom view, or an
   already-modified view. The same modifier value applies everywhere.
 - **One mechanism.** Core and application-authored modifiers are the **same
   surface**: a `ViewModifier` value applied via `.modifiers(...)`. There is
   **no per-modifier sugar on the view type**; a parameterized modifier is
   constructed by a lowercase static function named for the modifier ([§5.0](#50-authoring-a-modifier))
   and single-value modifiers pass the value directly.
 
 | | Canonical | Kotlin DSL (`dev.pathland.view.dsl`) | Rust DSL (`pathland-view`) |
 |-|-----------|-------------------------------|----------------------------|
 | authoring | `struct Card: ViewModifier { func body(content: Content) -> some View }` | `@FunctionalInterface ViewModifier { View body(View content) }` | `trait ViewModifier { fn apply(&mut Node) }` |
 | applying | `content.modifier(Card())` | `content.modifiers(card(c -> …))` / `content.modifiers(A, B)` | `content.modifiers(Card)` |
 | single-value | `.modifier(Padding(16))` | `content.modifiers(padding(p -> p.uniform(16)))` | `content.modifiers(Padding(16.0))` |
 
 **Composition**: a custom modifier composes core modifiers **or** wraps
 `content` with additional structure (a background, an overlay, a frame) and
 returns the decorated view — exactly SwiftUI's `body(content: Content)`.
 
 **Emission contract**: a custom modifier composed from core modifiers emits the
 same one-`SET_PROPERTY`-per-property deltas as writing the modifiers inline;
 emission stays diff-based, and a renderer that cannot apply a modifier
 **allows and ignores** it.
 
 **Realization deltas**:
 - **Rust** — every core modifier (`Padding`, `FontSize`, `ForegroundStyle`,
   `Frame`, …) implements `ViewModifier`, and `.modifiers(...)` applies them
   (a single modifier or a tuple).
   Caveat: `apply(&mut Node)` mutates the built node's properties only — it
   cannot wrap `content` with new structure (the Java/SwiftUI `body(content)`
   form can). A conformant DSL's custom-modifier mechanism should support
   wrapping.
 - **Java** — every core modifier is a `ViewModifier` value applied via
   `.modifiers(...)`; `View` has no modifier sugar, and a style
   (`ButtonStyle`, …) is itself a `ViewModifier` value (it binds the
   `Environment.BUTTON_STYLE` key down the subtree — subtree scoping is
   environment-only). Application-authored `ViewModifier.body(View)` is
   SwiftUI-shaped and can wrap content with structure.
 
 #### Media (`MediaController`)
 
 A media playback is a **state object**, not a view (spec/MEDIA.md; the SwiftUI
 `AVPlayer` analog). `MediaController` owns the transport as signals — commands
 (`source()`, `playing()`, `position()`, `volume()`, `muted()`, `loop()`,
 `rate()`) and reports (`time()`, `duration()`, `volumeReport()`) — plus
 `play()/pause()/toggle()/seek()/setVolume()`. The emitter materializes one
 non-visual `MEDIA_CONTROLLER` node per controller (keyed by object identity), so
 playback is stable across structural swaps.
 
 - **Audio has no view**: bind ordinary views (buttons/sliders) to the
   controller's signals. Include `controller.attach()` once in the tree — a
   non-visual marker that materializes the controller node — placed **outside**
   any swapping branch (e.g. a `SizeThatFits` slot).
 - **Video** is the only media view: `Video.make(controller)` renders the
   controller's output. `VideoStyle` supplies a custom control surface; the
   default `NativeVideoStyle` shows renderer-native controls.
 - A `MediaController` may be rebound to the app's own (e.g. persisted) signals
   (`controller.playing(signal)`), so the controller drives the same state the
   rest of the UI reads.
 
 ```java
 MediaController player = new MediaController(computed(() -> track.get().audio()));
 player.playing(playing.signal()).position(seekRequest.signal()).volume(volume.signal());
 player.time(position.signal()).onEnded(this::next);
 
 VStack.make().children(
     player.attach(),                                   // audio: non-visual
     Button.make(b -> b.action(player::toggle)),
     Slider.make(s -> s.value(player.time())),
     Video.make(player));                               // video: the only media view
 ```
 
 ## 5.7 Styleable controls (the style contract)
 
 A **style** customizes a view or control's *content*; the control owns its
 *component and interaction*. This is one contract for every styleable surface
 (`ButtonStyle`, `LabelStyle`, `VideoStyle`, …), and it is the
 author-facing shape of the protocol's **Composite Override Mode**
 ([PRIMITIVES.md §2](./PRIMITIVES.md#2-dual-mode-rendering-pipeline--platform-delegation)).
 
 - **The control owns the native component and the interaction.** A semantic
   control renders its **native control node** (its component id — `BUTTON`,
   `VIDEO`, …) and attaches its behavior to *that* node: the tap action /
   `EVENT_LISTENERS` (Button), the value/text/date sink, or the media binding
   (`Video`). The **whole control is interactive**, including its padding.
 - **The style owns the content.** A style returns the control's **content view**
   from `makeBody(Config)`; the control attaches it as the control node's
   **single child**. The content keeps its own component(s), layout, and
   properties — a style **never** sets or overwrites the control's component and
   never wires the interaction. The result is a control with children → protocol
   **Composite Override Mode**.
 - **The style consumes the control's config.** The `Config` a style's
   `makeBody(Config)` receives is the **same type** the view configured through
   `make(...)` ([§2](#2-canonical-signature-notation)): `ButtonStyle.makeBody(Button.Config)`,
   `LabelStyle.makeBody(Label.Config)`,
   `VideoStyle.makeBody(VideoStyle.Configuration)`. The style **reads** the config (the
   control's values: content, action, label, media state); it does not mutate it.
 - **A style is a modifier.** Styles are `ViewModifier` values scoped down a
   subtree with `.modifiers(<Style>)`, binding the style's `EnvironmentKey` over
   the wrapped subtree (nearest wins); the control reads it via its
   `Environment.<name>Style()` accessor. This is the one inheritance mechanism
   ([§6 rule 6](#6-authoring-conventions)); `ButtonStyle` binds
   `Environment.BUTTON_STYLE`, `VideoStyle` `Environment.VIDEO_STYLE`, `LabelStyle`
   `Environment.LABEL_STYLE`.
 - **Button content precedence (three developer options).** A `Button`'s content
   resolves as: (1) an **explicit child** supplied via `.children(...)` wins;
   else (2) the config **title** string (wrapped as a `Text`); else (3) the
   **style-supplied content** from `makeBody`. The `buttonStyle` modifier itself
   (option 3) lets a developer hand content in through the style. This mirrors
   SwiftUI's multiple button-authoring forms.
 - **Defaults preserve the native path.** The default style contributes the
   control's natural content: `PlainButtonStyle` → the label;
   `NativeVideoStyle` → **no content** (an empty-content
   sentinel), so the control stays a **leaf** in Native Token Mode and the
   renderer shows native media controls; `DefaultLabelStyle` → title + icon.
 - **Text/foreground modifiers cascade to content.** A `.foregroundStyle`/
   `.fontSize` (and the other inherited text modifiers) applied *to the control*
   reach the content's text — SwiftUI environment semantics. In the Kotlin DSL the
   properties ride the control node; renderers cascade them to child text.
 - **Main-axis alignment is the content's own layout — no protocol property.**
   A control's content box centers its child by default; to left-align a
   composite label (e.g. a navigation row), make the label full-width
   (`frame(f -> f.width(FILL))`) and let its own `ALIGNMENT` place its
   content. There is deliberately no main-axis/justification property (the engine
   describes WHAT, never WHERE — [§1](#1-design-principles-dsl-flavored)).
 - **Closed-variant ("token") styles are the same surface, not a wrapper.** Some
   styles select a whole native variant rather than supplying content:
   `ToggleStyle`/`PickerStyle`/`TextStyle` are wire **enums** applied as
   properties (`TOGGLE_STYLE`, …), and `LabelStyle` shapes which parts render.
   They are scoped/read exactly like the wrapper styles above.
 
 Canonical signatures (SwiftUI-shaped) and the realization:
 
 | Control | Style protocol | `Config` | Default style |
 |---------|----------------|----------|---------------|
 | `Button` | `ButtonStyle { makeBody(config) -> View }` | the `Button.Config` (title, action, content) | `PlainButtonStyle` (label) |
 | `Label` | `LabelStyle { makeBody(config) -> View }` | the `Label.Config` (title, icon) | `DefaultLabelStyle` (title + icon) |
 | `Video` | `VideoStyle { makeBody(config) -> View }` | the `VideoStyle.Configuration` (its `MediaController`) | `NativeVideoStyle` (no content) |
 
 ```java
 // Button: the control wires the action; the style decorates the label/content.
 enum MyButtonStyle implements ButtonStyle { INSTANCE;
     @Override public View makeBody(Button.Config c) {
         return c.content().modifiers(padding(p -> p.uniform(12)), background(b -> b.color(BLUE)));
     }
 }
 Button.make(b -> b.title("Save").action(this::save)).modifiers(MyButtonStyle.INSTANCE);
 
 // Label: the style decides which parts render (nullable parts = absent).
 enum BadgeLabelStyle implements LabelStyle { INSTANCE;
     @Override public View makeBody(Label.Config c) {
         return HStack.make().children(
                 c.icon().modifiers(frame(f -> f.width(18).height(18))),
                 c.title());
     }
 }
 ```
 
 The Kotlin DSL ships `PlainButtonStyle`/`BorderedButtonStyle`,
 `DefaultLabelStyle`/`TitleOnlyLabelStyle`/`IconOnlyLabelStyle`, and
 `NativeVideoStyle`; application-authored styles implement the
 same interfaces. **Delta:** SwiftUI's `LabelStyleConfiguration.title`/`.icon`
 are always-present views; Pathland passes `null` for an absent part (a style
 checks `hasTitle()`/`hasIcon()`). Because styles are modifiers, a style is
 applied with `.modifiers(<Style>)`.

 ## 6. Authoring conventions
 
 A conformant DSL follows these conventions:
 
 1. **Names**: SwiftUI view/modifier names; per-language case (camelCase,
    snake_case). `foregroundStyle` not `foregroundColor`; `fontWeight`,
    `multilineTextAlignment`, `scaledToFit`, `allowsHitTesting` keep their
    SwiftUI spellings. A modifier's type is **never** suffixed `Mod`.
 2. **Signature order**: canonical parameter order is preserved —
    `.border(color, width)`, `.frame(width, height, alignment)`,
    `.shadow(color, radius, x, y)`. Compound modifiers expand to one property
    per argument.
 3. **Values vs modifiers**: structural/layout values and a control's bound value
    are configured through a view's `make(...)` (modifiers through lowercase
    functions); everything else is a chainable `modifiers(...)` value. The three
    operations may be chained in any order.
 4. **Typed enums**: `HorizontalAlignment` (leading/center/trailing, for
    `VStack`), `VerticalAlignment` (top/center/bottom, for `HStack`), `Alignment`
    (2D — topLeading … bottomTrailing — for `ZStack`/grids and the `frame`
    modifier's content alignment); all **position-only, never stretching** (a
    child's `FILL` size kind stretches). Plus `TextAlignment`, `FontWeight`
    (100–900), `Truncation` (head/middle/tail),
    `TextCase` (none/uppercase/lowercase), `FontStyle` (normal/italic),
    `FontDesign` (default/serif/rounded/monospaced), `ContentMode` (fit/fill),
    `ControlSize` (small/regular/large), `ToggleStyle`
    (switch/checkbox/button), `PickerStyle` (menu/segmented/wheel/radiogroup),
    `DatePickerMode` (date/time/dateAndTime), `ShapeKind`
    (circle/rectangle/roundedRectangle/capsule/ellipse/path). Numeric codes
    come from MODIFIERS.md's appendix; the DSL resolves them.
 5. **`Spacer`/`Color` as views**: `Spacer` is a flexible expanding filler;
    `Color` in a tree is a layout-greedy fill.
 6. **The environment is the only inheritance mechanism.** Any value that must
    reach a whole subtree — a style (`ButtonStyle`), the router, the active path,
    the session's persisted state — is injected through the environment, never
    threaded through constructors and never through a second scoping system. The
    environment is a hierarchical, nearest-wins scope of typed `EnvironmentKey`
    values (the `EnvironmentBinding` modifier value / `Environment.value(key)`,
    Java; §4.5). A language MAY implement the scope with a thread-local over the
    synchronous render pass (Java does) — but that is the implementation of the
    one mechanism, not an additional one. A subtree-scoping modifier MUST be
    expressed as an `EnvironmentKey` binding: `ButtonStyle` binds
    `Environment.BUTTON_STYLE` (`EnvironmentKey<ButtonStyle>`), exactly like the
    router and the active path.
 7. **Reactivity discipline**: `body()` is a tracked render; a signal read there
    subscribes the component and a later write re-renders that component, whose
    subtree is diffed into deltas. A bound node stays fine-grained (one delta, no
    body re-run). Never write signals during render. Non-signal reads are
    mount-time only ([§3.4](#34-structural-reactivity-reactive-bodies--slots)).
 8. **Emission contract**: each DSL call emits exactly the documented
    properties with the documented value types; the emitter diffs. The DSL never
    computes layout, never positions, never serializes full trees.

 ## 7. Theme management
 
 Pathland theming is **application-owned over a renderer-owned token system**
 ([TOKENS.md](./TOKENS.md); the wire encoding lives in [OPCODE.md](./OPCODE.md)
 §Design Token System). The DSL gives the author two distinct surfaces:
 
 1. **Token references in style modifiers** — semantic intent instead of a
    literal: `foregroundStyle(f -> f.color(Color.token("color.primary")))`
    emits a `DESIGN_TOKEN` reference the renderer resolves against the current
    scheme. No opcode is re-emitted when a token or the scheme changes.
 2. **Global theme overrides** — a batch of `PARAMETER::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` commands
    rolled at mount: a single-scheme `Theme` or an `AdaptiveTheme` light+dark
    pair (base = **light**, `dark.`-prefixed = **dark**).
 
 > **Ownership**: the application owns theme values (base + `dark.*`) and token
 > references; the renderer owns token defaults (light + dark), effective
 > color-scheme detection, resolution (override → default → parent → fallback),
 > and interaction-state styling (hover/pressed/focus/disabled). The protocol
 > never transmits hover/click/transition styling.
 
 ### 7.1 Token-typed values
 
 Any property whose value type is `COLOR` / `F32` / `STRING` / `ENUM` MAY carry a
 **token reference** instead of a literal value (MODIFIERS.md §Value types). The
 reference rides the `DESIGN_TOKEN` value type (`0x08`) with the token path in
 the arena — **never** a packed literal. A property carries exactly one value
 (literal or reference, never both).
 
 | Canonical (SwiftUI-shaped) | Kotlin DSL | Rust DSL | Emits |
 |----------------------------|----------|----------|-------|
 | `Color.token("color.primary")` | `Color.token("color.primary")` | `Color::token("color.primary")` | `DESIGN_TOKEN` ref (`0x08`) in any COLOR-typed property: `COLOR` 0x100A (`.foregroundStyle`), `BACKGROUND_COLOR` 0x1001, `BORDER_COLOR` 0x1004, `SHADOW_COLOR` 0x1021, `TINT` 0x1030, … |
 | `Color.token("dark.color.surface")` | `Color.token("dark.color.surface")` | `Color::token("dark.color.surface")` | same — an explicit dark-variant reference (resolves the dark layer in either scheme) |
 | `.padding(space.2)` / `Spacing(space.2)` | `Padding.with(Length.token("space.2"))` / `spacing(Length.token("space.2"))` | `Padding(Length::token("space.2"))` / `spacing(Length::token("space.2"))` | `DESIGN_TOKEN` ref in a F32-typed property: `PADDING` 0x1011 / `SPACING` 0x0001 / `CONTENT_MARGINS` 0x0005, … (see TOKENS.md §Generative token families) |
 | `Font.body.family` token | `FontFamily.token("font.body.family")` | `FontFamily::token("font.body.family")` | `DESIGN_TOKEN` ref in a STRING-typed property (`FONT_FAMILY`) |
 
 Token references are **static paths**: a signal-bound property carries a
 literal value, not a token reference.
 
 `Color` keeps its dual identity: as a **View** it is a layout-greedy fill; as a
 token reference (`Color.token(path)`) it is a **data value** passed to
 style-taking modifiers. A token-typed property resolves renderer-side and
 **re-resolves automatically** when the effective scheme changes — overrides and
 scheme are renderer state, so no node is ever re-emitted for a theme/scheme
 change.
 
 Rules:
 
 1. Reference any token path — the standard catalog (TOKENS.md §Standard Token
    Catalog) or an application-defined path. A renderer that cannot apply a token
    falls back rather than erroring.
 2. `space.<N>` members are **generative**: reference them freely (`space.2`,
    `space.0.5`), but override only `space.base` (see §7.2 rule 2).
 3. A token reference must not be combined with a literal on the same property.
 
 ### 7.2 Global theme overrides
 
 A **theme** is a batch of token overrides. Every override defines **exactly one
 value**; combine a light and a dark `Theme` via `AdaptiveTheme` for adaptive
 theming.
 
 | Canonical (SwiftUI-shaped) | Kotlin DSL (`dev.pathland.view.dsl`) | Rust DSL (`pathland-view` / `pathland-engine`) | Emits |
 |----------------------------|--------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------|-------|
 | `Theme()` — one-scheme override batch | `new Theme().color(...)...` | `Theme::new()` | one `PARAMETER::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` per override (`A` = arena path, `B` = valueType, `C` = value) |
 | `.color("color.primary", 0xFF2563EB)` | `.color("color.primary", 0xFF2563EB)` | `.color("color.primary", 0xFF2563EB)` | `COLOR`-typed override (sRGB `0xAARRGGBB`) |
 | `.f32("space.base", 4.0)` | `.f32("space.base", 4.0f)` | `.f32("space.base", 4.0)` | `F32`-typed override (lengths in device pixels) |
 | `.u32("…", v)` / `.u8("…", v)` | `.u32(path, int)` / `.u8(path, int)` | `.u32(path, v)` / `.u8(path, v)` | `U32` / `U8`-typed override |
 | `.string("font.body.family", "Inter")` | `.string(path, String)` | `.string(path, "Inter")` | `STRING`-typed override (arena) |
 | `AdaptiveTheme(light, dark)` | `new AdaptiveTheme(light, dark)` | `AdaptiveTheme::new(light, dark)` | light overrides as base tokens; dark overrides `dark.`-prefixed |
 
 Emission contract:
 
 - The theme is emitted **once at mount** as a frame of
   `PARAMETER::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` opcodes before the tree. Java: `new Emitter(sink,
   theme)` emits it at the start of the mount and `renderFull` (resync) frames;
   Rust: `Engine::apply_theme` / `Engine::apply_adaptive_theme`.
 - Overrides are **renderer state**: they never re-emit nodes and never
   participate in the diff — an unchanged tree with a theme still emits **zero**
   per-node opcodes.
 - `AdaptiveTheme` emits the light `Theme`'s overrides as base paths and the dark
   `Theme`'s with the `dark.` prefix (added automatically when the author wrote a
   bare path). The renderer derives the effective scheme from the platform and
   resolves each override against it.
 - The renderer supplies light + dark defaults for the whole Tier 1 catalog, so
   dark mode works even when the author only overrides base tokens.
 
 Authoring rules:
 
 1. Override any token in the catalog or an application-defined path; never
    assume specific renderer default values.
 2. Override `space.base` to control the whole spacing scale — individual
    `space.<N>` members MUST NOT be overridden.
 3. Overrides are **global and renderer-wide**: apply the theme once per
    session/host at mount, not per view.
 
 ### 7.3 Runtime theming and scheme choice
 
 A host MAY replace the theme after mount. Replacement is **reset + apply**: the
 host emits `META::RESET_THEME` followed by the new theme's
 `PARAMETER::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` overrides in one frame. The renderer clears the
 old overrides, re-resolves every token-referencing property, and re-applies the
 new values; no node is re-emitted.
 
 The host MAY also force the effective scheme with
 `META::SET_COLOR_SCHEME`:
 
 | Canonical mode | Emits | Behavior |
 |----------------|-------|----------|
 | `.platform` | `SET_COLOR_SCHEME` A=0 | follow the OS/browser light/dark signal (default) |
 | `.light` | `SET_COLOR_SCHEME` A=1 | force the light design |
 | `.dark` | `SET_COLOR_SCHEME` A=2 | force the dark design |
 
 While forced, platform scheme changes are ignored. Returning to `.platform`
 restores native detection. Both commands are renderer state — the emitter
 re-resolves, never re-emitting the tree.
 
 Java exposes this through `Emitter.replaceTheme(...)` / `resetTheme()` /
 `setColorScheme(...)`; the server runtime's host-level
 `PathlandSession.setTheme(...)` / `setColorScheme(...)` delegate to the same
 emission path. Rust exposes `Engine::reset_theme` / `set_color_scheme` (and
 `replace_theme` / `replace_adaptive_theme`).

 ## 8. Kotlin DSL realization (adopted)
 
 The JVM reference DSL is Kotlin (`dev.pathland.view.dsl`). It is surface-complete
 and shares the canonical contract in [§4](#4-view-surface) and
 [§5](#5-modifier-surface).
 
 | Canonical | Kotlin |
 |-----------|--------|
 | `Text("…")` | `Text("…")` (String or `Signal<String>`) |
 | `Button("…", action)` | `Button("…") { action() }` |
 | `Toggle("label", isOn: writable)` | `Toggle(label = "…", isOn = writable)` |
 | `Slider(value: in:)` | `Slider(value, 0f..100f)` |
 | `.border(color, width)` | `.border(color, width = 2f)` |
 | `DatePicker(selection:)` | `DatePicker(selection, DatePickerMode.DATE)` |
 | `VStack(spacing: 8) { … }` | `VStack(spacing = 8f) { … }` |
 | `.frame(width:height:)` | `.frame(width = 100f, height = 24f)` |
 | `.padding(16)` | `.padding(16f)` |
 | `.foregroundStyle(.red)` | `.foregroundStyle(Color.RED)` |
 | `if/else` in a result builder | plain `if`/`when` in `body()` |
 | `Router` + `NavigationContainer` | `navigator { route(...) }` + `NavigationStack(router)` |
 | `content.modifier(Card())` | `content.modifiers(Card())` (custom `ViewModifier`) |
 
 - **`Component` owns composite bodies**: a signal read in `body()` subscribes the
   component; a later write re-renders only that component and diffs its subtree.
 - **Persisted state**: `val count by state(0)` / `state(0, "key")`, bound to the
   session's `PersistentState` before the first `body()` render.
 - **Styles** are Kotlin values: `PlainButtonStyle`, `BorderedButtonStyle`,
   label styles, `NativeVideoStyle`.
 - **Java hosting**: a Java Spring Boot/Quarkus app mounts a Kotlin view through a
   `PathlandApp` bean; Kotlin roots expose a public constructor or
   `@JvmStatic make(...)`.
 
 ## 9. Generation contract for a new language
 
 An AI (or a human) generating a Pathland DSL in a new language MUST produce the
 following and verify each item. This is a checklist; the authoritative details
 are the companion specs.
 
 ### 9.1 Required surface
 
 - [ ] **Views/controls** — every entry of [§4](#4-view-surface):
   `Text`, `Image`, `Color`, `Shape` (all `ShapeKind`s), `Divider`, `Spacer`,
   `ProgressView`, `Gauge`; `VStack`, `HStack`, `ZStack`, `Grid`, `GridRow`,
   `ScrollView`,
   `LazyVGrid`, `LazyHGrid`, `LazyVStack`, `LazyHStack`; `Button`,
   `TextField`, `SecureField`, `TextEditor`, `Toggle`, `Slider`, `Stepper`,
   `Picker`, `Menu`, `DatePicker`, `ColorPicker`.
 - [ ] **The three operations** — configure values, apply modifiers, supply
   children — available at creation or by chaining, in any order
   ([§2](#2-canonical-signature-notation)). Each language maps them to its idiom
   ([§9.3](#93-language-adaptation-rules)).
 - [ ] **Modifiers** — every entry of [§5](#5-modifier-surface), applicable to
   any view, innermost-first, emitting one property per underlying argument; a
   modifier's type carries no `Mod` suffix.
 - [ ] **Custom modifiers / unified mechanism** — a `ViewModifier` authoring
   surface (`body(content) -> View`) + a chainable `modifiers(...)` operation on
   **any** view; **core modifiers are implemented through the same mechanism**,
   never a separate syntax ([§5.6](#56-custom-modifiers-developer-authored)).
 - [ ] **Shared config with styles** — a style's `makeBody(Config)` receives the
   same config type the control configured via `make(...)`
   ([§5.7](#57-styleable-controls-the-style-contract)).
 - [ ] **Signals** — `signal`, `computed`, `effect`, `untracked`,
   `get`/`set`/`update`/`asReadonly`, with equality suppression, synchronous
   flush, glitch-free propagation, error caching, write discipline, circular
   detection ([§3.1](#31-signal-surface)).
 - [ ] **Two-way bindings** — every value control takes a writable signal (a
   config value) and exposes a sink the host routes its event into
   ([§3.2](#32-two-way-binding)).
 - [ ] **Persisted state** — `State<T>` keyed fields (or the language's
   equivalent wiring) against a platform-neutral store ([§3.3](#33-persisted-state-statet)).
 - [ ] **Gestures** — `.onTapGesture` (composed from raw pointer down/up) and
   raw `pointerEvents`/`EVENT_LISTENERS` bitmask ([§4.4](#44-gestures)).
 - [ ] **Structural reactivity (reactive bodies)** — a signal read in a
   component body (`if`/`switch`/`for`, or the language's equivalent) re-renders
   that component and reconciles it into `TREE` deltas with zero opcodes for
   identical structure; `View.of` is the inline supplier form
   ([§3.4](#34-structural-reactivity-reactive-bodies--slots)).
 - [ ] **Reactive lists** — `ForEach` over a static list or a
   `Signal<List<T>>`, each item a child component slot; static lists MAY use
   native iteration instead ([§3.4](#34-structural-reactivity-reactive-bodies--slots),
   [§9.3.1](#931-cross-language-reactive-vocabulary)).
 - [ ] **Navigation** — `Router` / `RouteTable` / `NavigationContainer` /
   `NavigationLink` over a plain `Signal<Route>`, the initial route host-seeded
   before mount, emitting `ROUTE` and `TRANSITION` and consuming the `NAVIGATE`
   event ([§4.5](#45-navigation)).
 - [ ] **Design tokens & theming** — a token surface: token-typed values usable
   in style modifiers (a `Color` accepting a token path, e.g. `Color.token("color.primary")`
   or the language's equivalent), a theme/override helper emitting
   `PARAMETER::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` (base values + `dark.`-prefixed dark values), and
   the **base=light / `dark.*`** color-scheme convention with renderer-derived
   scheme detection — see [§7](#7-theme-management) and [TOKENS.md](./TOKENS.md).
 
 ### 9.2 Mapping rules (signature → protocol)
 
 1. Each view/control maps to its **fixed component id** in PRIMITIVES.md.
    Application/custom component types live in `0x0100`–`0xFFFF`; a DSL must
    never reuse allocated ids.
 2. Each modifier maps to the **documented property id(s)** in MODIFIERS.md
    with the documented **value type** (U8/U32/I32/F32/STRING/ENUM/COLOR/
    DESIGN_TOKEN). Enumerated values use the numeric codes in MODIFIERS.md's
    appendix.
 3. `Color` values pack as sRGB `0xAARRGGBB`. A **token-typed** value instead
    carries the `DESIGN_TOKEN` value type with the token path in the arena
    (never a packed literal); the renderer resolves it against the current
    scheme. A theme/override helper emits `PARAMETER::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN`
    (`A` = arenaRef path, `B` = valueType, `C` = value); a `dark.`-prefixed path
    supplies the dark design (base = light — [TOKENS.md](./TOKENS.md)).
 4. `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` sentinels: `FILL` = −1.0, `HUG_CONTENT` = −2.0.
 5. `Grid` counts map to the **config values** `GRID_COLUMNS` (`0x001E`) /
    `GRID_ROWS` (`0x001F`): a positive `int` count emits a positive F32; absent =
    auto-fit. A **`List<GridItem>`** value serializes to the **`GRID_TRACKS`**
    (`0x0020`, STRING) per-track spec, which takes precedence over the counts. A
    `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` frame on a grid is the grid's **box**, never a count
    ([§4.2](#42-layout--container-nodes)).
 6. `DatePicker` value/event use the two-field encoding **days since epoch
    (I32) + millis of day (U32)**; there is no `DATE_VALUE` property.
 7. Value/text/date events are gated by the transport-aware event guards; the
    DSL's controls emit the `ACTION_ID`/`BINDING_ID`/`EVENT_LISTENERS` that
    declare intent.
 8. Emission is **diff-based and reactive**: the DSL describes values, the
    emitter diffs. A generated DSL must keep the retained tree + emitter
    separation; it must not hand-serialize full trees.
 
 ### 9.3 Language adaptation rules
 
 **The three operations are normative; their spellings are not.** A conformant
 DSL MUST expose *configure values*, *apply modifiers*, and *supply children*,
 each available at creation or by chaining (any order), mapped to the host
 language's idioms. The canonical (SwiftUI-shaped) spelling is
 `Text("x").padding(16)`; Java spells values `make(...)` (views) / lowercase
 functions (modifiers) and chains `modifiers(...)` / `children(...)`.
 
 | Aspect | Java | Rust | Go | Python |
 |--------|------|------|----|--------|
 | configure values | `make(c -> …)` (views) / `padding(c -> …)` (modifiers) | `Type::new(config)` / `with(\|c\| …)` | ctor + options | kwargs / `configure(…)` |
 | single-value shortcut | `make(value)` / `padding(value)` (sugar for the lambda) | `Type::new(value)` / `Type(sig)` | `Type(val)` | `Type(val=…)` / `Type(sig)` |
 | apply modifiers | `.modifiers(…)` | `.modifiers(…)` (single or tuple) | `.Modifiers(…)` | `.modifiers(…)` |
 | supply children | `.children(…)` | `.children(vec![…])` / `vstack![…]` | ctor args / `.Children(…)` | `.children(*v)` |
 | creation + chaining | static on the view; chain on the returned builder | associated fn `Type::new`; chain via a **trait** + macros | package ctor; chain via methods | kwargs + methods |
 | same-name static + chain | **builder split** (static on class, chain on builder) | assoc fn + trait method | package func + method (not type-scoped) | **not expressible** (methods are last-wins) |
 | `with` name legal | yes | yes | yes | **no** — `with` is a keyword → kwargs / `configure` |
 | varargs children | yes | no — slices/arrays or macros | `...` | `*args` |
 | value *is* the modifier | enum OK | enum OK | typed const + method OK | enum member with `apply` OK |
 
 Rules:
 
 - A language that cannot express "static-or-chained under one name" (Python)
   MUST still offer the three operations — value configuration via kwargs /
   `configure(...)`, modifiers and children via chainable methods.
 - A language whose enums cannot implement the modifier interface MUST supply an
   equivalent single-value modifier form.
 - **Reactive values are config members, in every language.** A config member
   accepts a raw value or a signal ([§2](#2-canonical-signature-notation)). Rust
   realizes this with `impl Into<Reactive<T>>` on each builder setter
   (`Reactive<T> { Static(T), Signal(SignalId) }`); the former `Bound` /
   `*.bound` modifier surface is folded into it and **removed**.
 - Names are recommendations; semantics
   ([§1](#1-design-principles-dsl-flavored)) are the contract.
 
 #### 9.3.1 Cross-language reactive vocabulary
 
 The **names and semantics** are shared; the syntax is the host language's.
 Swift is the canonical SwiftUI-shaped reference. Java spells the non-native
 helpers as `View.of` / `ForEach.of`; Kotlin and TypeScript use their native
 expression and collection forms; Rust parity is Phase 2.
 
 | Concept | Swift | Java | Kotlin | Rust | TypeScript |
 |---------|-------|------|--------|------|------------|
 | Component render | `var body: some View` | `View body()` | `View body()` | `fn build(&self)` | `body(props)` |
 | Signal read | `count` (`@State`), `signal.value` | `sig.get()` | `sig.value` / `sig()` | `sig.get()` | `sig()` |
 | Branch | `if`/`switch` in `@ViewBuilder` | `if`/`switch` in `body()`; `View.of(() -> …)` inline | `if`/`when` expressions | `if`/`match` expressions | ternary / `switch` expressions |
 | Inline subtree | `Group { … }` / `@ViewBuilder` | `View.of(() -> …)` | `View.of { … }` (rarely needed) | `View::of(\|\| …)` | `View.of(() => …)` |
 | Static list | `ForEach(items) { … }` / `for` in a builder | stream/`for` + `.children(…)` | `items.map { … }` + `.children(…)` | iterator + `.children(vec![…])` | `items.map(…)` |
 | Reactive list | `ForEach(items) { … }` | `ForEach.of(items, (item, i) -> …)` | `ForEach(items) { item, i -> … }` | `ForEach::of(items, \|item, i\| …)` | `ForEach(items, (item, i) => …)` |
 | Children | trailing closure | `.children(a, b)` | `.children(a, b)` / trailing lambda | `.children(vec![a, b])` | `children: [a, b]` |
 | Values | `VStack(spacing: 8)` | `VStack.make(v -> v.spacing(8))` | `VStack(spacing = 8)` | `VStack::new(\|v\| v.spacing(8.0))` | `VStack({ spacing: 8 })` |
 | Modifiers | `.padding(16)` / `.modifiers(…)` | `.modifiers(padding(16))` | `.modifiers(padding(16))` | `.modifiers(padding(16.0))` | `.modifiers(padding(16))` |
 | State | `@State` / `@Binding` | `State<T>` / `WritableSignal<T>` | `State<T>` / `WritableSignal<T>` | `State<T>` / `WritableSignal<T>` | `State<T>` / `WritableSignal<T>` |
 | Environment | `@Environment` | `Environment.value(key)` | `Environment.value(key)` | `Environment` | `useAppContext()` / `Environment` |
 
 Canonical examples:
 
 ```swift
 struct LibraryView: View {
     let tracks: [Track]
     @Binding var trackIndex: Int
 
     var body: some View {
         VStack(spacing: 8) {
             Text("Library")
             ForEach(tracks) { track in
                 TrackRow(track: track, trackIndex: $trackIndex)
             }
         }
     }
 }
 ```
 
 ```java
 VStack.make(v -> v.spacing(8)).children(
     Text.make("Library"),
     ForEach.of(tracks, (track, index) -> TrackRowView.make(r -> r
         .track(track)
         .index(index)
         .trackIndex(trackIndex))));
 ```
 
 ```kotlin
 VStack(spacing = 8) {
     Text("Library")
     ForEach(tracks) { track, index ->
         TrackRow(TrackRowProps(track, index, trackIndex))
     }
 }
 ```
 
 ```rust
 VStack::new(|v| v.spacing(8.0)).children(vec![
     Text::new("Library").into(),
     ForEach::of(tracks.clone(), |track, index| {
         TrackRow::new(track, index, track_index.clone()).into()
     }),
 ])
 ```
 
 ```ts
 VStack({ spacing: 8 }, [
   Text({ text: "Library" }),
   ForEach(tracks, (track, index) =>
     TrackRow({ track, index, trackIndex })),
 ])
 ```
 
 Rules:
 
 - **Use native control flow** where the language has it. `View.of` is the Java
   inline form because Java has no `if` expression; Swift/Kotlin/Rust/TypeScript
   use their own `if`/`switch`/`when`/`match`/ternary forms.
 - **Use native iteration for static lists.** `ForEach` is the reactive
   (component-scoped) list; static lists MAY use streams/`map`/`for` directly.
 - **Keep the anchors**: `View`, `Signal`, `computed`, `effect`, `State`,
   `ForEach`, `View.of`, `children`, `modifiers`. These are what make the DSLs
   recognizable; casing and construction follow the host language.
 - **`(item, index)` order** for `ForEach`, matching JavaScript `map` and Java
   `BiFunction`; Kotlin/Rust authors may name the lambda parameters.
 - **No keys yet.** The emitter reconciles by position + type; a keyed `ForEach`
   is a future protocol/emitter feature, not a syntax difference.
 - **Gaps**: Rust reactive-body/`ForEach` parity is Phase 2; the TypeScript plan
   currently defers structural reactivity; Swift is not implemented yet. Kotlin is
-  implemented by `lib/java/pathland-view-kotlin` (Kotlin-owned views over core;
+  implemented by `lib/java/pathland-view-core` (Kotlin-owned views over the engine;
   `Text("…")`, `VStack(spacing = 8) { … }`, `.padding(16)`), with its surface and
   gaps tracked in that module's `status.md`.
 
 ### 9.4 Conformance recipe
 
 A generated DSL is verified by proving it **emits the same bytes** as the
 reference implementations:
 
 1. Port the golden vectors in [CONFORMANCE.md](./CONFORMANCE.md) into the new
    DSL's test harness; assert byte-identical `TREE`/`PARAMETER`/`EVENT`/`META`
    opcodes for each canonical element.
 2. Port the Java `EmitterTest` cases (mount → `SET_TEXT`/`SET_PROPERTY`/`SET_DATE`
    deltas; unchanged tree → zero opcodes; two-way routing: `TEXT_CHANGED`,
    `VALUE_CHANGED`, `DATE_CHANGED` write into the bound signal).
 3. Verify the no-heap-allocation steady-state property where the target
    language supports it (the Rust engine proves zero dynamic allocations during
    steady-state emission).
 4. Cross-check every referenced id against PRIMITIVES.md/MODIFIERS.md/EVENTS.md
    (the specs are the source of truth, never the reference code).
 
-**Reference implementations to read**: Kotlin — `lib/java/pathland-view-kotlin`
-(the DSL: `dev.pathland.view.dsl`) + `lib/java/pathland-view-core`
-(`dev.pathland.view.core*` + `dev.pathland.view.engine`); Rust —
+**Reference implementations to read**: Kotlin — `lib/java/pathland-view-core`
+(the DSL: `dev.pathland.view.dsl`, plus `dev.pathland.view.core*` and
+`dev.pathland.view.engine`); Rust —
 `lib/rust/crates/pathland-view` + `pathland-engine` + `pathland-core::signal`.

 ([§2](#2-canonical-signature-notation),
 [§5.6](#56-custom-modifiers-developer-authored)); built-in and
 application-authored modifiers share the same `modifiers(...)` surface.
 
 **Status deltas captured by this table**: the Kotlin DSL is surface-complete with
 the three operations, modifiers as values via `.modifiers(...)` (no sugar on
 `View`), and styles as modifiers; **every value member carries a raw + `Signal<T>`
 form** (uniform signals-first configs, so any property — layout included — can
 react); the Rust DSL now exposes the surface plus
 **signals** — value, computed (lazy/memoized/equality-suppressed), and effect
 signals in a shared `no_std` runtime (`Signal<T>`/`WritableSignal<T>`,
 `Engine::signal`/`computed`/`effect`/`read`/`set`) with text/property binding —
 **two-way control bindings** (input sinks collected with
 `collect_input_handlers`) and **actions** (`Button::action`), plus
 **styles + environment** (a subtree `Environment` threaded through
 `View::build_env`, `ButtonStyle` applied with `ViewExt::button_style`),
 **structural reactivity + navigation** (`RouteTable`,
 `Router`, `NavigationContainer`, `NavigationLink`), and **persisted state**
 (a `StateStore` trait + `PersistentState::state` auto-load/auto-save). Both are
 per-project implementation status tracked in each project's `status.md`.
 
 ---
 
 ## Conformance
 
 - The wire footprint of every DSL element above is defined by the golden
   vectors in [CONFORMANCE.md](./CONFORMANCE.md). A new DSL element MUST add
   vectors before any implementation depends on it.
 - Component ids: [PRIMITIVES.md](./PRIMITIVES.md); property ids and value
   types: [MODIFIERS.md](./MODIFIERS.md); event ids and listener bits:
   [EVENTS.md](./EVENTS.md). These specs are the single source of truth.
 - The v3 authoring surface (`make` + lowercase modifier functions,
   config-with-styles, no `Mod` suffix, single-value shortcuts) is a
   **source-surface** change only: it emits the **same bytes** as the prior
   v2 `.of(...)` / `with(...)` surface for an equivalent tree — no
   component/property/event/opcode change.

===================================================================
--- spec/ENGINE.md	
+++ spec/ENGINE.md	
@@ -1,205 +1,205 @@
 # Pathland Engine Semantics
 
 **Status:** Draft
 **Wire protocol version:** 1
 **Last Updated:** November 1, 2026
 
 `OPCODE.md` defines the 16-byte wire format. `CONFORMANCE.md` defines individual
 opcode byte vectors. This document defines the **retained-tree engine behavior**
 that produces frames: what gets emitted, in what order, and what must emit
 nothing.
 
 The shared trace fixtures live in [`engine-traces/`](./engine-traces/). They are
 self-contained PLPL batches (opcodes + frame strings), emitted by the canonical
 Rust engine and compared byte-for-byte by the JVM engine test.
 
 ---
 
 ## 1. Scope
 
 The engine:
 
 - owns the application's retained tree and signal bindings;
 - compares the current tree with the last emitted snapshot;
 - emits only the `TREE` / `PARAMETER` deltas needed to reach the current tree;
 - never computes layout and never emits rectangles.
 
 The renderer owns native elements, layout, styling defaults, and input
 recognition.
 
 ---
 
 ## 2. Terms
 
 | Term | Meaning |
 |------|---------|
 | **Mount** | First emission of a tree. Emits the complete structure and content. |
 | **Snapshot** | A full re-emission of the current tree (`META::RESYNC` / reconnect). |
 | **Delta** | Opcodes for nodes that changed since the previous emission. |
 | **Frame** | One bounded batch of opcodes plus its string data. |
 | **Zero-op** | A recompute that emits no opcodes and produces no new frame. |
 
 A renderer may receive any number of deltas after the initial mount/snapshot.
 It must converge to the same rendered tree as a fresh snapshot of the same
 retained tree.
 
 ---
 
 ## 3. Node identity
 
 Node ids are assigned **pre-order**, root first, starting at `1`.
 
 ```text
 VStack(id=1)
 ├── Text(id=2)
 └── Text(id=3)
 ```
 
 Rules:
 
 - A frame MUST NOT contain two nodes with the same id.
 - Structural reconciliation keeps ids stable for position+type-stable nodes.
 - A removed node gets `TREE::DELETE_NODE`.
 - A new node gets `TREE::CREATE_NODE`.
 - A child relationship is established with `TREE::INSERT_CHILD`.
 - `MEDIA_CONTROLLER` nodes keep their **pinned** playback id across subtree
   re-emissions (spec/MEDIA.md).
 
 ---
 
 ## 4. Canonical mount order
 
 For each node, before its children:
 
 1. `TREE::CREATE_NODE`
 2. `TREE::INSERT_CHILD` (when the node has a parent)
 3. node properties (`PARAMETER::SET_PROPERTY`, including token/string/list
    properties)
 4. node text (`PARAMETER::SET_TEXT`) and date (`PARAMETER::SET_DATE`)
 5. recurse into children, in child order
 
 The child is attached **before** its own content/properties, so an id-keyed
 renderer can create and place the native element before applying content.
 
 The trace fixtures assert this order. Property ordering within a node is
 deterministic and follows the engine's stored property order.
 
 ---
 
 ## 5. Reactive emission
 
 The engine records which nodes read each signal during emission:
 
 - a text binding (`node.text_binding`);
 - a property binding (`node.property_bindings`);
 - a string-property binding (`node.string_bindings`).
 
 When a signal changes, only the bound nodes re-emit:
 
 - text → `PARAMETER::SET_TEXT`
 - property → `PARAMETER::SET_PROPERTY`
 - string property → `PARAMETER::SET_PROPERTY` with the `STRING` value type
 
 An unrelated signal change emits nothing. A write that does not change the
 signal value emits nothing.
 
 ### Zero-op recompute
 
 An unchanged tree or unchanged signal MUST emit **zero** opcodes and MUST NOT
 produce a new frame. This is the steady-state contract that makes the ring
 zero-allocation during idle re-renders.
 
 ---
 
 ## 6. Structural deltas
 
 When a tree changes structurally:
 
 | Change | Required opcodes |
 |--------|------------------|
 | Node added | `CREATE_NODE` + `INSERT_CHILD` + node content |
 | Node removed | `REMOVE_CHILD` (when parented) + `DELETE_NODE` |
 | Child reordered | `MOVE_CHILD` (same node ids) |
 | Parent changed | remove from old parent + insert under new parent |
 
 The engine does not resend unchanged subtrees. A structural change that leaves
 a descendant identical emits no descendant opcodes.
 
 ---
 
 ## 7. Fit, media, navigation
 
 These are engine-owned surfaces with the same diff discipline:
 
 - **`SIZE_THAT_FITS`**: only the selected candidate is normally transmitted;
   snapshot/SSR emission may include every candidate for first paint.
   `FIT_CHANGED` re-renders only the fit component.
 - **Media**: one non-visual `MEDIA_CONTROLLER` node per controller, stable id;
   registered controllers are pinned as root children (so audio needs no view),
   and a `VIDEO` surface references its controller via `MEDIA_CONTROLLER_ID`.
   Transport changes emit only the changed controller property.
 - **Navigation**: a `NavigationContainer` is an ordinary tracked component; a
   route change re-renders only its destination slot.
 
 Detailed wire contracts remain in `PRIMITIVES.md`, `MEDIA.md`, and `DSL.md`.
 
 ---
 
 ## 8. Shared engine traces
 
 Fixtures live under `spec/engine-traces/<scenario>/<step>.plpl.hex`.
 
 - Each file is one **self-contained PLPL batch** (`FrameCodec` format).
 - The hex is lowercase; comments start with `#`.
 - The batch includes the opcode list and the exact frame string table.
 - The fixture is emitted by the canonical Rust engine and compared byte-for-byte
   by the JVM engine test.
 
 ### Current scenarios
 
 | Scenario | Steps | Covers |
 |----------|-------|--------|
 | `mount_text_stack` | `000-mount` | Create/insert order, `SPACING`, `SET_TEXT` |
 | `signal_text_delta` | `000-mount`, `001-set-text` | Mount + text-signal delta only |
 | `property_signal_delta` | `000-mount`, `001-set-spacing` | Mount + property-signal delta only |
 | `styled_text_mount` | `000-mount` | Property-before-text emission order |
 | `structural_add_remove` | `000-mount`, `001-add-child`, `002-remove-child` | Create/insert append, remove+delete |
 
 ### Generate
 
 From `lib/rust`:
 
 ```bash
 cargo run -p pathland-engine-golden -- --emit
 ```
 
 ### Verify
 
 ```bash
 cd lib/rust && cargo run -p pathland-engine-golden -- --check
-cd lib/java && mvn -q -pl pathland-view-kotlin -am test -Dtest=EngineTraceTest
+cd lib/java && mvn -q -pl pathland-view-core -am test -Dtest=EngineTraceTest
 ```
 
 CI regenerates the fixtures from Rust and fails on drift; the Java reactor runs
 `EngineTraceTest` as part of `mvn test`.
 
 ### Adding a scenario
 
 1. Add the scenario to `pathland-engine-golden`.
 2. Run `--emit` and commit the new fixtures with the behavior change.
 3. Add the equivalent scenario to the JVM `EngineTraceTest`.
 4. Update the table above.
 
 ---
 
 ## 9. Not covered yet
 
 The trace set is intentionally small at this stage. Future traces should cover:
 
 - structural insert/remove/move deltas;
 - unchanged recompute (zero-op) as a frame-level fixture;
 - design-token and string/list property deltas;
 - window metadata and theme frames;
 - fit-slot selection and snapshot emission;
 - media transport changes;
 - navigation destination swaps.

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<project xmlns="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0"
         xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
         xsi:schemaLocation="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0 http://maven.apache.org/xsd/maven-4.0.0.xsd">
    <modelVersion>4.0.0</modelVersion>

    <parent>
        <groupId>dev.pathland</groupId>
        <artifactId>pathland-parent</artifactId>
        <version>0.1.5</version>
    </parent>

    <artifactId>pathland-demo-views-kotlin</artifactId>
    <packaging>jar</packaging>

    <!-- Demo application — not published to Maven Central. -->
    <properties>
        <maven.deploy.skip>true</maven.deploy.skip>
        <maven.javadoc.skip>true</maven.javadoc.skip>
    </properties>

    <name>Pathland Demo Views Kotlin</name>
    <description>
        Kotlin-owned demo views shared by the desktop and web demos, starting with
        the app-driven MusicPlayerView. Depends only on pathland-view-core,
        pathland-view-kotlin, and the DSL-neutral demo assets.
    </description>

    <dependencies>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>dev.pathland</groupId>
            <artifactId>pathland-view-core</artifactId>
            <version>${project.version}</version>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>dev.pathland</groupId>
            <artifactId>pathland-view-kotlin</artifactId>
            <version>${project.version}</version>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>dev.pathland</groupId>
            <artifactId>pathland-demo-common</artifactId>
            <version>${project.version}</version>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.jetbrains.kotlin</groupId>
            <artifactId>kotlin-stdlib</artifactId>
            <version>${kotlin.version}</version>
        </dependency>

                    <languageVersion>2.4</languageVersion>

# pathland-demo-views-kotlin — implementation status

**Last updated:** November 3, 2026

Kotlin-owned demo views over `pathland-view-kotlin`, with no Java-DSL dependency.
It owns the app-driven music player and the small sponsored-proxy ad app.

## Structure

- `music/` — the root `MusicPlayerView` (public, Java-mountable).
- `music/model/` — `Track`, `Lyrics`.
- `music/library/` — `LibraryView`, `TrackRowView`.
- `music/player/` — `PlayerMainArea`, `PlayerBar`, `PlayerControls`,
  `TransportControls`, `TrackInfoView`, `VolumeControls`.
- `music/player/controls/` — `SeekControl`, `PercentSeek`, `VolumeControl`.
- `music/service/` — `MediaPlayerService`: per-session player state, playlist,
  `MediaController`, and the environment key shared by the views.
- `music/lyrics/` — `SubtitlePill`.
- `music/sidebar/` — `NowPlayingSidebar`, `UpNextRowView`.
- `ad/` — `AdView`.

## Implemented

- **`MusicPlayerView`** — Apple Music-style root: one root `SizeThatFits`
  selects narrow (no volume), medium (volume), or wide (volume + `NowPlayingSidebar`),
  with the floating `PlayerBar`.
- **Persisted player state** — owned by `MediaPlayerService` (`player.position`, `player.playing`,
  `player.track`, `player.volume`, `player.seekRequest`, `player.volumeRequest`)
  and created with `Signals.state` while the framework's session state is active.
- **App-driven media** — `MediaPlayerService` owns and registers the
  `MediaController`, and the emitter projects it as a pinned root node; every fit
  candidate shares the same controller. `MEDIA_*` reports feed position/volume
  and `MEDIA_ENDED` advances the track.
- **Seek/volume decoupling** — `SeekControl` buffers drags and commits on release;
  `PercentSeek` maps seconds to 0..100; `VolumeControl` separates report from
  command (each in its own file under `player/controls/`).
- **Lyrics** — synchronized two-line karaoke pill driven by the parsed SRT cues.
- **Window metadata** — track-derived title/description and `locale("en")`.
- **Sponsored proxy** — optional `adUrl` appends a `ProxyView` in the sidebar.
- **`AdView`** — the small sponsored-proxy origin app: a title, a button, and a
  persisted click counter (`ad.clicks`), fully Kotlin-owned and Java-mountable.
- **Accessibility** — transport labels, slider labels, `MAIN`/`HEADER` roles.

## Verified by

`mvn test -pl pathland-demo-views-kotlin` — `LyricsTest`, `SeekControlTest`,
`MediaPlayerServiceTest` (persisted keys, select/next/previous), `MusicPlayerViewTest`
(tree/render, fit swaps, media state, seek echo guard, snapshot emission, sponsored
proxy), and `AdViewTest` (button click / persisted counter delta).

import com.sun.jna.Memory
import dev.pathland.demo.DemoTheme
import dev.pathland.demo.assets.DemoAssets
import dev.pathland.demo.music.MusicPlayerView
import dev.pathland.view.core.Environment
import dev.pathland.view.core.ffm.PathlandCore
import dev.pathland.view.core.ffm.RingOpcodeSink
import dev.pathland.view.core.signal.Signals
import dev.pathland.view.core.state.InMemoryStateStore
import dev.pathland.view.core.state.PersistentState
import dev.pathland.view.engine.Emitter
import dev.pathland.view.engine.InputDispatcher

/**
 * Runs the shared Kotlin [MusicPlayerView] under the native Qt Quick renderer.
 *
 * The Kotlin DSL mounts the view through the fine-grained [Emitter] into a
 * `libpathland_core` shared ring ([RingOpcodeSink], zero-copy). The in-process
 * Qt renderer pumps the same ring in place (`pathland_qt_run_ring`); native
 * inputs round-trip as `EVENT` opcodes that this host drains and dispatches
 * through [InputDispatcher] into the app's bindings.
 *
 * No Swing, no Qt API — only Pathland authoring.
 */
object QtHost {

    /** Max events drained per wake (× 16 bytes each). */
    private const val MAX_EVENTS = 64
    private const val WINDOW_WIDTH = 1180
    private const val WINDOW_HEIGHT = 800

    @JvmStatic
    fun main(args: Array<String>) {
        val core = PathlandCore.instance()
        RingOpcodeSink(core).use { sink ->
            val handle = sink.handle()

            // The session's state + theme, exactly as the server session seeds them.
            val state = PersistentState(InMemoryStateStore(), "desktop")
            // A placeholder host path signal: MusicPlayerView has no router.
            val activePath = Signals.signal("/")

            val emitter = Emitter(sink, DemoTheme.adaptive())
            val result = emitter.mount(MusicPlayerView.make(), Environment(state))
            val dispatcher = InputDispatcher(result, activePath)
            val reader = RingEventReader(core.ringPtr(handle), core.ringLen(handle))

            // Wake callback: drain raw EVENT opcodes and route them into the app's
            // bindings. Re-emission happens on the Qt main thread, the only writer.
            val onEvent = QtRendererNative.EventCallback {
                val buf = Memory(MAX_EVENTS.toLong() * 16)
                val n = core.drainEvents(handle, buf, MAX_EVENTS)
                if (n > 0) {
                    dispatcher.dispatch(reader.decode(buf.getByteArray(0, n * 16)))
                }
            }

            val renderer = QtRendererNative.instance()
            renderer.setAssetRoot(DemoAssets.extractToTemp().toString())

            // Blocks until the window closes; the ring (handle) must outlive it.
            renderer.runRing(core.ringMut(handle), onEvent, WINDOW_WIDTH, WINDOW_HEIGHT)
        }
    }

package dev.pathland.demo.qt

import com.sun.jna.Callback
import com.sun.jna.Library
import com.sun.jna.Native
import com.sun.jna.Pointer
import java.io.File
import java.util.Locale

/**
 * JNA binding to the Rust Qt renderer cdylib (`libpathland_qt`).
 *
 * The Kotlin DSL emits opcodes into a `libpathland_core` ring
 * ([dev.pathland.view.core.ffm.RingOpcodeSink]); [runRing] hands that borrowed
 * ring to the in-process Qt Quick renderer (`pathland_qt_run_ring`), which pumps
 * it in place. Native inputs are reported back through a no-payload callback;
 * the host drains them from the ring itself.
 */
class QtRendererNative private constructor() {

    /** Invoked (with no payload) on the Qt main thread after a raw input was written. */
    fun interface EventCallback : Callback {
        fun invoke()
    }

    /** The C ABI surface, mapped by JNA onto the Rust cdylib. */
    interface NativeQtRenderer : Library {
        fun pathland_qt_set_asset_root(dir: String)
        fun pathland_qt_run_ring(ring: Pointer, onEvent: EventCallback?, width: Int, height: Int)
    }

    private val nativeQt: NativeQtRenderer

    init {
        val libraryPath = resolveLibraryPath()
            ?: throw IllegalStateException(
                "libpathland_qt not found; set -Dpathland.qt.lib to its full path " +
                    "(cargo build -p pathland-render-qt)",
            )
        nativeQt = Native.load(libraryPath, NativeQtRenderer::class.java)
    }

    /**
     * Set the directory that web-style `/_pathland/...` media/image source paths
     * resolve against. Call before [runRing]; an empty value clears it.
     */
    fun setAssetRoot(dir: String) {
        nativeQt.pathland_qt_set_asset_root(dir)
    }

    /**
     * Run the Qt renderer over the borrowed ring. Blocks until the Qt event loop
     * exits. On macOS the JVM must run with `-XstartOnFirstThread`.
     */
    fun runRing(ring: Pointer, onEvent: EventCallback?, width: Int, height: Int) {
        nativeQt.pathland_qt_run_ring(ring, onEvent, width, height)
    }

    companion object {
        private val INSTANCE: QtRendererNative by lazy { QtRendererNative() }

        /** The process-wide binding; lazily links `libpathland_qt` on first call. */
        fun instance(): QtRendererNative = INSTANCE

        /** Resolve the native library's full path (system property, then `java.library.path`). */
        internal fun resolveLibraryPath(): String? {
            val override = System.getProperty("pathland.qt.lib")
            if (override != null) return override
            val fileName = "libpathland_qt" + platformLibraryExtension()
            val libraryPath = System.getProperty("java.library.path") ?: return null
            for (dir in libraryPath.split(File.pathSeparator)) {
                val candidate = File(dir, fileName)
                if (candidate.isFile) return candidate.absolutePath
            }
            return null
        }

        private fun platformLibraryExtension(): String {
            val os = System.getProperty("os.name", "").lowercase(Locale.ROOT)
            if (os.contains("mac")) return ".dylib"
            if (os.contains("win")) return ".dll"
            return ".so"
        }
    }
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Shared helpers for the Pathland demo scripts. Source this file; it defines
# $ROOT (the repository root) and the prerequisite-build helpers each demo uses.

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"

# Build the generated HTML base design and sync it into the renderer crate.
build_design() {
  if [[ ! -d "$ROOT/design/node_modules" ]]; then
    (cd "$ROOT/design" && npm ci)
  fi
  (cd "$ROOT/design" && npm run build)
  "$ROOT/scripts/sync-design-css.sh"
}

# Build the Rust HTML renderer cdylib (embedded in the Java pathland-render-html jar).
build_rust_html() {
  build_design
  (cd "$ROOT/lib/rust" && cargo build -p pathland-render-html)
}

# Build the Rust dylibs the desktop demos link: the core ring (libpathland_core)
# and the GTK4 renderer (libpathland_gtk).
build_gtk_dylibs() {
  (cd "$ROOT/lib/rust" && cargo build -p pathland-core-capi -p pathland-render-gtk)
}

# Build the Rust dylibs the Qt desktop demo links: the core ring

# pathland-gtk-demo (Java) — implementation status

**Last updated:** November 3, 2026

Runs the shared Kotlin `MusicPlayerView` (`dev.pathland.demo.music` from
`pathland-demo-views-kotlin`) under the **native GTK4 renderer**
(`libpathland_gtk`) — the cross-language, shared-renderer story for Java. Protocol contract: `spec/`.

## How it works

- The Kotlin DSL mounts the view through its fine-grained `Emitter` into a
  `libpathland_core` shared ring (`RingOpcodeSink`, **zero-copy**).
- The in-process GTK renderer pumps the same ring in place
  (`pathland_gtk_run_ring`, via `PathlandCore.ringMut`); no
  `pathland-view-native` host is involved.
- Native inputs round-trip as `EVENT` opcodes that this host drains
  (`pathland_core_drain_events`) and dispatches into the app's bindings via the
  shared `InputDispatcher` (taps, text/value/date inputs, **media events**,
  router back).
- State/theme/platform seeding mirrors the server session: `PersistentState`
  over an `InMemoryStateStore`, `DemoTheme.adaptive()` as the emitter theme.
- **App-driven media**: the renderer plays the demo's tracks through a direct
  GStreamer `playbin` (driven by the node's media control properties) and
  reports `MEDIA_*` events back through the ring. The app's web-style
  `/_pathland/assets/...` paths are resolved against a local asset root: the
  demo extracts its audio + covers from the shared `pathland-demo-common` jar at
  startup (`DemoAssets.extractToTemp`) and calls `pathland_gtk_set_asset_root`.

## Implemented

- `GtkRendererNative` — JNA binding to `libpathland_gtk`
  (`pathland_gtk_run_ring(ring, on_event, width, height)` +
  `pathland_gtk_set_asset_root(dir)`); library resolved from the
  `pathland.gtk.lib` system property or `java.library.path`.
- `RingEventReader` — decodes raw ring `EVENT` opcodes into
  `dev.pathland.view.core.transport.Event`, resolving `TEXT_CHANGED`/`NAVIGATE`
  strings from the shared host → guest event arena (header `0x40`), plus the
  `MEDIA_*` events (play state, time, ended, volume, duration) and
  `FIT_CHANGED` (routed to the emitter's fit sink, so the `SizeThatFits` slot
  swaps to its wide candidate and the now-playing sidebar appears). Headless
  unit tests cover pointer/value/date/text/navigate/media/fit decoding and
  bounds behaviour.
- `GtkHost` (`main`) — mounts `MusicPlayerView` (the Apple Music-style player:
  library, now-playing sidebar, player bar with transport/seek/volume), extracts
  the demo's audio + covers to a runtime dir, sets the asset root, runs GTK
  (1180×800), drains and dispatches events. Blocks until the window closes.
- The `Emitter` sets `BINDING_ID` on bound controls for `RingOpcodeSink`s (the
  GTK renderer gates `TEXT_CHANGED`/`VALUE_CHANGED` on it).

## Not implemented / gaps

- **Playback requires GStreamer** with the mp3 decoding plugins installed (the
  brew `gstreamer` formula bundles them); without it the app runs but the
  pipeline errors on play.
- The GTK renderer's `attach_control_events` covers `TOGGLE`/`SLIDER`/
  `TEXT_FIELD`/`PICKER` only: `DATE_PICKER`, `STEPPER`, `COLOR_PICKER`, and
  `TEXT_EDITOR` render but do not (yet) emit events under GTK.
- macOS requires `-XstartOnFirstThread` (GTK owns the main thread).
- No automated GUI test (headless renderer tests live in `pathland-render-gtk`).

## Verified by

`mvn test -pl pathland-gtk-demo` — `RingEventReaderTest` (6 tests, headless, no
GTK). Manual: `GtkHost` boots the window and renders `MusicPlayerView` via the
shared ring; with GStreamer installed the pipeline reaches `PLAYING` and reports
`MEDIA_*` events (verified with a seeded `playing=true` run + `GST_DEBUG`). The
full Java reactor compiles with this module.===== QT STATUS
# pathland-qt-demo — implementation status

**Last updated:** November 3, 2026

Fully Kotlin JNA desktop demo: the shared Kotlin `MusicPlayerView` under the native
Qt Quick renderer (`libpathland_qt`), over the `libpathland_core` shared ring.

## Implemented

- **`QtHost`** — mounts the Kotlin music player through the emitter into the shared
  ring, seeds per-session state/theme, extracts the shared demo assets, and runs
  `pathland_qt_run_ring`; blocks until the window closes.
- **`QtRendererNative`** — JNA binding for `pathland_qt_run_ring` +
  `pathland_qt_set_asset_root`; resolves `pathland.qt.lib` or `java.library.path`.
- **`RingEventReader`** — decodes raw ring `EVENT` opcodes, event-arena strings,
  media events, and `FIT_CHANGED`.
- **Fully Kotlin host** — no Java DSL, no Swing/Qt API in app code.

## Not implemented / gaps

- Qt6 dev libraries are required to build/run the renderer.
- macOS needs `-XstartOnFirstThread`.
- No automated GUI test; the headless `RingEventReaderTest` covers decoding.

## Verified by

`mvn test -pl pathland-qt-demo` — `RingEventReaderTest` (5 tests). Manual:
`scripts/run-java-qt-demo.sh`.

input.content:
# pathland-desktop-demo — implementation status

**Last updated:** November 5, 2026

Runs the shared Kotlin `MusicPlayerView` (`dev.pathland.demo.music` from
`pathland-demo-views-kotlin`) under the **native GTK4 renderer**
(`libpathland_gtk`, `dev.pathland.demo.gtk.GtkHost`) or the **Qt Quick renderer**
(`libpathland_qt`, `dev.pathland.demo.qt.QtHost`) — the cross-language,
shared-renderer story. Protocol contract: `spec/`.

## How it works

- The Kotlin DSL mounts the view through its fine-grained `Emitter` into a
  `libpathland_core` shared ring (`RingOpcodeSink`, **zero-copy**).
- The in-process renderer pumps the same ring in place
  (`pathland_gtk_run_ring` / `pathland_qt_run_ring`); no
  `pathland-view-native` host is involved.
- Native inputs round-trip as `EVENT` opcodes that the host drains
  (`pathland_core_drain_events`) and dispatches into the app's bindings via the
  shared `InputDispatcher` (taps, text/value/date inputs, **media events**,
  router back).
- State/theme/platform seeding mirrors the server session: `PersistentState`
  over an `InMemoryStateStore`, `DemoTheme.adaptive()` as the emitter theme.
- **App-driven media**: the renderer plays the demo's tracks and reports
  `MEDIA_*` events back through the ring. The app's web-style
  `/_pathland/assets/...` paths resolve against a local asset root: the demo
  extracts its audio + covers from the shared `pathland-demo-views-kotlin` jar
  at startup (`DemoAssets.extractToTemp`) and calls the renderer's
  `set_asset_root`.

## Implemented

- **`GtkRendererNative`** — JNA binding to `libpathland_gtk`
  (`pathland_gtk_run_ring` + `pathland_gtk_set_asset_root`); library resolved
  from `pathland.gtk.lib` or `java.library.path`.
- **`QtRendererNative`** — JNA binding to `libpathland_qt`
  (`pathland_qt_run_ring` + `pathland_qt_set_asset_root`); library resolved
  from `pathland.qt.lib` or `java.library.path`.
- **`RingEventReader`** (shared, `dev.pathland.demo.desktop`) — decodes raw ring
  `EVENT` opcodes into `dev.pathland.view.core.transport.Event`, resolving
  `TEXT_CHANGED`/`NAVIGATE` strings from the shared host → guest event arena
  (header `0x40`), plus `MEDIA_*` and `FIT_CHANGED` (routed to the emitter's fit
  sink, so the `SizeThatFits` slot swaps to its wide candidate).
- **`GtkHost`** (`main`) — Java host; mounts the Apple Music-style player,
  extracts the demo assets, runs GTK (1180×800), drains and dispatches events.
- **`QtHost`** (`main`) — Kotlin host; mounts the player, extracts the demo
  assets, runs Qt Quick, drains and dispatches events.
- The `Emitter` sets `BINDING_ID` on bound controls for `RingOpcodeSink`s (the
  GTK renderer gates `TEXT_CHANGED`/`VALUE_CHANGED` on it).

## Not implemented / gaps

- **GTK playback requires GStreamer** with the mp3 decoding plugins installed;
  without it the app runs but the pipeline errors on play.
- The GTK renderer's `attach_control_events` covers `TOGGLE`/`SLIDER`/
  `TEXT_FIELD`/`PICKER` only: `DATE_PICKER`, `STEPPER`, `COLOR_PICKER`, and
  `TEXT_EDITOR` render but do not (yet) emit events under GTK.
- Qt6 dev libraries are required to build/run the Qt renderer.
- macOS requires `-XstartOnFirstThread` for both hosts.
- No automated GUI test (headless renderer tests live in the Rust crates).

## Verified by

`mvn test -pl pathland-desktop-demo` — `RingEventReaderTest` (headless, no GTK/Qt;
pointer/value/date/text/navigate/media/fit decoding and bounds behaviour).
Manual: `scripts/run-java-gtk-demo.sh` and `scripts/run-java-qt-demo.sh`.

package dev.pathland.demo.quarkus.kotlin

import io.quarkus.test.common.http.TestHTTPResource
import io.quarkus.test.junit.QuarkusTest
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertEquals
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertFalse
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertNotNull
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertTrue
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test
import java.net.URI
import java.net.URL
import java.net.http.HttpClient
import java.net.http.HttpRequest
import java.net.http.HttpResponse

/** The Kotlin app boots, its CDI bean is discovered, and SSR renders the Kotlin tree. */
@QuarkusTest
class KotlinDemoSmokeTest {

    @TestHTTPResource("/")
    lateinit var base: URL

    @Test
    fun ssrRendersTheKotlinDemo() {
        val response = get("/")

        assertEquals(200, response.statusCode())
        assertTrue(response.body().contains("Library"), response.body())
        assertTrue(response.body().contains("Building on Solid Ground"), response.body())
        assertTrue(response.body().contains("8 songs · 8 albums"), response.body())
        assertTrue(response.body().contains("Pathland · Building on Solid Ground"), response.body())
    }

    @Test
    fun adViewIsMountedAndEmbeddedThroughTheProxy() {
        // Warm the mounted origin first: the first cold Kotlin view render can be slow on
        // CI, and the proxy's SSR snapshot budget starts only after the parent mounts.
        val ad = get("/ad")
        assertEquals(200, ad.statusCode(), "the ad app is mounted at /ad")
        assertTrue(ad.body().contains("Pathland Ads"), "the ad app renders directly at /ad")

        val html = get("/").body()
        assertTrue(html.contains("Pathland Ads"), "the proxied ad app's title is embedded: $html")
        assertTrue(html.contains("Clicked 0 times"), "the ad app's counter renders through the proxy")
        assertTrue(html.contains("data-pathland-id=\"1073741825\""),
            "the ad subtree carries remapped ids from the proxy range")
    }

    @Test
    fun ssrServesTheContentHashedDomBundle() {
        val html = get("/").body()
        assertFalse(html.contains("/_pathland/dom-renderer.js\""),
                "the pre-hash fallback must not be emitted when the app manifest is visible")

        val src = Regex("""src="(/_pathland/dom-renderer-[^"]+\.js)"""")
            .find(html)?.groupValues?.get(1)
        assertNotNull(src, "the SSR document references the content-hashed DOM bundle: $html")

        val bundle = get(src!!)
        assertEquals(200, bundle.statusCode(), "GET $src")
        assertTrue(bundle.headers().firstValue("Content-Type").orElse("")
                .startsWith("text/javascript"), "served as JavaScript")
    }

    private fun get(path: String): HttpResponse<String> =
        HttpClient.newHttpClient().send(
            HttpRequest.newBuilder(URI.create(base.toString()).resolve(path)).GET().build(),
            HttpResponse.BodyHandlers.ofString(),
        )
}

# pathland-quarkus-kotlin-demo — implementation status

**Last updated:** November 1, 2026

Kotlin-first Quarkus demo: SSR plus live 16-byte opcode deltas over WebSocket,
authored with `pathland-view-kotlin` and hosted by `pathland-quarkus-kotlin`.

## Implemented

- Kotlin `PathlandApp` CDI bean (`KotlinDemoApplication`) mounting the Kotlin
  `MusicPlayerView` at `/`.
- **Sponsored proxy** — a second `MountedApp` at `/ad` (`AdView`), embedded into
  the player's Now Playing pane via `ProxyView` (same-server loopback proxy).
- The standalone `KotlinDemoView` remains available as a small state/input
  showcase.
- Exercises persisted state (`count`, `items`), two-way text input (`name`),
  reactive computed text, `ForEach`, and Kotlin modifier sugar.
- Quarkus Kotlin build setup: `kotlin-maven-plugin`, `all-open` for CDI/JAX-RS
  annotations, `jvmTarget=17`.
- The removed Java DSL (`pathland-view`) and Java demo views are not on the
  classpath: the demo is
  Kotlin-DSL-only.
- `KotlinDemoSmokeTest` (`@QuarkusTest`) asserts the CDI bean is discovered, SSR
  renders the Kotlin tree, the `/ad` app is mounted and embedded through the proxy
  (with remapped proxy ids), and the SSR document references the content-hashed
  DOM bundle (a GET on that URL returns 200).
- The DOM renderer bundle + service worker are copied by
  `lib/typescript/scripts/copy-to-demos.mjs`.
- Run with `scripts/run-quarkus-kotlin-demo.sh` → `http://localhost:8080`.

## Not implemented / gaps

- No WebSocket delta integration test yet; SSR discovery is covered.
- No Quarkus codestart yet.
- Native image is not supported (Rust HTML renderer via JNA).

- **Observability seam** — `PathlandTelemetry` (default `NOOP`): the runtime emits
  session open/close, inbound event batches, flushed batches (frames/opcodes/bytes +
  merge-encode time), SSR render latency, resync requests, and send failures; the host
  binds a pull-based active-sessions gauge. `PathlandHost`/`PathlandRegistry`/
  `PathlandSession`/`DeltaBatcher` thread it through (a host with no telemetry pays
  nothing). `pathland-observability` provides the Micrometer + OpenTelemetry adapters;
  the starters auto-wire them. Logging is **SLF4J** (both frameworks bind it) — the old
  ad-hoc `System.out` is gone. See issue #62.
- **Concurrency stress** — `RegistryConcurrencyTest`: 100 sessions driven through the
  registry concurrently (clicks on each session's button) while SSR-style requests
  construct throwaway sessions on request threads — the shared-actor / global-`Scheduler`
  cross-session corruption guard. Each session must reach exactly its own click count
  (no lost effects, no cross-session values).
- **Shared WS test harness** — `dev.pathland.server.test.{WsSession,MultiSessionProbe}`
  (a JDK-WebSocket client speaking the PLPL protocol: env/resync/click/ping) lives in the
  **`pathland-test-kit`** module (main scope, so package builds resolve it as a normal
  jar); the starters' 100-session stress tests reuse it.
- **`StateStores`** — default state store: Redis when reachable, else the supplied
  fallback.
- **SSR debug comments (property-gated)**: `PathlandSession`/`PathlandRegistry` take a
  `debugHtml` flag (constructor + `isDebugHtml()`); when set, `renderHtml` uses the
  renderer's debug mode so every rendered node is prefixed with an HTML comment naming
  its component and the modifiers applied. The Spring/Quarkus starters bind it to the
  `pathland.debug-html` property (default `false`).
- **Reserved framework root**: `PathlandSession.PATHLAND_BASE` (`/_pathland`) — the
  SSR page carries the app's base as `data-pathland-base` and the DOM-client bundle is
  injected at `{base}/dom-renderer-<sha256>.js` (`PathlandAssets` reads the current
  name from the `_pathland/dom-renderer.current` manifest on the classpath, resolving
  through the thread context classloader first so a Quarkus extension parent loader
  can see the application's static resources; it falls back to the literal
  `dom-renderer.js` only when absent) so the client's WebSocket and
  asset refs resolve from the same reserved prefix (spec DSL.md). The content-hashed
  name busts the immutable asset cache with a fresh URL per build. The built-in
  base design is linked the same way: `renderHtml` renders through
  `HtmlRenderer.renderLinked(frame, root, base)`, so the CSS href is
  `{base}/base-<sha256>.css` (token overrides/fit rules stay inline).
  Multi-app hosts give each mount its own base.
- **Per-window-id service worker (opt-in, issue #155)**: `PathlandHost` carries a
  host-level `serviceWorker` flag (default `false`; one registration covers the
  whole origin) threaded to every `PathlandRegistry`; `PathlandSession.renderHtml`
  emits `data-pathland-service-worker="true"` on `<html>` when set, and the DOM
  client registers `{base}/sw.js` (root scope) / unregisters when absent (the kill
  switch). `PathlandRegistry.serviceWorkerUrl()` names the served script.
  `renderHtml` also emits `data-pathland-ssr-scoped="true"` when the request carried
  a real per-window id, so the client can skip its initial `META::RESYNC` (the SSR
  was already rendered with that window's state and the live session shares it).

## Not implemented / gaps

- No multi-node/shared sessions (each server owns its sessions in-memory).
- Quarkus mounted-app WebSocket endpoints require a **single-segment** mount path
  (the `/{app}` path param); Spring supports any depth.

## Proxy views (spec/PROXY.md) — M1 (live)

- **`proxy.ProxyIdMap`** — node-id namespacing: the reserved high range
  `[0x4000_0000, 0x8000_0000)`, 1024 blocks of `2^20`, the block math, and the
  opcode remap in both directions (`TREE` node ids + the node-id-bearing
  `PARAMETER` ops `SET_TEXT`/`SET_PROPERTY`/`SET_DATE` on ingress; `EVENT` targets
  on egress; `META` untouched). `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` is **not** remapped — its `A`
  is a token-path arena offset, not a node id (remapping it produced a huge
  out-of-bounds string offset → the client's RESYNC loop; regression-tested).
  Pure + unit-tested.

  attaches the origin root under the proxy node, forwards live deltas remapped,
  routes client events back (target unmapped), replies `PONG` to origin `PING`,
